I worship the two brothers Śrī Caitanya and Śrī Nityānanda. They are the most magnanimous Supreme Lords, transcendentally situated and embodying inconceivable spiritual potency. These two Supreme Controllers have now appeared upon this earth in Their eternal forms.

O Lord! You are the eternal truth—unconditioned by past, present, and future—and yet You have now appeared as the son of Śrī Jagannātha Miśra. I offer repeated obeisances unto You along with Your intimate servitors, Your unalloyed devotees, Your sons (Your renounced Gosvāmī disciples, and the devotional process of chanting the Holy Names of Lord Kṛṣṇa), and Your consorts (Śrī Bhū Devī, who appeared as Śrī Viṣṇupriyā; Śrī Devī, who appeared as Śrī Lakṣmīpriyā; and Śrī Līlā Devī, also known as Nīlā or Durgā, who manifested Navadvīpa-dhāma), and the two Gadādharas (one is Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, the expansion of Śrīmatī Rādhārāni; and the other is Śrī Gadādhara Bhaṭṭa from South India, who is Śrī Ranga-devī), and Dāmodara, Narahari, Rāmānanda, Jagadānanda, and all of your unlimited associates.

All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the beloved Lord of Lakṣmī Devī, the Goddess of Fortune! Śrī Nityānanda is most dear to Him.

All glory to the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha and the best amongst all the *sannyāsīs*!

All glory to His illustrious devotees! Śrī Gauracandra, You are the friend of the fallen souls, please place Your lotus feet upon the throne of my heart.

Please hear attentively the topics described in the *Antya-khaṇḍa*, which deal with the Lord’s activities after taking *sannyāsa* and His travel to Jagannātha Purī.

The night of His *sannyāsa* initiation, Lord Caitanya remained in Katwa. Immediately after the completion of the *sannyāsa* ceremonies, the Lord instructed Mukunda to sing. He stood up and began to dance vigorously. The devotees encircled Him and joined in the chorus. The Lord was immediately overcome with ecstasy. As the Lord danced, He experienced heavy breathing, laughter, perspiration, shivering, horripilation and roaring. Then, with a voice like thunder and the roaring of a thousand lions, He crashed to the ground. The impact of His fall sent shock waves amongst the spectators. The *kamaṇḍalu* flew out of His hand to one side and the *sannyāsa daṇḍa* went in another direction. The Lord became enraptured and maddened with love of Himself. Then, dancing and swirling, He went to His *guru* and embraced Him with glowing pleasure.

In the Lord’s merciful embrace, Keśava Bhāratī was enlightened with love of Hari. He began to dance, singing and pirouetting ecstatically. Similarly, His *kamaṇḍalu* and *daṇḍa* also flew from his grip. He became oblivious to the external world. Intoxicated with *kṛṣṇa-prema*, he rolled on the ground, unaware that his clothes no longer properly covered his body. The Lord was pleased to see Keśava Bhāratī in such ecstasy. They danced together, putting the devotees into fits of ecstasy. The devotees appreciated this rare sight with vociferous chanting of the Holy Name.

I offer my obeisances at the feet of Śrī Keśava Bhāratī, the most stalwart *sannyāsī*, for he danced with the Supreme Lord, whose association is difficult to achieve even for the Personified *Vedas*. He is the *guru* of the Lord of the entire unlimited creation. The night flitted by as the *guru* and his disciple danced together.

At dawn, the Lord begged leave of His *guru*, saying, “I will enter the forest, and there I will find the Lord of My heart, Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra.” His *guru* replied, “I will accompany You and relish with You the ecstasy of *saṅkīrtana*.” The Lord benedicted His *guru* and allowed him to accompany Him, requesting him to walk in front, while He followed behind.

As the Lord was preparing to leave, He embraced Candraśekhara Ācārya and began to cry loudly. Lord Caitanya said, “Please return home to all the Vaiṣṇavas and tell them that I have left for the forest. Please go back without the slightest remorse, I am always imprisoned in your heart. You are My father and I, your son. You are My eternal associate.” The Lord then left. Candraśekhara Ācārya was overpowered by strong emotions and fell unconscious. No one can understand the Lord’s inconceivable potency, and therefore even the unbearable pain of separation can keep a person alive.

After some time, when he regained consciousness, Candraśekhara Ācārya left for Navadvīpa. He informed everyone in Navadvīpa that the Lord had entered the forest wearing His *sannyāsa* robe. This news deeply pained all the devotees and they cried out in the excruciation of separation. The devastating effect of the news was widespread and intense.

Advaita Ācārya, numbed with grief, cried, “I cannot live!” and fell unconscious. The heart-rending cries of the devotees could have melted the cruellest heart. Śacīdevī stood motionless like a wooden doll in stony silence, shocked by the news. The other ladies fell to the ground wailing piteously. Advaita Ācārya, regaining consciousness exclaimed, “What further use do I have for this life now that my Lord has gone away. I will throw myself into the Gaṅgā and if you restrain me, I shall do it in the darkness of night.”

The throbbing pain of separation rendered everyone restless and gloomy. They felt sick, uneasy, and ready to finish their lives. Although the devotees are grave and learned persons now they were greatly anxious, their minds in turmoil.

As the devotees were preparing to end their lives and their unbearable misery, suddenly a heavenly voice caught their attention: “O Advaita Ācārya and all devotees, do not be sad, go worship Kṛṣṇa happily. Your Lord and master will return in a few days and be amongst you again. Give up your resolve to take your own lives, because you shall be with the Lord just as before.” Hearing this heavenly message, the devotees forgot about giving up their lives and sat around Śacīdevī singing the Lord’s glories.

Gauracandra, the best of the *sannyāsīs* now travelled with Nityānanda, Gadādhara and Mukunda in a westerly direction, all the time chanting the Holy Name. In front of the Lord went Keśava Bhāratī and behind Him was Govinda. Walking like the king of the forest, the Lord was followed by thousands of wailing people. They were all around stamping through the difficult forest, but still they followed undeterred.

Filled with compassion, the Lord turned to them and said, “All of you go home and chant Kṛṣṇa’s Holy Name. May you soon be blessed to have Kṛṣṇa as the priceless gift of your life. May that devotional mellow, which is desired by Śiva, Brahmā, Śukadeva Gosvāmī and other great personalities, appear in your hearts.” The devotees loudly voiced their appreciation and joy and returned home as if in trance.

The Lord walked into the district of Rāḍhadeśa and blessed the entire tract of land. This district is pleasant, with *aśvatthāmā* trees everywhere. Cows were grazing peacefully in the beautiful natural setting, and the Lord upon seeing this scene began to dance blissfully. Devotees quickly gathered around Him singing and clapping. The Lord chanted, “Hari! Hari!” in a roaring voice that boomed across the universe, and whoever heard Him was purified of his material contamination. In this way, He graced the residents of the Rāḍhadeśa district, dancing all the way.

The Lord said, “I want to stay in the forest in the vicinity of the Vakreśvara Deity. It is quiet and lonely there.” The Lord then continued on His way accompanied by His followers, dancing and singing ecstatically. The local residents ran out to see the Lord and His wonderful dancing. Although *saṅkīrtana* had never been performed in that area before and no one had even seen the effects of *kṛṣṇa-prema* manifest in a devotee, now they were offering obeisances to the Lord as He danced and wept in ecstasy. This was a rare experience for them.

Amongst them were a few fallen sinners, who asked, “Why is He crying so much?” Nevertheless, even those fallen souls were affected by the scene and by the Lord’s mercy they also began to roll on the ground crying. The entire universe was now echoing the Lord’s name, yet there remained a few who refused to chant. Anyone who is against the chanting of the Lord’s name is indeed the worst kind of sinner. Finally, at the day’s end, the Lord with all His followers came to a village and spent the night in the house of a pious *brāhmaṇa*.

There the Lord took His meal and went to sleep. The devotees slept all around the Lord; however, just a few hours before dawn, Śrī Caitanya quietly stole away from the rest of the devotees and left for an unknown destination. When the devotees awoke early next morning, they found the Lord missing. Again, they were swept with waves of despair and melancholia and began to weep bitterly. They searched for Him everywhere inquiring from everyone in the village, but to no avail. They left the roads and paths and went into the fields.

The Lord was absorbed in the transcendental ecstasy of love of Kṛṣṇa. He walked in the middle of the expansive meadows, wept, and wailed loudly. He loudly called out, “O Kṛṣṇa! My Lord! My father!” The Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, the Supreme Lord of all living entities, and the best of the *sannyāsīs*, wept openly. He cried so loudly that He could be heard several miles away. The devotees, searching for the Lord quite a distance from where He was, heard this out of the ordinary crying. They began to follow the sound and soon saw the Lord crying loudly. Seeing their beloved Lord weeping, the devotees also began to cry. Finally, Mukunda started to sing. When the Lord heard the *kīrtana*, He began to dance, and all the devotees surrounded their Lord and happily joined the *kīrtana*. The Lord then continued His journey westward, dancing along the way, with the devotees following, singing *kīrtana*.

When they were only eight miles from Vakreśvara, the Lord decided to change direction. He turned around and went East, still absorbed in the ecstasy of dancing. He was blissful and laughing to Himself. Finally, He revealed the mystery behind His laughter and change of direction. He said, “I am going to Nīlācala, Purī, because Lord Jagannātha has instructed Me: ‘You should come to Purī immediately!’ ” The devotees were relieved to learn of the Lord’s plan.

No one can know the workings of the Lord’s mind save His intimate devotees, and then only by His mercy may they know His innermost desires. Who can fathom why the Lord was first going to Vakreśvara and then why finally He did not go? It seems that the Lord in a deceptive way was purifying the residents of Rāḍhadeśa by His presence. There was no other reason for Him to go to Rāḍhadeśa.

The Lord now journeyed towards the Gaṅgā, which lay at a distance. He was always engrossed in the ecstasy of love of Kṛṣṇa, yet He saw that the residents of the tract of land through which He was passing were disinterested in devotional life. No one chanted the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa; *kṛṣṇa-kīrtana* was alien to them. Pained, the Lord said, “Why did I come to such a country where they never chant Kṛṣṇa’s Holy Name? It was a grievous mistake for which I must relinquish my life.”

Just then a group of little cowherd lads, who were grazing their cows, passed by. One of them was a very pious boy, and he suddenly began chanting Kṛṣṇa’s name. The Lord was extremely happy to hear the Holy Name from the mouth of this little boy. Joyfully, He relished the moment and said, “For the last few days, I have passed through many villages and nowhere was Kṛṣṇa’s name being chanted. Suddenly now, unexpectedly, a young lad is chanting the Holy Name. Tell me what could be the reason?”

The Lord spoke again, “How far is the Gaṅgā from here?” The devotees replied, “About an hour’s walk.” The Lord continued, “This is the greatness of Mother Gaṅgā. Due to her influence, one hears the chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s name here. The breezes from the Gaṅgā have purified this place.” Glorifying Gaṅgā devī in this manner, the Lord increased everyone’s reverence towards her. The Lord spoke again, “I will cleanse Myself completely in the Gaṅgā today.” Then, He restarted His journey.

The Lord walked with the pace and grace of a maddened lion and the devotees ran to catch up with Him. The Lord’s eagerness to see Gaṅgādevī quickened His steps and the devotees found it impossible to keep up with Him. Only Lord Nityānanda, also walking like a lion, accompanied Him. They reached the banks of Gaṅgādevī early in the evening. Śrī Caitanya and Nityānanda entered her waters with relish and thoroughly washed Themselves, profusely praising the Gaṅgā with selected verses. They drank her cooling waters and offered obeisances to her.

The Lord prayed, “O Gaṅgādevī, your waters are the ambrosia of love of Kṛṣṇa. Lord Śiva is conversant with the truth about you. Such is your potency that the mere utterance of your name invokes devotional service to the Supreme Lord, and the result of drinking your water is miraculous. By your mercy, the living entities acquire a taste for chanting Kṛṣṇa’s Holy Name. Because of your influence, even the wild beasts and birds that live close to your waters become more fortunate than wealthy men who live far away from you. No one is more potent than you in purifying sins. In fact, you have descended to this material plane only to alleviate the sins of the living entities.”

As the Lord glorified Gaṅgādevī in this manner, she became abashed, for she was being glorified by the Supreme Lord whose feet are her very source. How wonderful is the incarnation of the Supreme Godhead in the form of Śrī Caitanya. One who hears these verses in praise of Gaṅgādevī with faith will certainly develop attachment for Śrī Caitanya.

That night, the Lord and Nityānanda Prabhu stayed in a righteous *brāhmaṇa’s* house. The next day, the rest of the devotees arrived and found Śrī Caitanya. Together they again proceeded towards Nīlācala, Purī. Śrī Caitanya said to Nityānanda Prabhu, “My dear magnanimous Prabhu Nityānanda, You must immediately leave for Navadvīpa. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and the other devotees are grievously afflicted due to My departure. You must alleviate their pain. Take this message from Me to them that on My way to Nīlācala I will be waiting for them in Śāntipur in the house of Advaita Ācārya. You bring them there right away. I am going to Phuliyā to see Haridāsa.” Sending off Nityānanda, Śrī Caitanya headed for the village of Phuliyā.

Having received His orders from Lord Caitanya, Nityānanda Prabhu journeyed toward Phuliyā in exultation. Nityānanda is always absorbed in the bliss of love of Kṛṣṇa, His voice booming like thunder in ecstasy. Now He travelled almost like a maddened elephant, oblivious of everything around Him, no rules or taboos restricting His actions.

He stopped under a *kadamba* tree for a while standing like Kṛṣṇa. His body bending in three places, He began to play the flute rapturously. When He saw some cows grazing nearby, He rolled on the earth, and then moving like a calf, He sucked milk from cows. Sometimes, He would break out into a dance while walking, unaware of His surroundings, always submerged in bliss.

At other times, He just sat down on the road and wept so bitterly that it would pain one to see Him in that condition. Then He might suddenly stop weeping and start shaking with peals of laughter. Then again, He would take of the clothing covering His body and wrap it around His head leaving Him naked.

At other times, He would feel in the mood of Ananta Śeṣa. Making serpent-like movements He would enter the waters of the Gaṅgā, float, and swim gracefully in the currents. Lord Nityānanda’s potencies are inconceivable, transcendental and mysterious. His limitless compassion is unmatched in all the three worlds.

Śrī Nityānanda swam in the Gaṅgā all the way to Navadvīpa, where He got out onto the banks, and withdrawing His inner mood within Himself, went straight to the Lord’s house. What He saw pained Him greatly. Śacīdevī had been totally fasting for twelve days. Life remained in her only on the strength of her devotional service. She was completely imbued with Mother Yaśodā’s mood of pining for her son, and tears rained down from her eyes. Whoever she met she would eagerly ask, “Are you from Mathurā? What is the news of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma?” and swoon in ecstatic spiritual bliss. Then, gradually, she would again start speaking, “There! I can hear Their flutes and horns. Is Akrūra coming to get Them?” In this manner, submerged in the mood of intense separation, she had completely forgotten her physical needs.

Nityānanda fell at Śacīdevī’s feet, offering His obeisances. The devotees greeted Him enthusiastically, but His presence merely intensified their pining, and they began to weep. Mother Śacīmātā cried out, “My son! My darling boy!” and swooned. The devotees felt a surge of new emotions ripping through their hearts. They embraced Nityānanda, and were bathed with His tears of ecstasy. He calmed them down and told them the good news.

He said, “You must come immediately, the Lord is awaiting us in Advaita Ācārya’s house in Śāntipur. I have come here to take you there.” The devotees, who had become lean and weak due to intensely missing their Lord, now received new life. They were jubilant and loudly chanted Kṛṣṇa’s name.

Śacīdevī had not touched food or water from the day Nimāi left her house to take *sannyāsa* twelve days earlier. Only thoughts of Nimāi could sustain her life. For Nityānanda, her condition was unbearable. He spoke soft reassuring words to her, “Nothing is unknown to you about the mysterious activities of Kṛṣṇa. What knowledge can I give you about Kṛṣṇa? Do not burden your heart with despair. Even the *Vedas* Personified cannot receive the grace and good fortune already in your possession, for that supreme object sought by the *Vedas* is your son. He is the life and soul of every living entity and that same Supreme Personality has accepted all spiritual and material responsibilities concerning you. He made this promise with His hand upon His chest. The Lord always knows what is best for everyone. You should simply surrender everything at His feet and live happily and peacefully. Now, mother, please cook for the satisfaction of all the devotees, for this is devotional service to Kṛṣṇa. Everyone is eager to taste your cooking. If you remain fasting, then Kṛṣṇa has to fast also. I am extremely desirous of relishing the offerings prepared for Kṛṣṇa by you.”

Nityānanda’s sweet words were like soothing balm to her afflicted heart. She got up and went to make the necessary arrangements for the cooking. First, she fed Nityānanda Prabhu and then she fed all the Vaiṣṇavas. She carefully saw to it that everyone was fully satisfied and then sat down to eat herself. The devotees were relieved that Śacīdevī had broken her twelve day fast.

Enlivened by the *prasāda*, the Vaiṣṇavas prepared to go and meet their beloved Lord with Nityānanda Prabhu. The residents of Navadvīpa were by now familiar with the details of Nimāi’s *sannyāsa* ceremony. The Lord’s wonderful *sannyāsa* name, Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, had a miraculous effect on them. They chanted aloud the Lord’s name, and glorified Him.

When the people of Navadvīpa came to know that the Lord was presently in Phuliyā village, they became elated and decided to go and see Him there. Old, young, men, women and children all hastened to Phuliyā chanting jubilantly, “Hari! Hari!” Those atheists and faultfinders who had previously been vituperative against the Lord were now eager to reach Phuliyā with their friends. They said, “He was born in Navadvīpa, but His real identity remained a secret. Out of ignorance, we maligned His work and spiritual mission. Now we must fall at His feet and beg forgiveness. Only then will all our offences be exonerated.”

Thousands of people flocked to the pier. The boatmen were in a dilemma, for everyone wanted to be first and they could not risk crossing the river overloaded with people. Therefore, many found their own means to cross the river. Some went in small dinghies. Others tied themselves to upturned earthen water vessels, which made them float easily. Someone used a raft made out of banana tree trunks, which was also very handy. Even pregnant women dared the crowd and jostling. Breathing heavily from exertion, they simply chanted Śrī Caitanya’s name and somehow made the journey. For the blind and lame, the way became suddenly broad and facile just by remembering Caitanya’s name. A boat carrying hundreds found it impossible to make the other bank and capsized in midstream. This of course did not deter the people. They jubilantly chanted the Lord’s name and floated upstream. The people’s hearts were so infected with joy that it seemed they actually floated in an ocean of divine mirth.

Those who did not know how to swim seemed to have miraculously become buoyant. By the grace of the Lord, they also were able to cross the river without difficulty. The sky reverberated with ecstatic sounds of the Holy Name. The people had only one thought in their mind—to reach Phuliyā. Disregarding all comfort and bodily needs, they joined in the mass chanting with carefree happy abandon. Their loud cries of, “Hari! Hari! Hari! Hari!” echoed in the vaults of the cosmic creation as they approached Phuliyā.

This wonderful sound of many people chanting reached the Lord and He came out to greet them. The people saw Him and held their breath. His exquisite appearance as a *sannyāsī* and His extraordinarily beautiful face, which eclipsed the beauty of millions of moons, were a memorable vision for all. The Lord was continuously chanting the Holy Name as tears of ecstasy cascaded down His cheeks.

Everyone was now falling to the ground to offer their obeisances. People fell on top of each other in their fervour to show respect to their Lord. They did not care if there were thorns on the ground. They were all boundlessly happy. They lifted their hands and prayed to the Lord for His protection and shelter, crying out, “Save us! Save us!” The village of Phuliyā was now teeming with millions of people who were captivated by the infinitely charming face of the Lord. The fields and roads were overflowing with people, who had forgotten about returning to their houses, for they had, even for a just moment, beheld the lustrous benign face of the Lord.

The Lord blessed them all with His merciful glance and proceeded towards Śāntipur. When He arrived at Advaita Ācārya’s house, Advaita Prabhu fell at His beloved Lord’s lotus feet. He began to weep, relieved of the miserable pain of separation. He remained prostrate, His arms curled around the Lord’s lotus feet. He bathed them with His tears of love. At last, Śrī Caitanya bent down and lifted Advaita Ācārya into His warm embrace. Advaita, now soaked by the ecstatic tears of the Lord, again fell to His lotus feet in spiritual perturbation. Calming Himself and Advaita, the Lord sat down as Advaita’s house vibrated with loud exultation.

Acyutānanda was Advaita’s son. He was a charming and effulgent little child endowed with extraordinary intelligence and supreme influence. Naked as is usual for that age and covered in dust, Acyutānanda came running to greet the Lord. His great fortune was that he was Advaita’s son. He was blissful and smiling for he knew the identity of Lord Caitanya. He fell at the Lord’s feet full of respect. The Lord lovingly took him into His arms in spite of the dust smeared on his small frame.

The Lord said, “Acyuta, you know that Advaita Ācārya is also my father, hence this makes us brothers. Little Acyuta replied, “You are the well-wishing friend of all living entities. The *Vedas* describe that You are the original father of everyone.” This greatly pleased and amused the Lord, and He smiled knowingly. The Vaiṣṇavas were amazed at Acyuta’s words. They said, “These words are not the babblings of a mere child, but actually carry deep import. Acyuta must be a great personality.”

At this moment, Nityānanda Prabhu arrived with all the devotees and intimate servitors of the Lord from Navadvīpa. When the devotees saw their dear Lord, Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and the others began loudly chanting and fell flat on the ground offering prayers and tears at the Lord’s lotus feet. These devotees were as precious to the Lord as His very life and He lovingly embraced each one of them. The devotees cried out in the pain of ecstasy and separation. Their cries purified the entire earth. To hear pure devotees weeping in love of Kṛṣṇa can cut asunder the bondage of birth and death of all living entities. This wonderful opportunity was now made available to everyone by the mercy of Lord Caitanya. Even Lord Brahmā rarely receives such favours.

Upon seeing again His beloved associates from Navadvīpa after what seemed a long absence, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya began to dance rapturously, saturated in ecstatic love of Himself, for He alone is the Supreme Lord. The devotees began to sing and the Lord encouraged them with loud exclamations of “Sing! Sing!” The Lord caught Nityānanda Prabhu by the hand and spun around in ecstatic joy.

Stealthily, Advaita Ācārya came up from behind and touched the Lord’s feet, placing the dust upon His head. The Lord’s dancing postures were enchanting. Simultaneously, He manifested all the different symptoms of devotional perturbation by weeping, shivering, horripilation, mirth and so on. The movements and nuances of the limbs and different parts of His transcendental body were an expressive composition of some divine love poetry. His arms raised in exultation, and chanting “Hari! Hari!” He enchanted the devotees and submerged them in an ocean of ineffable bliss.

The devotees had only just recently been deprived of their Lord’s presence and now, by His mercy, to be again in His company was certainly a cause for extreme exhilaration and celebration. They surrounded their Lord, danced, and pranced, oblivious of everything else. They fell on each other, bumped against each other, and rolled on the ground, smearing their bodies with the dust of everyone’s feet. One pressed another devotee’s feet against his chest and remained saturated in bliss, tears of joy flowing unrestrainedly from his eyes. The devotees could not contain their happiness having regained their beloved Lord and Master. The Lord of Vaikuṇṭha dancing free from all care with His associates is indeed an extraordinary sight.

Above the sounds of the dancing, the singing of the Lord’s name rang out, loud and clear. Advaita Ācārya’s house resounded with sounds of mirth, of which only Nityānanda Prabhu was fully aware. Śrī Caitanya went around embracing His loving associates and infusing them with *kṛṣṇa-prema*. Receiving the Lord’s divine touch, the devotees became mad with joy. In a loud voice that resembled the rumbling of thunder, they expressed their boundless bliss. This further increased the pleasure of the others present.

As the Lord danced with His associates, Mother Earth seemed to sway and tilt. Nityānanda, Advaita and all the devotees were caught in a maelstrom of infinite ecstasy, and they freely allowed their limbs and body to express their continual happiness. After a while, the Lord stopped dancing and entering a mood of divine Lordship, He sat down upon the throne of Śrī Viṣṇu.

The devotees stood around Him in great awe and reverence with folded palms as the Lord began to reveal His real identity as the Supreme Lord. He said, “I am Kṛṣṇa, Rāma, Nārāyaṇa, and Matsya. I have assumed these incarnations and more. I am Kūrma, Varāha, Vāmana, Buddha, and I will be Kalki. I am Pṛśnigarbha and Hayagriva, the Supreme Lord of Lords. I am the moon of Nīlācala, Lord Jagannātha, and I am Kapila and Nṛsiṁha. All living entities visible and invisible are My servitors. The *Vedas* sing of My supra-mundane excellences, and I am served by the endless planetary systems. I am Time, the destroyer of everything, except My devotees. All dangers are easily eradicated simply by remembering Me. In this way, I rescued Draupadī from great public shame and insult. I also saved the Pāṇḍavas from the firetrap in the house of lakh. I protected Śiva by slaying the terrible demon Vṛkāsura. I liberated My servant, Gajendra, the elephant, from excruciating death pains. I stood by Prahlāda in all his tortures. I protected the cowherd boys from all kinds of harm and attacks. I churned the Milk Ocean to extract the nectar of immortality. I deprived the demons of that nectar and gave it to the demigods, thus aiding them to victory. I slew the obnoxious demon Kaṁsa, who was threatening My devotees. I finished the demon, King Rāvaṇa, destroying his entire race. I lifted Govardhana Hill with My left hand, and I tamed the vicious snake-demon, Kāliya.

“I appeared in Satya-yuga to propagate the practice of austerity and meditation, and in Tretā-yuga to introduce the performance of sacrifices. In Dvāpara-yuga, My purpose was to establish the proper procedures of temple worship. Presently in Kali-yuga, I have come to promulgate the congregational chanting of the Holy Names of Kṛṣṇa. Even the *Vedas* fail to enumerate all My incarnations. In Kali-yuga, by participating in this *saṅkīrtana* movement, every sincere soul will taste the nectar of *kṛṣṇa-prema*. This is the reason for My appearance in this *yuga*. The entire Vedic literature instructs the searching soul to seek My shelter, but I am only to be found in the company of My surrendered devotees. They are everything to Me—father, mother, friend, son, and brother. Although I am absolutely independent, My nature is to be captivated by My devotees’ pure love for Me. All of you are My eternal associates. All My incarnations are only for your pleasure and protection. Know for certain that I cannot remain even for a moment bereft of your association.”

Out of His causeless mercy for His devotees and all the living entities, the Lord revealed this confidential knowledge about Himself. The devotees were jubilant. They fell flat on the ground, offering obeisances. They were so devotionally perturbed that they were unable to do anything. They prayed and rolled on the ground, relishing the highest ambrosia of *kṛṣṇa-prema*. The Lord’s associates were now saturated in divine nectar; their previous heartache due to separation from the Lord was now cured. The compassionate Lord is expert in alleviating everyone’s grief, so why should suffering humanity not take shelter of the Lord. Śrī Gauracandra is an ocean of mercy. He always discounts the wayward soul’s faults and sees only his goodness.

Thereafter, withdrawing His mood of supreme opulence and absolute autocracy, the Lord returned to His normal self, calm and composed and He led everyone down to the Gaṅgā to bathe. He played and frolicked in the waters with the devotees. Upon returning, He watered the *tulasī* plant and circumambulated her, indicating that the accompanying devotees should follow His activities. Then they all went to the temple room, offered obeisances to Śrī Viṣṇu, and circumambulated the Lord. Śrī Gaurahari called everyone and they sat down together to eat. The Lord sat down beside Nityānanda amidst the happy and cheerful devotees. The Lord was the cynosure of everyone, with His smiling face and golden body covered with sandalwood paste. The scene of the devotees, sitting around Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya with Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu sitting beside Him, was an exact replica of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma sitting in the forest of Vṛndāvana surrounded by Their cowherd boyfriends, all having a picnic with Their packed lunches. Who can fully describe this wonderful happening?

As soon as the Lord had finished and left, the devotees jumped up and grabbed the remnants from His plate. Even the old men acted like little boys, such is the transformation that takes place due to contact with the Lord’s divine potency.

One who hears these pastimes of the Lord and His associates, their reunion, *saṅkīrtana* and eating together, will certainly attain Śrī Caitanya’s mercy and relish *kṛṣṇa-prema*.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Nityānanda Prabhu are my life and soul. I, Vṛndāvana dāsa, humbly offer this song at Their lotus feet.

## 2: Śrī Caitanya Arrives in Jagannātha Purī

All victory to the moonlike Śrī Gaurāṅga, the life and soul of all living entities! He is Fear Personified to the evildoers and the protector of the righteous.

All glory to the Lord and master of Śrī Ananta Śeṣa, Śrī Ramā Devī, Lord Brahmā, and Lord Śiva! He is the ocean of compassion, the friend of the fallen and wretched, and the best amongst the renounced *sannyāsīs*.

All glory to the Lord along with His pure devotees! I simply pray that He may shower His mercy upon me so that I may eternally repose my mind at His Lotus-feet.

The Supreme Lord Śrī Gaurasundara exhibited wonderful pastimes in the house of Śrī Advaita Ācārya in Śrī Śāntipur, thus revealing the unlimited mystique and charisma of His own Transcendental Personality. He spent the night in *kṛṣṇa-kathā* with His Vaiṣṇava devotees, experiencing great bliss and joy.

In the morning, after completing His daily morning spiritual duties, He sat surrounded by His disciples, who had been unaware of the passing of the night. Śrī Caitanya said, “I am going to Śrī Nīlācala Purī, but do not feel sad thinking that I am leaving you. I will drink the nectar of Śrī Jagannātha’s moonlike beautiful face and return soon to be with you again. Return to your homes and engage in continuous *kīrtana*. Every one of you are my very being and you are my companions life after life.”

The devotees replied, “My dear Lord, who has the power to go against your wishes, still we wish to inform you that the times are bad, full of danger, and no one now dares to travel in that direction. There is growing enmity between the two kingdoms, Bengal and Utkala, and the borders are infested with bloodthirsty fighters. So we pray to you to rest here awhile until the tension subsides.”

To this the Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya, replied, “Let there be danger of any magnitude, I will certainly go, this I say to you.” Śrī Advaita Ācārya understood Śrī Caitanya’s mind and knew no one could dissuade Him from it. Palms joined, Śrī Advaita began to speak, “Who can dare to obstruct your path? All so-called impediments and dangers are simply your order carriers. No one possesses the power to stop you. You have resolved to travel to Nīlācala, and so your journey will be a source of great joy and You may leave at Your own sweet will.”

Śrī Caitanya was pleased to hear to hear the truth spoken so plainly by Śrī Advaita and, feeling great satisfaction, chanted the Holy Name, “Hari! Hari!” Wasting no time the Supreme Lord made an auspicious start to His journey, bidding His beloved ones farewell. As He walked toward Nīlācala, His gait was that of a stalking, maddened lion.

The devotees, feeling completely bereft, followed behind Him unable to halt their tears of separation. Some distance farther, Śrī Gaurasundara spoke softly to them with soothing words, “Do not allow this pain to laden your hearts. I could never live without you. I am always with you. Chant the Holy Name sitting in your homes while I am gone and very soon I will return.”

The Supreme Lord then embraced all the Vaiṣṇavas individually and bathed them with His cascading tears of love. After so comforting them with His divine sweetness, He headed south. The Vaiṣṇavas, touched by His love wept piteously in separation falling repeatedly to the ground with stunned hearts. The scene appeared the same as when Kṛṣṇa was being taken to Mathurā from Vṛndāvana and all the young cowherd damsels were drowning in a vast ocean of sorrow. The Vaiṣṇavas managed to contain their agony of separation from Śrī Caitanya in the same manner as the *gopīs*, who went on with their lives whilst tending their broken hearts.

Being composed of pure spiritual goodness, *viśuddha-sattva*, the transcendental emotions shown in the pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His associates are non-different in spiritual quality from the emotions displayed in the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya and His devotees. They are of the same spiritual status and purely transcendental.

One should always remember that the matter of life and death is entirely in the hands of the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, He decides if one should live even after consuming poison, and He decides if one should die even after drinking the nectar of immortality.

On this journey to Nīlācala, Śrī Gaurasundara was accompanied by Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Śrī Mukunda, Śrī Govinda, Śrī Jagadānanda Paṇḍita and Śrī Brahmānanda. The Supreme Lord, wishing to test His followers, enquired, “Has anyone amongst you brought anything along for this journey? Tell me frankly.” To this they replied, “My dear Lord, without your permission, which of us would dare to bring anything?” The Lord was greatly pleased at their reply.

The Lord now spoke, delineating the import of this seemingly simple question. He said, “You have made He very happy by not bringing anything with you. Everyone is liable to enjoy only what is destined to him. Even if he is in the forest, that which is due to him through destiny will find him. If Providence wills that someone goes without food, then even if he is a prince, he will have to fast. The prince’s larder may be filled with food, but if the Lord so wills it, he cannot eat. He may suddenly get into a quarrel with someone and out of anger refuse to eat and remain sulking. He may also, without warning, be attacked by high fever, in which case there is no question of eating anything. This is all happening in truth by the Lord’s sweet will. The entire universe is Kṛṣṇa’s storehouse filled with grains and foodstuff. If the Lord so desires, we can get food anywhere and everywhere.”

The Supreme Lord, as Śrī Gaurasundara, was personally instructing everyone on the Absolute Truth and the correct attitude towards Kṛṣṇa. Those who accept His words with faith, taking them into their hearts, experience immense joy. The efforts of the soul, the *jīva*, will never bear fruit unless the Supreme Lord sanctions them. One may try very carefully to do something, but the result of the endeavour depends entirely on the Lord’s will.

Teaching the devotees spiritual knowledge and discussing the entire way, Śrī Gaurasundara’s party arrived in the village of Āṭisārā. A very advanced scholar and pure devotee, Śrī Ananta Paṇḍita, lived in this village. The Lord decided to sojourn in his residence. I am unable to describe the extent of his good fortune.

Śrī Ananta Paṇḍita was an extremely magnanimous and saintly soul. The Lord’s presence in his home made him so jubilant that he become oblivious to his external surroundings. Joyful that the Lord and Master of Vaikuṇṭha had arrived in his own home as a guest, he happily busied himself to prepare fine foodstuffs for the Lord and His devotees. Śrī Gaurasundara and His followers sat down and honoured the cooked *prasādam*. In this way, the Lord was instructing everyone how to lead the ideal mendicant life of a *sannyāsī* by subsisting upon alms.

Throughout the night, the Lord made *kīrtana* and spoke *kṛṣṇa-kathā*, thus blessing Śrī Ananta Paṇḍita’s home. Next morning after blessing Ananta Paṇḍita with His merciful glance, the Lord proceeded upon His journey with Kṛṣṇa’s name constantly vibrating on His lips.

When the villagers saw the Lord’s compassionate moon-like face, which was a soothing balm for all tribulations, they spontaneously began to repeat the Lord’s Holy Name. The unbearable heat of material existence scorching their lives subsided as they continuously chanted the Holy Names of Kṛṣṇa. *Yogis* steeped in long arduous meditation find it practically impossible to attain *darśana* of the Lord’s lotus feet within their hearts, yet now even ordinary persons could freely see the unlimited beauty of the Lord as He went upon His journey.

The Lord followed the course of Jāhnavī-Gaṅgā, feeling great exhilaration as He walked along her sacred banks. He soon arrived in Chatrabhoga, where Gaṅgā devī divides herself into a hundred streams bestowing benediction and joy upon all. Also situated here is a famous bathing place known as Ambuliṅga- ghāṭa. Lord Śiva is present here in his submerged *liṅga* form known as, ‘Ambuliṅga in Water’. I will now narrate the history of how Lord Śiva received this appellation, kindly pay attention.

In the distant past, King Bhagiratha worshiped Gaṅgā devī, calling for her appearance in this world, as her waters were the only means to return life to his ancestors. When Gaṅgā devī complied and started flowing upon the earth, Lord Śiva, feeling Gaṅgā devī’s absence, started to pine for her association; eventually, Lord Śiva came down to earth and in the course of searching for Gaṅgā devī arrived at Chatrabhoga. Seeing her, Śiva became jubilant and unable to bear any further pangs of separation, he entered her waters.

Gaṅgā devī upon seeing Lord Śiva began to worship him with great devotion, offering him prayers with deep reverence. Lord Śiva knows the depth of Gaṅgā devī’s devotion and attachment for the Lord, and Gaṅgādevī is aware of Lord Śiva’s highly elevated position in *kṛṣṇa-prema*. By the touch of Gaṅgā water, Lord Śiva Himself became water and desired to remain thus submerged within her. Similarly, Gaṅgā devī was also happy for him to remain at that place and thus she worshiped him there with humility. From that time, the place became famous as Ambuliṅga-ghāṭa.

The village of Chatrabhoga is truly a very holy place of pilgrimage by the presence of Lord Śiva and Śrī Gaṅgā devī. However, with the visit of Śrī Gaurasundara, its transcendental significance and glories have increased unlimitedly, since He has left the impressions of His lotus feet upon this hallowed ground. Lord Caitanya became most ecstatic upon seeing Ambuliṅga and Gaṅgā devī’s one hundred streams.

Chanting loudly Lord Hari’s name, Śrī Caitanya embraced Nityānanda and they both fell swooning to the ground. Tumultuous chanting of the Holy Names from the assembled Vaiṣṇavas rent the air. Thrilled with spiritual joy, everyone led by the Lord Himself bathed in the sanctified waters of Gaṅgā devī at the ‘Ambuliṅga-ghāṭa’. Later in detail, Vedavyāsa will compile all these descriptions.

The Lord came out of the water and began to weep in uncontrollable divine exhilaration. As He changed into fresh dry clothes, they quickly became soaked with His tears of ecstasy. In the form of the river, Gaṅgā devī was flowing in one hundred streams, but also from the eyes of the Lord another one hundred cascades of ecstatic tears had appeared. Seeing this extraordinary phenomenon, the devotees were so amazed that they could only exult in jubilation.

The feudal landlord of that village was Rāmacandra Khān. Although materialistic, he was also a pious man, otherwise how could he meet the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, face to face? By the will of Providence, Rāmacandra was passing by seated in his palanquin when he saw the resplendent form of the Lord. He spontaneously felt awe and reverence for the Lord and immediately alighted from his palanquin. Falling like a stick, he prostrated himself at the lotus feet of the Lord. The Lord was still absorbed in *kṛṣṇa-prema*, and oblivious to everything about Him. He was crying tears of divine love profusely, heaving deep sighs and falling to the ground rolling in the dust. He kept chanting: “O Jagannātha! O Jagannātha!”

Rāmacandra Khān was extremely moved to see such an intense devotional mood. He thought, “There seems to be no way to stop this piteous crying for the Lord!” and he himself broke out into tears. Who in the three worlds could remain impassive and see these tearful entreaties? Even a stonehearted person would melt. The Lord calmed Himself and inquired from Rāmacandra, “Who are you?” Offering prostrated obeisances at the Lord’s feet, he spoke with folded hands, “O Lord, I am the servant of Your servants.” However, the local people who had gathered there spoke up, informing the Lord, “Our Lord, he is the landlord of the entire southern provinces.” Gaurasundara said, “It is heartening to know that you are a high ranking administrator. Kindly tell us how we may proceed to Nīlācala tomorrow.” As the Lord was speaking about Nīlācala, He was once again overcome by divine ecstasy. Crying out Jagannātha’s name, He began to weep profusely and again fell to the ground swooning.

Rāmacandra spoke in a concerned voice, “O Lord, whatever You order I consider my prime duty to fulfil. The roads are very dangerous during these times of enmity. Travelling between the two countries has become practically impossible. The inimical kings have placed camouflaged spears hidden in the ground all along the borderland, and if the soldiers find even an innocent traveller in these sensitive areas, they capture, torture, and murder him, thinking him an enemy spy. The only safe way I can arrange is to send you in secret. I am placing myself in great danger, but I do not care for this danger, I will certainly carry out your bidding. My Lord if You will kindly accept me as Your servitor then I pray that You and Your associates will take food in my house. I will use everything I possess—money, influence, men—to bring You across the border tonight.” The Lord was pleased with Rāmacandra and blessed him with His merciful glance.

By that one glance, Rāmacandra was purified of all material attachment. The Lord proceeded to his residence. By the visit of the Lord, Rāmacandra’s house became sanctified and everyone in the house exulted, being immediately awarded with unlimited pious *sukṛti*. The *brāhmaṇa* Rāmacandra himself prepared the food with great devotion and deference. The Lord nowadays ate very frugally. He had no spare moments away from His deep ecstatic absorption within Himself. He sat down to eat only for the satisfaction of His beloved devotees, for now His only real food was the spiritual mellows. Ever since He had embarked on this journey to Jagannātha Purī, He had eaten very little.

All the way the Lord had exhibited the mood of separation, imploring Lord Jagannātha. Day or night, land or water, were just fading images of no consequence to Him. He was constantly steeped in meditation within Himself, tasting the bliss of love of Kṛṣṇa. The devotees were always by His side keeping watch over Him, and protecting Him from any external harm. The different ecstatic moods exhibited by the Lord are impossible for an ordinary mortal to describe. The ecstatic manifestations of His spiritual trance are so sublime and esoteric that none other than Śrīla Vyāsadeva is able to describe them. Who can understand the character of the Supreme Lord? Who can predict how Kṛṣṇa will act next? Lord Nityānanda knows fully well the object of Lord Caitanya’s love, that Lord for whom He pines so imploringly. The Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, is always engrossed in the transcendental exchange of mellows where He Himself is the object of love. Yet, He forgets Himself as the main actor of these pastimes. On one hand, He thinks of Himself as Śrī Jagannātha, and on the other, He yearns for union with Śrī Jagannātha, in this way bringing the devotees to His side with concern for Him. How can the living entities realize the Supreme Lord unless He Himself does not shower them with His causeless mercy?

The Lord sat with Nityānanda Prabhu and the other devotees who were so dear to Him. He barely took a morsel of food and got up with a thunderous roar. With the after-lunch ablutions finished, He kept on asking, “How far is Jagannātha Purī? How far is Jagannātha Swami?” Mukunda quickly started to sing and the Lord began to dance with graceful postures. The fortunate and pious residents of Chatrabhoga had a rare treat. They saw the Supreme Lord, the Hero of Vaikuṇṭha, dance before their very eyes. As He danced, one after another of the ecstatic symptoms began to manifest upon His person in continuous waves whose dimensions were beyond comprehension—crying, shivering, roaring, horripilation, profuse perspiration, and becoming stunned like a statue. Who could understand the many subtle spiritual transformations that appeared in the Lord as He spun round and round? Tears gushed out of His eyes like the rushing currents of the Gaṅgā during the monsoon, drenching everyone. The incarnation of love of Kṛṣṇa in the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya has descended, who else but Śrī Caitanya has the potency to exhibit such pastimes.

Time passed and deep into the night, the *kīrtana* and dancing continued. When the night was almost at an end, the Lord calmed Himself and sat down. Although it was almost dawn, the long hours seemed to have gone by in just a few moments. Everyone was liberated and delivered by the Lord’s causeless mercy. Rāmacandra Khān, waiting for this opportune moment, said, “My Lord, the boats are ready waiting for You.”

The Lord immediately got up and went to the riverbank. Amidst tumultuous chanting of the Holy Name, the Lord alighted upon the boat and cast His blessed, compassionate glance upon everyone, bidding them all farewell. The boat then headed towards Jagannātha Purī as the Lord eagerly looked forward to reaching there, His own eternal abode.

Resting peacefully on the boat, Śrī Gaurasundara asked Mukunda to sing. As the boat moved silently in the still night, Mukunda started a beautiful melody. The boatman was a simple and illiterate person and said, “This singing is very fearful. I will surely lose my life tonight. On land, the tigers will maul us, and the water is infested with crocodiles. This part of the river is terrorized by bands of pirate dacoits who if they catch us will forcibly take both our wealth and our lives. So please remain quiet until we reach Orissa.”

The devotees were put into consternation, but the Lord’s absorption in spiritual mellows continued uninterrupted. In a short while, the Lord sounded like thunder and said, “What do you fear? Who are you afraid of? The Sudarśana-chakra, the lethal spinning disc of the Supreme Lord that protects the Vaiṣṇavas at all times from every danger, is here. Just look around you! Assail your trepidations and loudly continue the *kṛṣṇa-kīrtana*!” The reassuring words from the Lord had a miraculous effect on the devotees and they began to sing with renewed gusto.

Utilizing this exigent situation, the Lord gave instructions to the devotees, “The Sudarśana-cakra is always present to protect the devotees of the Lord. Sudarśana immediately scorches and destroys any inimical and atheistic forces that try to harass the devotees. If the Vaiṣṇava devotees have such an invincible protector as Śrī Viṣṇu’s own weapon, then who could possibly harm them?”

Thus, Śrī Gaurasundara constantly instructed His followers on esoteric truths. Only those who have received the Lord’s mercy can fathom the meaning of these confidential instructions.

The devotees performed *kīrtana* the entire way and soon the boat reached Orissa, stopping at the river port called Prayāga-ghāṭa where Śrī Caitanya landed from the boat. Reception of this narration of Śrī Gaurasundara entering Orissa accelerates the process of reaching spiritual perfection and all who hear are sure to swim in the nectar of *prema-rasa*.

The Lord was extremely joyful upon setting His lotus feet upon the soil of Orissa. He offered His obeisances to the holy land of Utkala and the devotees did the same. In that area there is a well-known bathing place called Gaṅgā-ghāṭa. The Lord took His bath there and later went to offer obeisances to the nearby Śiva-liṅga Deity known as Maheśa, which had been established right next to the bathing place by King Yudhiṣṭhira of the Pāṇḍavas. The Lord brought the joyful devotees to a temple and requesting them to wait and rest there, He went away to beg alms.

The Lord went door-to-door with His cloth spread out to receive alms. As He stood before each house, the people were captivated by His magnanimous appearance and immediately gave generously their best foodstuff, rice and vegetables, etc. Whatever was available in the household they gave with great pleasure. Lakṣmī Devī, the Goddess of Fortune, also known as Śrī Annapurna, the giver of all foodstuff and opulence, is always praying to receive shelter at the lotus feet of the Lord. That same Supreme Personality was now knocking on every door in the guise of a *sannyāsī* begging alms only to benedict the conditioned souls.

Feeling content, the Lord returned to the devotees after collecting alms. The devotees were joyful upon seeing what the Lord had collected and said, “Truly, dear Lord only you can maintain everyone!” Jagadānanda Paṇḍita gladly prepared a wonderful feast to which the Lord and all the devotees sat down. The whole night was passed in the village performing *kṛṣṇa-kīrtana* and at the first light of dawn they were again on the road walking towards Purī.

After a few miles, however, some persons demanding tax and refusing right of way to the devotees unless they paid, suddenly stopped them. Yet, when the tax collectors saw the grave and imposing figure of the Lord, they were impressed. They inquired, “How many men are with You?” The Lord replied, “I do not have anyone in this world, and I do not belong to anyone. I am all alone. The entire world is mine.”

Upon saying this, the Lord began shedding incessant tears, which flowed out in streams. The taxman said, “O master, You may kindly leave, but I will not release the others until I have received full payment.” The Lord left the group of devotees, remembering Kṛṣṇa and chanting His names. The devotees were plunged into an abyss of despondency, thinking that the Lord had left them.

However, the devotees, after some consideration, began to laugh at how the Lord had displayed wonderful detachment, but in the next moment they were again despairing, worried that the Lord would leave them altogether. Nityānanda Prabhu pacified them saying, “Do not worry. The Lord will not leave us behind.” The taxman said, “You are not accompanying that *sannyāsī*, so you must pay the proper charges.”

Chanting loudly Govinda’s name, the Lord had gone just a short distance and sat down with His head hanging down, tears welling out of His eyes. Even a heart of stone would melt seeing the Lord weeping in such an entreating way. The taxman was filled with wonderment. He said, “He is certainly not an ordinary soul. It is impossible for a human being to shed such an excessive amount of tears.”

Looking again carefully at everyone, he enquired from several devotees, “Tell me clearly who you are. Whose associates are you?” The devotees replied, “That *sannyāsī* is our master. You must have heard of Him; His name is Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and we are His servitors.” Saying this, the devotees broke down in tears of divine love for their Lord. The taxman was now completely dumbfounded. Being infused by their mood and purified by their association, he also began to cry, tears coursing down his cheeks.

The taxman now hastened toward the sitting figure of the Lord and threw himself down on the ground like a rod before the Lord’s lotus feet. Very humbly, he said, “My great fortune of seeing You has actually resulted from the pious activities of many millions of lifetimes. Kindly forgive my offences at Your feet, and I pray that You may arrive safely in Nīlācala.”

The Supreme Lord of all living entities, Śrī Gaurahari, blessed the taxman with his compassionate glance, chanted the Holy Name and restarted His journey. The Supreme Lord has advented as Śrī Caitanya to deliver all living entities with the exception of those atheistic, sinful reprobates who offend Vaiṣṇavas and commit sins on the strength of the Holy Name. Those who are inimical towards the Vaiṣṇavas will be deprived of the Lord’s mercy. Lord Caitanya’s name is so potent that even the demons have a change of heart by chanting His name and glories. Yet, the devilish reprobates do not accept this mercy, nor have faith in the power of His name.

The Lord of Vaikuṇṭha showered His merciful glance upon everyone as He went on His way to Nīlācala. Day and night, He was always internally absorbed, drinking deep from the endless nectarine ocean of loving mellows of Lord Kṛṣṇa. A few days later, He arrived on the banks of the River Suvarṇarekhā, finding her waters crystal clear. The Lord and the Vaiṣṇava devotees took their baths in the pellucid river thus further sanctifying it, and then continued onwards to their destination.

Somehow, Nityānanda Prabhu and Jagadānanda Paṇḍita had fallen back a distance from the rest of the group. Śrī Caitanya decided to sit down and wait for the two to catch up with them. Nityānanda Prabhu was always engrossed in deep meditation on Śrī Caitanya. This loving mellow made Him act intoxicated and seemingly mad. Sometimes, He would cry loudly almost wailing, then suddenly begin roaring loudly with the ear-splitting voice of a thunderbolt; then again, he would abruptly start to laugh whilst rolling on the ground. Whenever He saw a river or stream, He would plunge into the water and swim about in various directions for a long time. Then at other times, He would cover His body with dust. He would sometimes fall swooning in ecstasy to the ground so hard that everyone would believe that all His bones were shattered. When He started dancing, just on His own, it seemed the earth quivered like a leaf and tilted, appearing to be about to fall out of balance. This sort of behaviour and power is not unnatural for Śrī Nityānanda, for Śrī Ananta Śeṣa is His partial expansion and Śrī Caitanya resides eternally in His heart.

One time, Jagadānanda Paṇḍita, who had been assigned by the Lord to carry His *sannyāsa daṇḍa*, staff, on the journey, wanted to go and beg food from a nearby village. He considered it best to leave the Lord’s *daṇḍa* behind and so he said to Śrī Nityānanda, “Here, look after the Lord’s *daṇḍa* very carefully while I am gone.” With this, Jagadānanda gave Nityānanda the *daṇḍa*.

Nityānanda Prabhu, who was always meditating on Śrī Caitanya and thus absorbed in *prema-rasa*, took the *daṇḍa* and sat down. He started laughing, and holding the *daṇḍa* in one hand, He began speaking to it. He said, “O *daṇḍa*, you are carried by the same person I always carry in my heart. What logic is there in that?” Nityānanda Prabhu, who is Balarāma, got up and then smashed the *daṇḍa* to the ground with immense force breaking it in three places.

The Supreme Lord alone knows His own desires. How can I fathom why Nityānanda Balarāma broke the *daṇḍa*? Nityānanda Prabhu knows intimately the mind of Śrī Caitanya and Śrī Caitanya also fully understands the mind of Śrī Nityānanda. They are brothers eternally and They appear together in every *yuga*. Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa knew each other’s hearts deeply, for they are the one and same Supreme Lord. They have separated only to teach and enhance the loving mellows of devotional service. I am able to know Śrī Caitanya and His pastimes only by the mercy of Nityānanda Prabhu. Who other than Balarāma Himself would have had the power to smash the *daṇḍa* of the Lord? Actually, it is Śrī Caitanya, the supreme teacher, who is teaching, sometimes in many subtle ways. One who can penetrate and understand these puzzles and grasp their essential truth enjoys blissful devotional life.

When Jagadānanda Paṇḍita returned, he found Nityānanda sitting with the three broken pieces of the *daṇḍa* lying next to Him. At first, He was startled and astonished, but soon felt great anxiety. He inquired from Nityānanda, “Who broke the *daṇḍa*?” Nityānanda replied, “The one who took the *daṇḍa* in the first place. The Lord Himself has broken His own *daṇḍa*. Who else would dare and even do such a thing?” Jagadānanda thought it best not to retort—he simply picked up the broken pieces of the *daṇḍa* and silently walked away.

Jagadānanda went directly to where Lord Caitanya was seated. He threw the broken pieces of the *daṇḍa* in front of the Lord. The Lord looked up and asked, “How was the *daṇḍa* smashed like this? Did you get in a fight? Tell Me what has happened.” Jagadānanda narrated everything. He said, “Nityānanda, who is always rapt in ecstatic trance, has done this.” Śrī Caitanya, turning to Nityānanda, inquired, “What was Your reason for smashing My *daṇḍa*?” Nityānanda Prabhu retorted, “They were just some bamboo poles that I broke and if You cannot forgive Me for this action, then punish Me as You wish.” The Lord replied, “A *daṇḍa* is the residence of all the demigods and You reduce its importance to some bamboo poles!”

Who can comprehend the profound, esoteric pastimes of Lord Caitanya? What He considers in His mind He may never explain, and then say something quite different. So if anyone falsely claims to know the Lord’s mind, he is certainly ignorant and a fool. Internally, the Lord may decide to vanquish someone, but in His external dealings with the same person, He may be extremely endearing and affable. Similarly, when dealing with His beloved devotees, dearer to Him than His own self, He shows externally that He is impartial. These are the various moods and pastimes the Lord reveals. They are inconceivable and inscrutable, only those who are graced by the Lord’s mercy can perceive their true nature.

The *daṇḍa* was broken by the Lord’s own desire and arrangement, yet now He was showing His anger. The Lord said, “I had only My *daṇḍa* as a companion, but now by Kṛṣṇa’s will that also is broken and lost. Now I am alone, so all of you go ahead and I will follow behind.” No one dared to refute Lord Caitanya’s decision, but the devotees became concerned over this matter. Mukunda intervened and said, “You go ahead of us my Lord, for we must stay back for some work.” Saying, “Very well,” with polite agreement the Lord left, walking away like a lithe, mad lion with a supple gait that is hard to describe.

The Lord soon arrived in Jaleśvara village. He went directly to the temple of Lord Śiva, the main Deity of that village. The Śiva-liṅga Deity was well looked after by the local *brāhmaṇa* priest. The floral decorations in the temple and upon the Deity were attractive, and the smell of incense permeated the air giving the place an exhilarating devotional mood. Devotees in the temple were singing, playing musical instruments, and dancing. The Lord’s anger subsided in that joyful atmosphere. He let the loving devotional feelings in His heart gradually flow into and merge with the music. Enlivened by the opulence and influence in the temple of His dear devotee, Lord Śiva, Śrī Caitanya began to dance happily. Lord Caitanya knows the glorious character of Lord Śiva, for he is a favourite amongst His devotees. If anyone disrespects Lord Śiva, not following the example of Śrī Caitanya, then he cannot be considered a Vaiṣṇava, and all his spiritual advancement is annulled.

As the Lord danced, He made joyful sounds so loud that the very mountains seemed to tremble. Lord Śiva’s devotees were struck with amazement, and thought that Lord Śiva must have appeared in person. The musicians and singers reached again for a further crescendo, and the Lord became fully absorbed in dancing, losing all contact with the outside world. Meanwhile, His devotees arrived and Mukunda began to sing, joined by others. Seeing His beloved associates, the Lord experienced great joy, and danced more exuberantly than ever, while the devotees danced encircling Him. The whole scene was dynamically transformed. Tears flowed out effusively into a hundred streams from the Lord’s eyes. Who can describe all these happenings properly? The temple of Lord Śiva was now sanctified by the Lord’s presence and dancing. The actual purpose for which the temple was built was now fulfilled.

After awhile, the Lord became peaceful and embraced all His devotees with great love, giving them divine pleasure. Upon seeing Nityānanda Prabhu, the Lord rushed to embrace Him and holding Him firmly, Caitanya said, “Your real duty is to calm Me down, restrain Me, and help Me to maintain My *sannyāsa* vows, but instead You are misleading Me and increasing My madness. If you wish to continue in this way, then it is better that you finish me off right now. I am openly declaring: Whatever You want of Me, I will always act accordingly. This is the truth.”

The Lord then turned to the assembled devotees, instructing everyone, “Always give great care and respect to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu. His position is much more elevated than Mine. This is not spoken in an exaggerated manner—it is the simple truth. If anyone commits an offence at His lotus feet, but has not offended Me directly, still he is refused entry into the more confidential devotional service of the Lord. An offender against Nityānanda may be situated in devotional service, hence is considered by some as a devotee, but I reject him.” When Nityānanda Prabhu heard His own praise, He bashfully hung His head. All of the Lord’s pastimes are so wonderful, and they bring unlimited pleasure to the devotees.

Passing that night in Jaleśvara, at early dawn, the Lord restarted His journey accompanied by all the devotees. He went towards Vaṁśadaha and upon the way was stopped by a *śākta sannyāsī* (one who worships Devī, the energy of the Lord, as the Supreme). The Lord knew that the stranger was a *śākta*, but spoke to him with sweet words.

The Lord said, “Please tell me My friend, where you have been for so long that I am meeting you only now? Where are your other friends?” The *śākta* became captivated by the Lord and slowly began revealing all information about himself and all the other *śāktas*. Śrī Caitanya smiled as He listened to him. The *śākta* invited the Lord to his so-called monastery, saying, “Please come now to my *maṭha* and we can all enjoy the ‘bliss-drink’ together.”

The *śākta* was referring to an alcoholic drink as ‘bliss’ and this amused Śrī Caitanya and Nityānanda Prabhu. The Lord replied, “I will definitely come to enjoy your ‘bliss-drink’. First, You should go ahead to be sure everything is prepared for when we come.” The *śākta* was very pleased to hear that his invitation had been accepted and he left quickly, feeling elated.

How fathomless is the character of the Lord. The *Vedas* declare that Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the friend and deliverer of the poor and wretched. Hence, the Lord spoke so amiably to the *śākta sannyāsī*. Upon hearing the conversation, the devotees began to say, “This *śākta* has now been delivered, and by his contact, other *śāktas* will also become purified just as he is now.” The Lord uses various means to liberate the conditioned souls.

The Lord arrived at Remuṇā village, where is situated the Deity of Śrī Gopīnātha. Upon seeing Himself in this Deity form, the Lord began to dance ecstatically with all His devotees. Lost in love of Himself, He became oblivious to everything. He wept piteously in loving separation and even the cruellest of hearts melted upon hearing Him cry.

After a few days more of travel, Gaurasundara came to Yājapura village and stayed in the locality called Brāhmaṇa-nagara. There He visited the temple of Śrī Adi Varāha, where the self-manifested Deity is most wonderful and unique. By seeing this Deity, all material entanglements are surely severed. The temple was situated on the bank of the River Vaitaraṇī. By seeing this river, one is cleansed of all sins and the entire area is a very holy pilgrimage site. Even if just an animal crosses the river at this spot, the demigods see the animal to have attained liberation and taken a fourhanded Vaikuṇṭha form. Nīlācala Purī is exactly eighty miles away from this spot, which is known as Nābhi Gayā and also Virajā-kṣetra as this sacred area is abode of Virajā-devī. The entire area is dotted with many temples and holy spots, which are impossible to tabulate in detail. Upon arriving, the Lord first went with the devotees to take a dip in the holy river at the bathing place named Daśāśvamedha-ghāṭa. Thereafter, all went to the temple to offer worship to Lord Ādi-varāha. The Lord danced ecstatically in front of Ādi-varāha Deva, and the devotees blissfully sang, creating a wonderful, devotionally saturated atmosphere.

The Lord was very happy to be in Yājapura, ecstatically dancing before the Deity. His divine exhilaration and happiness increased with every moment of time, and He danced with increasing vigour. Suddenly, however, without warning, Śrī Caitanya left the devotees and disappeared. Certainly, the Lord’s desires and the reasons for His actions are most enigmatic. When the devotees discovered that Śrī Caitanya was missing from their company, they began to look throughout the temple in consternation. Their search proved futile and they became very worried.

Nityānanda Prabhu, realizing the plight of the devotees, said, “Please calm yourselves. I am certain I know where the Lord has gone. Surely, He wants to visit all the temples and holy places in Yājapura—but alone. Therefore, we should now beg for food and then return to this very same spot. Tonight, we will rest here, for the Lord is sure to return here tomorrow morning.”

Relieved, the devotees went out, collected alms, and returned to cook, after which they respected the *prasādam* all together. In the meantime, Śrī Caitanya had visited the different temples and holy spots and returned to the devotees. The devotees were jubilant and greeted Him with loud chanting of, “Hari! Hari!” In this way, the Lord with His associates blessed Yājapura with their blissful presence and then continued upon their journey.

After a few days, the Śrī Caitanya arrived in Kaṭaka city. From there, He went to take a dip in the crystal-clear waters of the River Mahānadī, leaving it more sanctified and fortunate than ever before. He then went to the temple of Sākṣi-gopāla to offer worship. The charming, unsurpassable beauty of the Deity of Sākṣi-gopāla greatly enraptured Śrī Caitanya and feeling surging ecstasy, He began to roar in thunderous voice. He offered many prayers, and exhibited wonderful devotional symptoms crying in ecstasy for the Lord. Chanting the *mahā-mantra* opens the spiritual vision of the devotees enabling them to see the Deity-forms of the Supreme Lord as non-different from the Lord Himself. Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya is the personality who has inaugurated the chanting of the *mahā-mantra*, and although He is the incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, yet He is always exhibiting the mood of servitorship to the Supreme Lord.

Śrī Caitanya then came to Bhuvaneśvara. This city is actually the hidden Kāśī, the residence of Lord Śiva, Śrī Śaṅkara. Previously, Lord Śiva had collected a drop of the waters from all the different holy places and brought them here to Bhuvaneśvara to form the lake known as Bindu-sarovara. Śrī Caitanya knew the significance of the lake as being most dear to Lord Śiva; thus, He took His bath in the lake and further increased its auspiciousness. The *liṅga* form of Lord Śiva, worshipped by the lake, is self-manifest. Śrī Caitanya took *darśana* of the *liṅga* and happily mingled with the crowds of Śiva devotees, who were all loudly chanting the praises of Lord Śiva. Small burning ghee lamps set in rows offered by the visiting devotees surrounded the *liṅga*, which was being bathed constantly.

Śrī Caitanya was pleased to see the rituals, worship, and opulent temple of His beloved devotee, Śrī Bhuvaneśvara Śiva. The Lord’s associates were also very happy in that devotional atmosphere. Lord Śiva is always immersed in the meditation upon the Supreme Lord, which makes him relish the nectar of devotion. Sometimes, He cannot keep from dancing, and sometimes He so forgets himself in bliss that He does not realize that He is without clothes. Now the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gauracandra, his master, was dancing ecstatically in front of him. The Lord and His devotees spent the night there.

I will now describe from the *Skanda Purāṇa* how Lord Śiva attained this place as His residence. Lord Śiva and his consort, Śrīmatī Pārvatī Devī, were living contentedly in Kāśī for a very long time. After time, they went to Mount Kailasa and left Kāśī to be ruled by kings who were ordinary mortal beings. Soon a king named Kāśīrāja ascended the throne. He was an ardent worshiper of Lord Śiva; however suddenly, by the will of destiny, he lost everything in a war. Yet, he was determined to destroy his conqueror, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, in further battle. With vengeance in his heart, he sat down to perform the most terrible of austerities, meditating upon Lord Śiva and imploring his benediction. Lord Śiva was attracted to appear before him by the potency of his austerity and offered him any boon he desired. Kāśīrāja eagerly asked, “I pray for only this boon from you, my lord, that I may avenge my defeat and destroy Kṛṣṇa in battle.”

Lord Śiva is a magnanimous personality, but no one can predict the manner in which he will bestow his favour upon someone. He said to Kāśīrāja, “O King prepare for battle. My army of followers will be right behind you in the field. Let me see who is strong enough to defeat you as long as I am behind you with my weapon, the ‘Paśupati’.”

Reassured by Śiva’s words, the foolish King Kāśīrāja again went off to battle against Kṛṣṇa, smiling confidently. Lord Śiva, accompanied by his associates and followers, followed the army of Kāśīrāja. His intention was to fight for the king. However, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supersoul situated within the heart of everyone, could immediately know what was happening. He swiftly sent His disc weapon, Sudarśana, to destroy the entire enemy army. The Sudarśana disc of the Lord is invincible, so unchallenged it went straight to Kāśīrāja and severed his head from his body.

Then, Sudarśana started burning everything in His wake, destroying the entire city of Vārāṇasī, the capital of Kāśīrāja. The city was razed to the ground. Unfortunately, this enraged Lord Śiva, and upon seeing his abode being devastated, he released his terrible Paśupati weapon. Yet, what can any weapon, however powerful, do against Sudarśana? The Paśupati weapon quickly retreated in fear and Sudarśana then went after Lord Śiva himself, who fled, terrified of the awesome weapon. The power and heat from the Sudarśana covered the entire world and Lord Śiva had no place to hide. Lord Śiva found himself in the same predicament as the sage Durvāsā, who had also experienced the pursuit of the very same fearsome weapon.

Lord Śiva finally understood that since the invincible Sudarśana disc was preying him upon, only Śrī Kṛṣṇa could help him out of his anxious predicament. Making his decision, he remembered Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and taking shelter at His lotus feet, he began to offer prayers to the Lord, “All glory to the Supreme Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mother Devakī. You are omnipresent and the shelter of all living entities. You give men both good intelligence and alternatively ill motivation. You are the creator, maintainer and protector. You never see the faults of others and are an ocean of compassion. You are the only well-wishing friend of all those in distress. You are the forgiver of all offences, so kindly forgive my offences since I have taken shelter of You.”

Śrī Kṛṣṇa, being thus appeased by the prayers of Lord Śiva, recalled His Sudarśana and appeared before him. Lord Śiva saw the Lord faintly smiling, although His eyes were still stern. His cowherd boyfriends and Vṛndāvana damsels manifested and surrounded the Lord.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said, “O Śiva, you are well-aware of My position and power, so what suddenly prompted you to act in this fashion? That degraded king, Kāśīrāja, was no better than a little insect and by siding with him you were fighting with Me. Now you have seen the fearsome might of My Sudarśana disc, which not even you could counter. All the most powerful weapons of the universe—such as the Brahmāstra and Paśupati-āstra combined—are no match for Sudarśana. Furthermore, a unique feature of the Sudarśana disc is that it will certainly attack the owners of weapons who challenge His power. I am surprised to see that you, of all persons, have become antagonistic towards Me. I am now feeling that there is no one in the entire creation who dislikes Me more than you!” Hearing these somewhat angry words of chastisement, Lord Śiva felt trepidation within.

Lord Śiva threw himself down to the ground and caught hold of the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Surrendering himself to the Lord, Śiva said, “O Lord, the entire creation is subservient to Your will. Who can claim to act independently? Just as dry straws are strewn by the wind, so does the entire material nature bend to Your command. Everyone executes Your wishes. There is no one who can disobey Your bidding. Somehow, You gave me the feeling of false pride and blinded by this foolish pride I was unable to perceive anything else—only myself as big and powerful. I am helpless, my Lord; it is only You who made me think in this manner. Your lotus feet are my life and soul eternally. Blissfully, I reside in the forest and meditate solely upon Your lotus feet. Yet, You churned this mood of arrogance within me. What could I do? For, I have acted, as You desired. Yet, in spite of everything, I have certainly committed serious offences at Your lotus feet, so now kindly forgive me and bless me with Your mercy. I pray for the boon that I may never again develop such evil intelligence. I have been rightly punished for my arrogance. Now kindly tell me where I can reside now that Kāśī is destroyed, who else but You can give me shelter.”

Śrī Kṛṣṇa smiled slightly and spoke kindly, “Listen, My dear Śiva, I am giving you a very beautiful place. Live here with all your associates and followers. This place is known as Ekāmrakavana. In this idyllic surrounding, you will appear and be worshipped. This place is in every way as captivating as Vārāṇasī. Besides, this place is also extremely elevated spiritually, but few know of this truth. Today, I will reveal to you the esoteric significance of Ekāmrakavana, which is so dear to Me.

On the shores of the ocean, covering a very large area is the place known as Nīlācala. This is also known as Puruṣottama-kṣetra, the abode of the Supreme Person. It has a most pleasing and peaceful atmosphere. Even at the time of the cosmic annihilation, this place remains intact, unscathed. I reside there eternally, and daily receive opulent offerings of foodstuffs.

Puruṣottama-kṣetra’s is spread over eighty square miles and within this area, all living entities possess fourhanded forms, though this is visible only to the demigods and their equals. The demigods glorify this place as the most auspicious of all places of pilgrimage. The act of sleeping here is equivalent to deep meditation, *samādhi*. Similarly, simply taking a lying posture here accrues the same pious result as offering obeisances to the Deity. Simply walking about here is the same as circumambulation, *pradakṣiṇa*, and all speeches here are the equivalent to glorification of the Supreme. These glories are all enumerated in the *Vedas*. Such is the potency of this *kṣetra* that even if one eats fish here it is the same as eating sacrificial vegetarian food, *haviṣya*. This place is very dear to Me; hence, it is known by My name and all the residents here are My equals. It is outside the jurisdiction of Yamarāja, the Guardian of Death. I am the judge here who determines the evil and pious deeds of an individual and their results.

The place I have designated as your residence lies north of My abode, Jagannātha Purī. Your place is, as I have described before, very beautiful and charming. Here one can very easily attain liberation and bliss. This place will be famous as Bhuvaneśvara.
