After delivering everyone in Kuliyā, the Lord proceeded towards Mathurā accompanied by His associates. He travelled along the banks of Gaṅgā devī, often drinking from and bathing in her waters, thus fulfilling her long-standing wishes.

On the banks of the Gaṅgā and near to the city of Gauḍa lay Rāmakeli, a township with a large community of *brāhmaṇas*. There the Lord remained incognito for a few days. Nevertheless, soon everyone came to know that Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya had arrived. Is it not an exercise in futility, if one tries to hide the sun? So soon, men and women of all kinds and ages poured in from every direction, feeling excited and flushed with pleasure.

As was usual, the Lord was absorbed in divine ecstasy—nothing could interfere with His immersion in the transcendental mellows. One after another, the different ecstatic symptoms manifested upon His person and He fell swooning, again and again. The devotees were also enwrapped in the blissful mood of the Lord and they performed continuous *kīrtana*, leaving aside all other business.

When sometimes the Lord cried out in a spiritual mood, this sound would carry far and be heard by travellers even a couple of miles away. Although most of the people were simple rustic folk, ignorant about the mellows and intricacies of devotional service; yet, by seeing the Lord in His entire variegated splendour, they became most happy.

Enraptured, the people remained watching the Lord from a distance and offered their prostrated obeisances, loudly resounding the Holy Name of, “Hari! Hari!” When the nectarine sound of the Lord’s name entered the ears of Śrī Caitanya, His bliss would increase several fold. He would lift His arms and encourage them saying, “Go on! Chant! Chant! Chant!”

The Lord blessed these people with such feelings of overwhelming joy that even the Muslims joined in by also chanting, “Hari! Hari!” The Lord was emanating so much compassion that even the Muslims would offer prostrated obeisances from a distance to the Lord. The Lord had no other thought in His mind than *kīrtana* and dancing.

Now, the crowd began to swell and grow; they watched entranced and no one had any desire to leave. The people were jubilant and their chanting made a tumultuous sound that rose upwards and rent the atmosphere for miles around. The only sound was: “Hari! Hari! Hari! Hari!”

Close by, within earshot, was the ruling Muslim king’s assembly house, yet, this did not cower the spirit of the *saṅkīrtana*. The assembly chanted loudly and fearlessly, forgetting all attachments to home and family.

However, in the meantime, the police inspector had gone to the King’s palace and reported the arrival of a *sannyāsī* in Rāmakeli. He also reported that this *sannyāsī’s* continuous chanting of some ghostly *mantra* of the faithless had attracted a huge gathering. To this news the king replied, “Tell me, how is this *sannyāsī*? What does He eat? What is His name? Describe His appearance.”

The inspector said, “Listen, your majesty, I have never seen anything so marvellous. His beauty far excels the beauty of Cupid and His complexion overshadows the brilliance of gold. His tall, majestic appearance, long arms extending to His knees, and slender concave abdomen are most charming. His lion’s neck, elephant’s shoulders, lotus eyes, and exquisite face more effulgent than a million moons, are incomparable. With red coral lips, a perfect set of pearly teeth, arched eyebrows like Cupid’s bow, a full broad chest decorated with sandalwood pulp, and generous hips covered by a cloth with the colour of the rising sun, He completely captures the mind. His feet are like two blooming pink lotuses; His ten toenails are like ten shining mirrors. I think He must be a prince out and about, travelling in the dress of a *sannyāsī*.

“The most remarkable thing about Him is that His body, which is as soft as freshly-churned butter, keeps falling to the ground with great force. He crashes down at least a hundred times in an hour, yet His body remains unhurt, unscathed. The hairs of His body are always standing on end like the skin of a jackfruit. At times, He shivers so violently that hundreds of people cannot keep Him calm. His eyes emit tears like two effusive rivers flowing endlessly, and sometimes He laughs out so long and loud that even for a couple of hours He does not stop. Then suddenly, overcome by the *kīrtana*, He falls swooning to the ground and remains lying unconscious to the great alarm of the onlookers. When He dances, undoubtedly it is the most sublime treat for the eyes as He raises His hands and incessantly chants, “Hari! Hari!” He seems to forget and be unaware of every other activity.

“The people who converged on that spot from all directions had no desire to leave. I myself have come across many *sannyāsīs*, mystics, and wise men in my lifetime, but this *sannyāsī* is certainly extraordinary. I repeat, your majesty, the arrival of this *sannyāsī* in your land is indeed the greatest blessing. He does not seem to eat or sleep. He is simply all the time enrapt in *kīrtana* and dancing.” The king, although grossly materialistic, heard everything, and he marvelled at the description of the *sannyāsī*.

Still quite in disbelief, the king called for Keśava Khān and inquired from him, “Keśava Khān, I want your opinion on this matter. Tell me what you think about this person everyone calls Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. Let me know in detail about the character of this powerful *guru* and *sannyāsī*. People are running from everywhere to see Him. What brings Him here?” Keśava Khān, a noble and upright gentleman, became a little wary. He answered, “Who is it that says He is a Gosāñi, a famous *guru*? He is a mendicant *sannyāsī*, a poor foreigner. He travels about just living under trees.”

The king firmly replied, “Do not refer to Him as poor. Surely, it is offensive even just to hear such things. This *sannyāsī* is obviously not an ordinary mortal. Undoubtedly, He is that Person whom the Hindus call Kṛṣṇa and the Muslims call Khoda. This kingdom of mine runs under my direction, but His orders control the entire universe. I am the King yet even in my own kingdom there are so many who are inimical to me; whereas, surely He is the Supreme Godhead, for one and all from everywhere worship Him with complete surrender.

If I stop my staff’s salary for but six months, then they will have so many complaints against me. However, in His case, I see that people are maintaining themselves at their own expense and even then eagerly going to see and serve Him without reservation. Therefore, please understand that this *sannyāsī* is the Supreme Lord. Do not say that He is some poverty-stricken mendicant.”

After a thoughtful pause the king continued to speak, “Now hear my orders concerning this *sannyāsī*. I do not want anyone to disturb Him. He is free to go anywhere and preach anything He chooses from His own scriptures. Let Him perform *kīrtana* with the people and be pleased to stay wherever He desires. If anyone tries to stop Him for anything, be he the Kazi, police inspector, or anyone else, then surely I will punish him with death.”

With these words, the king went inside to his inner quarters. Such are the wonderful ways of Śrī Caitanya, for this was the very same King Hussein Shah, who was responsible for desecrating and destroying hundreds of temples in Orissa.

Although Hussein Shah was such a fanatic and despotic Muslim ruler, even he accepted Śrī Gauracandra as the Supreme Lord. Nevertheless, the spiritually blind cannot see Gauracandra as the Supreme Personality. They shave their heads and become *sannyāsīs*, but when they hear the eulogies of the Lord, they burn within their stone-like hearts with envy.

The whole universe resounds with panegyrics of the Lord, and hearing of His glories quickly dissipates ignorance. Ananta Śeṣa, Lakṣmī Devī, Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva are all intoxicated and mad after relishing the super excellent pastimes of the Lord. The *Vedas* sing laudatory hymns in His praise, describing His supreme lordship over everything.

Therefore, if anyone feels irked upon hearing the sublime transcendental qualities of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, then even if he be endowed with all good characteristics, then those qualities become malefic and will surely cause him distress. On the other hand, if a person bereft of any good qualities sincerely remembers the lotus feet of the Lord, he is immediately elevated to the spiritual abode of Vaikuṇṭha.

The concluding portion, the *Antya-līlā*, of this book reveals the transcendental activities of the Lord performing *saṅkīrtana*.

The wise words of the King created new confidence in him amongst the pious circles. They secretly assembled in a house and began discussing this news. They said, “Our king’s character is terribly tyrannical. He is always influenced by the mode of ignorance. He has caused widespread devastation, demolishing thousands of temples in Orissa. Suddenly, by some divine arrangement, he is now being prompted by the mode of goodness. His words strongly indicate this change. Nevertheless, now again, if someone influential comes along and sways the King with ill advice against Śrī Caitanya, then the King might have Śrī Caitanya brought into his presence and then anything could happen. Therefore, we must immediately send a message to the Lord suggesting that this place, being always under the close surveillance of the Muslim king, is unsafe, and so He must proceed to the next village. A secret message containing this idea was quietly dispatched to Śrī Caitanya through a reliable and honest *brāhmaṇa*.

At the time, the messenger *brāhmaṇa* arrived, the Lord was submerged in divine ecstasy, relishing the bliss within Himself, and was continuously roaring like the rumbling of thunder. Millions of people chanted, “Hari! Hari!” and Śrī Caitanya danced in incalculable ecstasy. Unnecessary words or other activities never distracted Him from dancing, singing, and encouraging all to sing. The messenger *brāhmaṇa* stood there amazed at the sight, but failing to find the right opportunity to convey the message to Him.

What to speak of others trying to talk to Him, the Lord even refused to converse with His own associates. The Lord was swimming in the deep tides of ecstatic bliss, tasting the sweetest nectar of His devotion unto Himself, forgetting every other activity.

The messenger could not find the right occasion to speak to the Lord, so he approached the Lord’s intimate devotees. The *brāhmaṇa* said, “You are all followers of the Lord, so please approach Him timely and give Him a message from the pious section of our village. It is, ‘What is the necessity of staying so close to the King’s palace?’ ”

The *brāhmaṇa* then offered his repeated *daṇḍavats* to the Lord from a distance and left. The Lord’s associates were worried by the implications of the message. Yet, they could not deliver the message to the Lord—He was simply engrossed in dancing and oblivious to everything else. Raising both His arms, with a beautiful melodious voice, He called out, “Sing! Sing the name of Hari!” The millions who were swaying to the music joined in with clapping hands and exultant singing of, “Hari! Hari!”

Simply by remembering the devotees of the Lord, all obstacles are removed and the noose of material entanglement falls away. The living entities are able to perform even their smallest activities only by the help of His energy. He is glorified in the *Vedas* as the Supreme Brahman, the Absolute Truth, eternal, and pure. His illusory potency, *māyā*, puts the errant living entity into illusion whereby he forgets his constitutional position and becomes shackled by the chains of material life. Bringing with Him the immortal nectar of *kṛṣṇa-prema*, this very same Supreme Lord has now appeared only to liberate all conditioned souls.

What king can cause fear in the Lord? The *Vedas* declare that the Lord and Personification of Death, Yamarāja, is the menial servant of the Lord. Śrī Gauracandra, the son of Śrī Śacīmātā, is the Lord of both the material and spiritual planets. He now continued *kīrtana* with unbounded joy, unconcerned about anything else. The Lord had ignited the hearts of the teeming millions who had come to see Him with such transcendental happiness that even they were unafraid of the King’s close proximity, what to speak that the Lord Himself. Even though the spectators were mostly very simple folk, when they saw Śrī Caitanya they became fearless of even Death Personified, so how could the thought of a mere king invoke trepidation in them? The atmosphere resounded with jubilant chanting of, “Hari! Hari! Hari!” as the crowd joyously appreciated the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha freely mingling with them, singing and dancing.

Suddenly, the devotees who had received the message began to worry and the Lord, who is the Supreme Soul within the heart of everyone, immediately felt this. The Lord smiled and returned to His external consciousness and behaviour. To cut asunder the anxiety of His devotees, the Lord spoke, “I know you are very concerned and afraid for Me, but why should the King call for Me? It is natural that I meet someone who wishes to see Me; however, it is not possible that everyone should wish to see Me. So why be worried? If the King comes to see Me, then I will see him. On the other hand, how can the King order Me to come to him? What power does he have to do so? Only upon My prompting can the King say such words. Moreover, what is his ability to see Me when others far more powerful seek My grace and sight? The *Vedas* search for Me, yet do not see Me. Have not great kings, sages, demigods, and perfected *yogis* failed to see Me even after long and arduous searches?

“I have advented to propagate the congregational chanting of the Holy Names of Kṛṣṇa and by this I will deliver this sinful material world. In this age, those demons and evil forces that have never accepted My lordship and authority will weep in joy by chanting My names. Furthermore, I will vigorously distribute this ordinarily most rare devotional service, which is always most earnestly sought after by the demigods, sages, and perfected beings, to even the most abominable sinners, dog-eaters, untouchables, and women. However, those who, becoming intoxicated with education, wealth, family heritage, and knowledge, criticize and offend My devotees, I will deprive of everything and they will never know My true identity.

“I declare truly that My name will be preached in every town and village of this earth. I have appeared in this universe and I want that people should seek after Me, yet not all are doing so. Therefore, it is highly improbable that the King would want to see Me.”

The Lord finished His talk placating the devotees and giving them and hope and joy. The Lord stayed in that village for another few days performing *kīrtana* and dancing without any shadow of fear hanging over the people. Yet, who can actually understand the desire and mind of the Lord? For the Lord now turned around instead of proceeding onward to Mathurā.

Śrī Caitanya told the devotees, “I am going to see the Lord of Nīlācala.” The supremely independent Lord, the source of the highest spiritual bliss, then travelled southward, singing and dancing along the path. He stayed close to the Gaṅgā all the way, and in a few days, He arrived at the house of Advaita Ācārya. At this time, neglecting all other work, Advaita Ācārya was blissfully absorbed in watching the wondrous activities of His son.

I shall now describe the marvellous conduct of the son who had so captivated the whole attention of his father, Śrī Advaita Ācārya. The name of Advaita Ācārya’s son was Acyutānanda and he was certainly the fit son of an able father. One day, an elevated *sannyāsī* visited their house and met with Advaita Ācārya. The *sannyāsī* was at first hesitant, but then Advaita Ācārya offered His respects and seated him comfortably. Advaita inquired, “How can I serve you, master?” The *sannyāsī* replied, “There is just one thing I want to beg of You. I have a few questions I would like You to answer.” Advaita Ācārya replied, “Kindly take some *prasāda* first and then we shall talk.” However, the *sannyāsī* insisted, “I want to first know the answers to my queries.” Advaita Ācārya relented and said, “All right, please ask your questions.”

The *sannyāsī* said, “Please explain the relationship of Keśava Bhāratī with Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya?” Advaita Ācārya immediately considered the question in His mind, thinking, “There are two contrasting concepts involved here, the common social norms of this world and the higher spiritual perspective. Although the Supreme Lord does not have parents, still we say Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mother Devakī. Similarly, in a spiritual sense the Supreme Lord certainly does not need a *guru*, yet we find that the Lord is actually taking a *guru* and we widely glorify this activity of His. Therefore, why should I talk about the spiritual aspect first? Better that I speak about the social norms first.”

After thinking in this manner, Advaita Ācārya said to the *sannyāsī*, “Śrī Keśava Bhāratī is the *guru* of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. You already know that, yet why do you ask?” As Advaita Ācārya was speaking these words, Acyutānanda came running into the room. Acyutānanda was five, without any clothes, his chubby and charming form was covered with dust. He was as beautiful and attractive as Kārtikeya. Even at this age, he was already very knowledgeable, devoted, and an extremely potent personality. When he heard his father’s words saying that Śrī Caitanya had a *guru*, he became very upset and angry. Yet, when he spoke he smiled and said, “Father, what did You say? Could You please repeat it? Do You really think that Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya has a *guru*? I cannot understand how You can dare to say such a thing. If such words have emanated from Your mouth, then surely we now find ourselves in Kali-yuga, or perhaps this has happened because of the insurmountable illusory potency of Śrī Caitanya. This deluding potency may cover even Brahmā and Śiva and now I see that You have been affected by its unlimited power. If you are not under the influence of the Lord’s illusory potency, then how could You have uttered a statement such as: ‘Lord Caitanya has a *guru*’?

“By the desire of Śrī Caitanya the entire cosmic manifestation enters into the pores of His own transcendental body as He lies in the waters of the Causal Ocean. Many wise and powerful sages, proud of their great status, find themselves totally confused and lost by even the least of His pastimes.

“For example, by Śrī Caitanya’s sportive wish, Brahmā was born from the lotus that grew from His own lotus navel. Initially, Brahmā was completely lost and could not understand anything about his own source or present position. Finally, he began to meditate on the lotus feet of the Lord and when the Lord was satisfied with his *tapasya*, the Lord bestowed upon Brahmā transcendental knowledge. With this knowledge, Brahmā then began to create this material universe. Brahmā then passed down this knowledge to the elevated sage, Śanaka, and other great devotees, who very mercifully have propagated this knowledge to the whole world by the process of disciplic succession. How then, is it possible that You could say that that very same Supreme Personality, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, has a *guru*? You are my father and my instructing spiritual master, so I duty bound to learn from You. Why then are You giving wrong instructions?”

Acyutānanda became silent. Advaita Ācārya felt rising pride mixed with unbounded joy within Himself. He cried out, “Dear son, dear son!” and picked Acyutānanda up in His arms, drenching him with tears of ecstasy. He said to His son, “As a matter of fact, you are My father, and I am your son. You have come to Me as My son to give Me spiritual instructions. I have certainly offended you, so please forgive Me. I promise never to say such things any more.”

Acyutānanda became immediately shy hearing his own praises, and he kept his head down. Hearing the words of Acyutānanda so overwhelmed the visiting *sannyāsī* that he fell down to the ground like a stick offering his obeisances. He said, “Truly, he is worthy of being the son of Advaita Ācārya. Like father, like son. All this is very wonderful to me. Right here and now is proof of the inconceivable potency of the Lord. Otherwise, how could such words emanate from the mouth of a mere child? I have chosen an auspicious moment to come and see Advaita Ācārya and I have seen the most amazing miracle.” He offered repeated obeisances to Advaita Ācārya and his son, and feeling deeply content and blissful, the *sannyāsī* left, chanting the Holy Name of Śrī Hari.

Acyutānanda was indeed a worthy son of Advaita Ācārya because he had taken complete shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. If someone worships Advaita Ācārya, but disregards Śrī Caitanya, then even if he is Advaita Ācārya’s own son, he will be doomed. Advaita Ācārya was so impressed with His son that He forgot all other duties. He took him in His arms and wept in great satisfaction. He smeared the dust from His son’s body all over His own body. He began to dance happily saying, “The associate of Śrī Caitanya has appeared in My home.” Who can know the extent of Advaita Ācārya’s devotion as He danced with His son in His arms.

Śrī Caitanya found Advaita Ācārya engrossed in so dancing when He arrived at His house with all His associates. When Advaita Ācārya saw that the dear Lord of His heart had arrived, He fell to the ground and offered His obeisances chanting, “Hari! Hari!” He immediately went into a state of intense ecstasy oblivious to His body and home. The ladies of the house chanted loudly, praising the Lord. Advaita Ācārya’s house echoed with jubilant sounds and became full of bliss. Quickly, Śrī Caitanya took Advaita Ācārya firmly in His embrace and showered Him with tears of immense joy. However, Advaita Ācārya fell to the ground and placed the Lord’s lotus feet upon His chest whilst weeping profusely. The devotees were amazed to see such wonderful loving exchanges between the Lord and His dear associate, so they also were unable to contain their tears of happiness.

After some moments, Advaita Ācārya Prabhu composed Himself and with the utmost humility, He offered Śrī Caitanya a seat. The Lord sat down upon the elevated seat and His associates sat surrounding Him. Meanwhile, Advaita Prabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu grasped each other in a warm embrace reading each other’s hearts, which were effervescent with joy. All the devotees offered obeisances to Advaita Ācārya, who in turn clasped everyone in a loving embrace. Only Vedavyāsa is able to fully describe the transcendental joy that descended into the house of Advaita Ācārya that day.

Suddenly, Advaita Ācārya’s son, Acyutānanda, appeared in that assembly and fell at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya. The Lord quickly picked him up onto His lap and bathed him in tears of love. The Lord kept him lovingly, not letting him go, and Acyutānanda clung to the Lord not wanting to get down. The devotees were moved to tears of joy seeing the Lord’s extraordinary mercy upon this small boy. Everyone dearly loved Acyutānanda and similarly, all the Lord’s associates were very much loved and respected by Acyutānanda. Certainly, Śrī Nityānanda and Svarūpa Dāmodara loved him most dearly and he was the foremost of Gadādhara Paṇḍita’s disciples. For these reasons, Acyutānanda was considered by everyone to be the worthy son of an equally worthy father. Accordingly, now the Lord was experiencing divine bliss to be amongst His old and dear associates once again. He remained for a number days in Advaita Prabhu’s house constantly immersed in the ecstasy of *kīrtana*. Advaita Ācārya’s joy at having His dear Lord in His house was ever increasing.

After the initial excitement, Advaita Ācārya gave more thought to other matters. First, he sent a messenger to Navadvīpa to inform Śrī Śacīmātā of the Lord’s arrival in Śāntipur. The messenger was transported in a palanquin for speed and upon arrival in Navadvīpa, he requested Śrī Śacīmātā to immediately accompany him back to Advaita Ācārya’s house.

Since Śrī Caitanya had left home, Śrī Śacīmātā had gradually become increasingly immersed in an ocean of spiritual bliss of *kṛṣṇa-prema*. She now spent most of the time unaware of the external situation. She spoke things that appeared to have no immediate relevance, and often seemed to be listening to someone unseen. When Śacīmātā met anyone, she would ask, “Please tell me the news from Mathurā, Vṛndāvana. How are Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma faring in Mathurā? Just how well is that sinful demon, Kaṁsa, continuing his tyrannical activities? What about that thief, Akrūra, who stole my Rāma and Kṛṣṇa? In fact, I have heard that that demon, Kaṁsa, has died and Ugrasena has been crowned the new king.”

Sometimes Śacīmātā cried aloud, “Rāma! Kṛṣṇa! Quickly go to milk the cows. Then I shall sell the milk in the market.” Sometimes she was seen running absorbed in deep thought with her hands stretched out in front saying, “Hold Him! Hold Him! There runs the butter thief. Let me just see if You escape today. I will surely catch You and bind You up.”

At other times, when seeing another woman manifest before her, she would say, “Come, let us go to the Yamunā for a bath.” Many times, she appeared to wait piteously, her eyes releasing endless gushing streams of tears in such a manner that would cause even stone hearts to melt.

Sometimes, Śrī Kṛṣṇa would appear in her meditation and she would laugh in loud peals, perhaps for hours, exuding inexplicable joy. Then suddenly she would fall into an ecstatic swoon lasting several hours, where the external world would cease to exist for her.

Another amazing symptom was that when she began to tremble it was as if someone were repeatedly lifting her up in the air and hurling her down to the ground. No one other than Śrī Śacīmātā could exhibit such ecstatic feelings of *kṛṣṇa-prema*.

Śrī Caitanya is certainly the unlimited reservoir of love of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. He has also infused into Śrī Śacīmātā that same spiritual loving potency. Therefore, who can fully describe the various ecstatic transformations of Śacīmātā? Day and night, she was fully immersed in an ocean of devotional bliss, without a moments loss all her activities were devotional service to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Occasionally, when her consciousness would focus on the external reality, she would perform worship to her Deities of Śrī Viṣṇu. Fortuitously, when Śacīmātā was thus engaged in her Deity worship, the messenger from Śāntipur arrived.

The messenger said, “Śrī Gaurasundara has come to Śāntipur. Come, Śrī Śacīmātājī, let us go right away to see Him.” This news deeply moved Śacīmātā into a state of overwhelmingly placid bliss; she was indescribably contented. The word soon spread and the devotees became jubilant. Gaṅgādāsa Paṇḍita, Murāri Gupta, and all other beloved devotees of the Lord immediately accompanied Śacīmātā to Śāntipur. When Śacīmātā and the devotees arrived in Śāntipur, the news was quickly brought to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. The Lord rushed to meet His mother. When He saw her from a distance, He fell to the ground like a rod, offering obeisances. Chanting many verses, He circumambulated her repeatedly, offering repeated *daṇḍavats*.

He prayed, “You are the Universal Mother, the embodiment of pure devotion, transcendental to all material inebriety. Just by your gentle glance alone, the living entities can develop love and attachment for the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. You are the personification of devotional service to the Supreme Lord and have the potency to fulfil the desire of everyone. In fact, you are Gaṅgā devī, Mother Devakī, Yaśodā, Devahūti, Pṛśni, Anusūyā, Kauśalyā and Aditi. They have all emanated from you and will finally merge in you. You dwell in everyone’s heart; who can describe your transcendental glories?” In this manner, the Lord chanted eulogies, falling to the ground in joy, offering His loving obeisances.

Who other than Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself can exhibit such extraordinary heights of devotion to His father, mother, *guru*, and all superiors? As He offered obeisances and chanted prayers, His whole body was bathed in ecstatic tears. Seeing her son for the first time after such a long interval, Śrī Śacīmātā became inert with ecstatic bliss. All the while, as the Lord sang verses of praise, she remained stiff in spiritual shock like a wooden doll. The Lord continued exuberantly, “Whatever devotion I have for Kṛṣṇa is only due to your grace. All the millions of the Lord’s servitors who have even the slightest relationship with you are dearer to Me than my very life. Anyone who simply remembers you will become free from all material bondage. Gaṅgā devī and Tulasī devī are famous for purifying everything by their mere touch, but even they are highly privileged to have your association.

“You have used so much time, energy, and love to raise Me from birth. Your affection has cushioned Me at every step of My life. I will never be able to repay this incalculable debt of love to you. Only your very own wonderful qualities can counteract this burden of debt.” The Lord felt a special satisfaction in glorifying His mother and hearing the Lord, the devotees experienced deep transcendental joy. Śrī Śacīmātā, or ‘Ai’ as she is more popularly known, knew that her son was Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord incarnate upon earth, and so understood that whatever He wished He could say.

Śrī Śacīmātā then spoke, “Who can understand Your words? Logs in an ocean are tossed about and drawn away by the waves, not having any control of their direction. Similarly, without any volition, the living entities in this material ocean are being swept away by the waves of Your illusory potency. My dear son, I can only say that whatever You do is for the good of all. I see You are praising me and offering obeisances to me, but I only understand that You are independent, therefore You can act as You wish.”

The devotees greeted the words of Śacīmātā with spontaneous appreciation. Who can actually glorify the extent of Mother Ai’s devotion to the Supreme Lord? From her glorious womb the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Gaurasundara appeared. Even if someone speaks the name, ‘Ai’ without proper understanding of its spiritual significance, still by the transcendental potency of the word, he is alleviated from all suffering.

Śrī Śacīmātā’s heart was filled with immense satisfaction upon seeing her son. The devotees were swept away by tides of trembling ecstasy. To fully describe the joy that permeated the gathering is impossible for a puny mortal. Seeing the satisfaction of Mother Śacī, Nityānanda was overwhelmed by bliss. Advaita Ācārya whilst reciting prayers to Devakī devī, offered repeated obeisances to Śacīmātā. All the devotees like Haridāsa, Murāri, Śrīgarbha, Nārāyaṇa, Jagadīśa, Gopīnātha and others were most blissfully affected by her joys. Whosoever reads and hears these ecstatic narrations is enriched with the jewel of love for Kṛṣṇa.

Advaita Ācārya came to Śrī Caitanya and took permission for the fortunate Mother Śacī to cook for the Lord. Mother Ai went to the kitchen with bubbling joy, thinking, “I am cooking for my Gauracandra, who is the Supreme Lord, Nārāyaṇa.” Innumerable items of food appeared as if by magic. Many of the preparations she cooked are unknown to me and so I have no name to describe them. Śacīmātā knows that the Lord loves to eat *śāk*, spinach, so she turned out twenty varieties of *śāk*. In fact, each vegetable was prepared in ten to twenty different ways. After cooking, she brought all the dishes and placed them neatly in the dining hall, putting some *tulasī* buds on each item. In the middle of the room, she spread a very nice sitting mat for the Lord.

The Lord came with all His associates to eat. When He saw the elaborate arrangement with the countless dishes, He fell down and offered *daṇḍavats*. The Lord exclaimed, “Leave aside partaking of these foodstuffs. Just by seeing this transcendental food, one becomes freed from all material entanglement. How can I adequately glorify the quality of this cooking? In fact, simply by smelling the food one develops pure devotion to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. I can now understand that Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself, along with His associates, must have already tasted this delectable food.”

The Lord then circumambulated the *bhoga*, foodstuffs, and sat down to eat. Taking permission from the Lord, the devotees also sat down to see Him eat. As the Lord of all the Vaikuṇṭha planets ate, the fortunate Mother Ai feasted her eyes upon Him. He tasted every single item that was there with childlike relish. Yet, amongst all the dishes, the Lord preferred the different types of *śāk*, spinach. He ate from those preparations, again and again. Thus, the *śāk* gained the special favour of the Lord. The joyful devotees were thoroughly enthralled upon seeing the Lord constantly returning to the *śāk*. The Lord then began to explain the esoteric efficacy of eating *śāk*.

The Lord smiled and said, “This *śāk* here is known as ‘acyuta.’ By relishing this *śāk*, one quickly develops a special attachment for Śrī Kṛṣṇa. The result of eating *paṭala-vāstuka* and *kāla śāks* is that one attains the association of pure Vaiṣṇavas, birth after birth. By eating *sāliñcā* and *helāñcā śāk*, one is not only free from diseases, but achieves the platform of pure devotion to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.”

The Lord ate beautifully, and in between mouthfuls, spoke of the transcendental nature of eating the different kinds of *śāk*. That day while the Lord took *prasāda*, everyone experienced such spiritual ecstasy that only Śrī Ananta Śeṣa knows the facts in detail and He is now constantly describing them with His thousands of tongues. In Kali-yuga, the same Śrī Ananta Śeṣa, the support of all the three worlds, has now appeared as Śrī Nityānanda, the Avadhūta. All the *sutras* that I write are simply pointers given to me by His grace. In the future, Śrīla Vyāsadeva and other great sages will explain them all in detail. Anyone who reads and hears these descriptions becomes free from the darkness of ignorance.

After this pleasurable experience of eating, the Lord got up and cleansed Himself, rinsing His lotus mouth. As soon as He left His seat to wash up and then sat down elsewhere to relax, the devotees pounced on the Lord’s remnants and joyfully began to eat.

Someone said, “Why should a *brāhmaṇa* take these remnants? I am a *śūdra*, only I have the right to eat this.”

The other replied, “I am not a *brāhmaṇa*.”

Many just slipped in through the crowd and taking a handful of *prasāda* dashed away.

Someone said, “The *śūdras* are not eligible to eat remnants. Try to understand this by analysis. It is already stated in the scriptures.”

In reply, another said, “I do not want any remnant food. I just want the food vessels.”

Yet another devotee said, “It has always been my duty to throw away the Lord’s leaf plates, but now you are forcibly taking the remnants, simply showing your bossy natures.”

In this way, the devotees playfully used all cunning and any means to steal some of the nectarine remnants touched by the lotus mouth of the Lord. Considering that the food was cooked by Mother Ai and then respected by the Supreme Lord himself, it was hardly surprising that everyone was so greedy for such nectar. Happily licking their fingers after eating, they washed up, and returned to sit in front of the Lord.

The Lord looked at the devotees sitting around Him and spotted Murāri Gupta. The Lord smiled and said to him, “Murāri, I have heard that you have composed something about Lord Rāghava in eight verses. Please read it.” Murāri then began to read the verses in Sanskrit as if in a trance of ecstasy.

These are the verses: “I constantly serve the lotus feet of Śrī Rāmacandra, the spiritual master of the three worlds, whose brother, Śrī Lakṣmaṇa, is Śrī Ananta. Always walking in front of the Lord, Lakṣmaṇa, with a bright golden complexion, is dressed in opulent kingly attire. He is a most expert archer and always meditates upon serving His older brother, Śrī Rāma.

“I constantly serve the lotus feet of Śrī Rāmacandra, the spiritual master of the three worlds, who slew Khara, Triśirāḥ, and Kambandha, thus clearing the idyllic forest of Daṇḍakāraṇya of mischievous demons and making it pure and glorious. Killing the enemy Vāli, He befriended Sugrīva.” In this manner, Murāri Gupta recited all the eight verses and then upon the Lord’s instruction he began to explain the meaning of the verses.

Murāri explained, “With a complexion like that of fresh *dūrvā* grass, He is seated, smiling benignly, upon a majestic gem-studded throne. Śrī Jānakī devī, Sītā, is on His left. He is the supreme archer, teaching all the art of archery. He is the desire tree who more than fulfils all the yearnings of His devotees. His younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, is Śrī Ananta Śeṣa and is constantly absorbed in serving His elder brother, Śrī Rāma. Walking everywhere ahead of His elder brother, Lakṣmaṇa is an extraordinary archer. Lustrous with a golden complexion, He dons a stately golden robe. Śrī Rāmacandra, the pride of the Raghu dynasty, is the supreme teacher of everyone. I worship His lotus feet birth after birth. Bharata and Śatrughna fan Him with whisks, and Hanumān and his army of monkeys kneel with folded hands singing of the glorious activities of their Lord.

“I pray that, birth after birth, I may sing of His transcendental activities, for it is He who graced and befriended Guhaka-caṇḍāla, who belonged to the low caste of dog-eaters. The Lord willingly renounced the kingdom and crown upon the instructions of His *guru* and then lived in the forest to perform divine deeds. He killed King Vāli and mercifully offering His friendship to Sugrīva, He made him king. Everyone should take shelter of His lotus feet for He is the Lord of all the three worlds and He kindly liberated His devotee, Ahalyā. All should worship the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord who built a bridge across the ocean with the help of Śrī Lakṣmaṇa and the monkey army and then killed the demon King, Rāvaṇa, who was powerful enough to defeat even Indra, the king of the heavens.

“Worship the lotus feet of the best of the Raghu kings. By His mercy, the devout Vibhīṣaṇa became the King of Laṅkā although he was not in the least interested in the position. Such are the wondrous activities of the Lord that even the Muslim Yavanas are eager to hear of His pastimes.

“For all time He carries His bow for the suppression of the miscreants and cares for the subjects of His kingdom as His own children. By His mercy alone, all the residents of Ayodhya were transported to the spiritual sky in their selfsame form and became permanent residents of Vaikuṇṭha.

“Just worship the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord, Śrī Rāghavendra, who is eulogised in the *Vedas* as the Supreme Brahman. The Lord of the Universe, Maheśvara, Lord Śiva, forgets his clothing intoxicated by the nectar of chanting His Holy Name and Lakṣmī Devī is eternally engaged in massaging His lotus feet.”

Thus, Murāri Gupta recited and explained all the eight nectarine verses composed by himself in praise of Śrī Rāmacandra. Śrī Caitanya was very satisfied with Murāri Gupta and He placed His lotus feet upon the head of Murāri in blessing. The Lord said, “Listen, dear Gupta, by My blessing you will eternally serve the lotus feet of Śrī Rāmacandra and whoever takes your shelter and association for even a single moment will easily attain the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma.”

The devotees resounded their loud approval upon hearing the Lord shower His blessings on Murāri Gupta. In this way, the magnanimous Lord dispensed boons to His dear devotees. His associates always surround Him, they are like bees eternally attracted to the nectar emanating from the lotus feet of the Lord.

Suddenly a leper appeared in the assembly and came before the Lord. He threw himself down on the ground like a stick, groaning in pain. Then getting up he lifted his arms high and began to wail loudly. He said, “O merciful Lord, You have risen like the sun over this earth only to dissipate the sufferings of this material life. Your compassionate nature is always moved by the distress of others and so I have come to You. I am burning in the pain of leprosy. Kindly tell me how I may be relieved.”

However, when the leper had finished speaking, the Lord addressed him angrily with a thundering voice. He said, “Go! Go away from here! Just seeing you incurs sin. Even if a very pious man just sees your face, that day will bring him only woe. You are a wretched sinner and a Vaiṣṇava offender and surely much more suffering is in store for you. If you cannot even tolerate this pain, you contemptuous reprobate, then how are you going to live through the sufferings in Kumbhīpāka Hell?

“A Vaiṣṇava is so pure that just by uttering his name one can cleanse the entire universe. Lord Brahmā takes great pleasure in singing panegyrics on the qualities and activities of the Vaiṣṇava and one easily attains the association of the inconceivable Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa simply by serving the Vaiṣṇava. In fact, nothing is superior to the worship of a Vaiṣṇava. The *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* unequivocally explains that a Vaiṣṇava is dearer to Śrī Kṛṣṇa than even elevated personalities like Śrī Ananta Śeṣa, Lakṣmī Devī, Lord Brahmā or even Lord Śiva. The *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* 11.14.15. states: ‘O Uddhava, you and My devotees are more dear to Me than anyone else. Although Brahmā is My son; Śiva, My partial expansion; Sankarṣaṇa, My brother; and Lakṣmī Devī, My wife, they are not so dear as you are to Me. What to speak of others, you are dearer to Me than even My own self.’

“So anyone who offends a Vaiṣṇava and criticizes him has to suffer terrible consequences, life after life. A person’s piety, education, and austerity are all rendered worthless by criticism of a Vaiṣṇava and should the offender attempt to worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa, then this will also be useless, as the Lord will certainly refuse to accept such offerings.

“Mother Earth feels blessed when the Vaiṣṇava dances ecstatically upon her. In every direction that he glances, the Vaiṣṇava destroys nescience and sin. If when dancing, the Vaiṣṇava lifts his arms towards the sky, then he waives away any ill fortune in the heavenly abodes.

“Such an elevated devotee is Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and you are so demoniac that you have offended him. Your leprosy is just a mere reminder of your offences. The actual punishment is yet to come, to be meted out by Yamarāja, the God of Death. Therefore I do not even want to see you and surely I am not the one to deliver you.”

The leper quietly heard the chastisement of the Lord, then with utmost humility and meekness, holding straw in his teeth, he began to speak. He prayed, “In my ignorance I have destroyed myself. Delirious with the material disease, I have grievously criticized and offended a Vaiṣṇava. For this heinous act, I have rightly received my painful dues. Now my Lord, pray think of my deliverance. It is the nature of saintly personalities to heal the suffering of the wretched and forgive the blasphemers. Therefore, I beg to take shelter of You, but if You turn me away, who will save me? You know the penances for the different sinful activities, so, as You are a kind father to all, please tell me what penances will eradicate my offences. As I have sown the seeds of *vaiṣṇava-aparādha*, so I have painfully harvested my grief.”

The Lord replied, “Leprosy for an offender is just his first punishment. It is only the beginning; the worst is yet to come. Yamarāja has eight lakhs, forty thousand types of excruciating punishments awaiting the offenders. You should go right away to Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and throw yourself at his feet. It was Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita whom you offended and so you can be excused by his mercy alone. If a thorn is stuck in the foot, then it has to be picked out by another thorn, not that the shoulders have to be treated. This is the only means for your reprieve. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita is very elevated and intelligent. If you beg him, then he will surely forgive you.”

The devotees expressed their loud approval of the Lord’s perfect and honest instructions. The leper paid his obeisances to the Lord and the devotees and hurried off to see Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, out of his causeless mercy, exonerated the leper from all offences and saved him from the worst of fates. The Lord had clearly described the horrific results of offending a Vaiṣṇava. In spite of hearing this, if a person is still so foolish to indulge in criticism and blasphemy of the Vaiṣṇavas, then Śrī Caitanya will personally mete out the due punishment.

If one sees two Vaiṣṇavas quarrelling, then one should never think that something is amiss, or that there is enmity and malice between them. Such quarrelling is in fact pleasing to the Lord and is transcendental. The arguments and abuses exchanged between Rukmiṇī devī and Satyabhāmā devī although sounding like serious fights are factually not so, because they are forever united in their service to their common Lord and master. There is no enmity between Vaiṣṇavas.

The Supreme Lord Himself induces these fights due to His frolicsome nature. Nevertheless, if anyone foolishly sides with one Vaiṣṇava against another, then he is doomed due to offending a Vaiṣṇava. The Vaiṣṇavas are the extensions of the limbs of the Lord, so how may one benefit by serving Him with one hand and inflicting pain upon Him with the other?

To become steady in devotional service, one should develop the vision that Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His devotees, the Vaiṣṇavas, are non-different and then immersed in this perception one should serve the Lord and His dear devotees. One can then easily cross the ocean of nescience. One who glorifies, hears, and understands these transcendental subject matters will always avoid *vaiṣṇava-aparādha*.

The Lord remained a few days more in Śāntipur enjoying His stay in the house of Advaita Ācārya. Soon, it was time to celebrate the auspicious appearance day of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī. Although in status there is no difference between Mādhavendra Purī and Advaita Ācārya, yet Advaita Ācārya always considered Himself the disciple of Mādhavendra Purī. Unquestionably, Gaurasundara is personally present eternally in the body of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī. His devotion to the Supreme Lord is unparalleled and by the grace of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the transcendental potencies of the Lord were manifest in Mādhavendra Purī. Kindly hear attentively how Advaita Ācārya became the disciple of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī.

Before the advent of Śrī Caitanya in this world, the entire planet was bereft of any devotional feelings towards the Supreme Lord. Yet, even then, Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī, by the special mercy of Śrī Caitanya, was constantly experiencing devotional ecstasy. All the ecstatic symptoms would manifest upon his person. Internally, he was so completely immersed in meditation upon the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa that he was unmindful of what he was doing. While walking on the streets, suddenly he would start to dance very gracefully and chant the Holy Name. Sometimes, due to intense devotional feelings, he would be stunned and go into a spiritual coma lasting several hours. Again at times, experiencing acute love in separation, he would cry shedding torrential tears that gushed out like the River Gaṅgā in spate. Then there were instances where he would break out into loud peals of laughter and, being intoxicated by the nectar of *kṛṣṇa-prema*, he would be unaware that he had lost the clothes he had been wearing.

Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī spent his days happily relishing his sublime relationship with Śrī Kṛṣṇa. However, the absence of devotion amongst the general populace disturbed him and made him morose. Feeling great compassion, he thought deeply on how to alleviate this suffering of the people. He arrived at the conclusion that the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, must appear. At that time, the society had neither interest, nor understood the importance of celebrating nightlong *kīrtana* festivals glorifying the pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. However, the people would stay up nights listening to songs about the demigoddess Maṅgala-Caṇḍī and consider this as a perfect religious activity. The only gods they knew were demigods such as Ṣaṣṭhī and Viṣahari, and they worshiped these demigods with much fanfare and ostentation.

Many persons simply desired to increase their wealth and dynasty. To achieve this end, they worshiped demons and ghosts with offerings of wine and animal flesh. Their fondest enjoyment was to listen to banal songs of equally mundane songsters. It was truly a sign of great piety if someone would utter the names of Śrī Hari, ‘Govinda or Puṇḍarīkākṣa,’ just once, at the time of the morning bath. People were so steeped in the mode of ignorance and deluded by Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s illusory potency, *māyā*, that they had no concept of what or who is a Vaiṣṇava, what is *kṛṣṇa-kīrtana*, and why do devotees dance and even weep in ecstasy during *kīrtana*.

Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī was deeply pained by the godlessness of the people, yet he found no one to speak to. Thinking that *sannyāsīs* would be sympathetic to his concern because of their renounced order, he would approach them, but to his dismay he found them polluted by the desire to become one with the Supreme, so he gave up further attempts to talk to them. He felt forlorn—he had no place to turn where he could discuss the topics of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. Learned scholars, *yogis*, hermits, and even *sannyāsīs* were never heard speaking any instructions guiding the people to serve the Supreme Lord. All of them were only interested in exhibiting their so-called learning by presenting logic and argument. In fact, they had become agnostics refusing to accept and revere the Deity forms of the Supreme Lord. Seeing these negative conditions and finding himself all alone, Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī decided to live in the forest away from such a fallen society.

Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī observed, “Why am I roaming amongst such people searching for a Vaiṣṇava? How can I meet one amongst them, if they themselves have no appreciation for a Vaiṣṇava? Therefore, let me just go to the forest and live there. There at least I will not have to associate with the non-devotees.” About the time he had made up his mind to withdraw from society, by divine arrangement he met Śrī Advaita Ācārya, who was also greatly afflicted for the very same reason. Advaita felt despondent upon seeing the people’s empty and meaningless existence, their lives devoid of devotion to the Supreme Lord.

In the meanwhile and in spite of such reverse conditions, Śrī Advaita Ācārya by the Lord’s mercy alone had continued to preach about devotional service to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. His discourses on the *Gītā* and *Bhāgavatam* always stressed devotional service to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, which is, in fact, the essential truth of these books. Therefore, when Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī came to the house of Śrī Advaita, it was a wonderful meeting of two highly elevated Vaiṣṇavas.

When Śrī Advaita saw Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī, recognizing all the signs of saintliness in him, he immediately fell to the ground offering his obeisances. Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī picked up Śrī Advaita and embraced him warmly, drenching him with tears of spiritual ecstasy. They sat down together and entered the unlimited nectar ocean of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. They forgot themselves and everything else talking to each other about Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī was such an elevated devotee and lover of Kṛṣṇa that just by seeing a blackish cloud he would become unconscious due to uncontrollable spiritual agitation. Hearing the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa would bring him immediate ecstasy and roaring loudly, he would manifest various symptoms of divine love. Śrī Advaita could see all these Vaiṣṇava qualities in Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī. He was extremely pleased to meet him and so he wanted to hear spiritual instructions from him. This was how the two spiritual stalwarts met.

Since that time, Śrī Advaita Ācārya had always celebrated the appearance day of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī with great joy and festivity leaving aside all other work. So now, he applied himself fully to commemorate this special occasion. Śrī Caitanya and His associates were also most happy to join in the celebration, especially upon seeing how vigorously Śrī Advaita went about decorating and making endless preparations for the celebration. Necessary requirements began pouring in from different people, clearly indicating just how many persons were attracted to the saintly qualities of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī. The devotees enthusiastically distributed different duties amongst themselves according to their capabilities to help with the preparations.

Śrī Śacīmātā accepted the responsibility for all the cooking. The housewives gathered around her and began to get things ready. Śrī Nityānanda, who is always self-satisfied, wanted to serve and worship such a special Vaiṣṇava. One devotee expressed his desire, “I want to make all the sandalwood paste.” Another said, “I will make the flower garlands.” “I will fetch the water,” said another, “Then give me the duty to wash and clean the floors,” said yet another. Another devotee said, “All right then, let me wash the feet of all the Vaiṣṇavas.”

Everywhere the devotees were very busy. Some were spreading multicoloured cloth awnings overhead and tying the corners to nails. Others hurried to bring vegetables, oils and so on to the kitchen. Many devotees began *kīrtana* and dancing and some joined in playing the gong and blowing conchshells. The devotees were jubilant, loudly chanting, “Hari! Hari!” while they enthusiastically performed their various services. The festive mood had everyone in a grip and a happy tumult echoed everywhere. The loud chanting of the Holy Name, the blowing of conches, and the sounds of cymbal, gong and drums transformed the house of Śrī Advaita into Vaikuṇṭha.

The Lord was very satisfied with all the elaborate arrangements and went around the house looking at everything. At least two rooms were packed solid with bags of rice. The high stacks of firewood were like mountains. Several rooms were being used for cooking with innumerable pots strewn everywhere. A few rooms were filled with just lentil dhal and about seven rooms were packed with clothes. Rooms and rooms were taken up with flat rice, puffed rice, and leaf plates. It would be impossible to count the number of bananas, coconuts, and big lumps of molasses, lying around. Then came the many, many rooms filled with an array of all sorts of vegetables like *paṭoḷa*, (squashes), aubergine, *khoḍas* (banana tree stem), *alus* (potatoes), *śāk* (spinaches), and so on. Another spectacle that met the Lord’s eyes was the rows and rows of large containers filled with milk, yoghurt and cream. Piled high were the sugar canes and next to them were large vessels of oil, ghee, and salt. The miraculous display, which appeared as if from nowhere, is indescribable in its variety and volume.

The Lord was filled with wonder for He knew that it was not humanly possible for one person to accomplish all this at such short notice. The Lord said, “Such a manifestation of opulence cannot be the work of an ordinary mortal. Śrī Advaita must be Maheśa, Śiva; this is what I strongly feel. This miracle is possible only for Mahādeva, Lord Śiva. Advaita Ācārya must be the incarnation of Lord Śiva.” The Lord smiled and kept repeating these words.

In this manner, through such intimation, the Lord revealed the actual spiritual identity of Advaita Ācārya. One who is pious will accept these statements of Śrī Caitanya with great spiritual joy; and those non-believers, who have no faith in the Lord’s words, will be confronted by Advaita Ācārya Himself as a horrendous consuming conflagration. Although Śrī Advaita is inherently very compassionate and His shelter is as cooling as the embalming rays of millions of moons, He transforms Himself into the terrible form of All-devouring Death to those who have no faith in Śrī Caitanya.

The *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*, the *Vedas*, in fact all the scriptures clearly declare that if anyone utters the name of Lord Śiva, even without understanding the correct esoteric truth about such a great personality, still he is absolved of all sins immediately. Conversely, if there is such a wretched person who will denounce the glorious name of Lord Śiva and even feels depressed through envy upon hearing that wonderful name, then he is certainly thrown into an ocean of dark despondency.

In the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* 4.4.14. Satī says to her father Prajapati Dakṣa, “My dear father, you are committing the greatest offence by envying Lord Śiva, whose very name, consisting of two syllables, ‘*śi*’ and ‘*va*’, purifies one of all sinful activities. His order is never neglected. Lord Śiva is always pure, and no one but you envies him. He is famous as being completely pure-hearted and you are trying to be inimical to such an exalted personality. Fie upon you! You embody misfortune!”

Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself asks how could any person worship Him and not worship Lord Śiva? How can one develop love for Kṛṣṇa, if he disregards Śiva who is so dear to Kṛṣṇa? In the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*, Kṛṣṇa states: “How can anyone render devotional service to Me without worshiping My dear devotee, Śiva, in the proper devotional mood. A person who does not respect Śiva is certainly envious of the Vaiṣṇavas and is a sinful reprobate.”

Further, the Skanda *Purāṇa* declares: “Firstly, one should worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the cause of all causes, and then worship the best of the demigods, Lord Śiva. Next, all the other demigods should be worshiped with great faith and devotion.” Śrī Advaita Ācārya is accepted by the greatest saintly personalities as Lord Śiva himself, because Śrī Caitanya gave sufficient and clear indications to establish this truth. Naturally, less-intelligent persons raise clamorous objections against such truths; unable to gauge the transcendental potencies of Śrī Advaita Ācārya, they perish.

Thus, the Lord went around taking stock of all the bountiful arrangements, although it is impossible for me as the author to note them all down in complete detail, such was the elaborate array. The Lord was very pleased and He began to glorify Śrī Advaita to everyone. The Lord then returned to the place of the *kīrtana* and His presence immediately accelerated the enthusiasm of the *kīrtana*, drowning the devotees in a deluge of divine nectar. Devotees danced in every direction, singing and clapping, their uncontained joy increasing with every passing moment. Clearly discernable and far above all other reverberation was the singing of the Holy Names of Godhead. The devotees were now shining with even greater effulgence, their bodies decorated with sandalwood paste and flower garlands. The associates of the Lord were all very near and dear to Him and their joyous singing of the Holy Name spread everywhere purifying the entire universe.

Śrī Nityānanda, with His tall impressive stature like that of a powerful wrestler, danced and pranced about like a little boy, chuckling with pure innocent glee. Śrī Advaita Ācārya was totally absorbed in dancing and unaware of the passage of time. Haridāsa Ṭhākura and all the other devotees danced and sang jubilantly. Then, after first inspiring everyone else to dance, Śrī Caitanya joined with all the devotees in the joyful dancing. Exuberantly dancing, the devotees encircled Him and kept Him there in the centre. The whole day passed in the ecstasy of *kīrtana* and dancing, and finally the Lord sat down with all the devotees. Śrī Advaita begged permission from the Lord to prepare for the feasting and then busied Himself making the all the necessary arrangements for the *prasādam* of the Vaiṣṇavas.

Soon the Lord sat down to eat with His entire group of devotees. As usual, the devotees sat around Him, everyone wanting Him to be in the centre. Like the many shining luminaries in the dark purple sky were the devotees, and the Lord arose on the horizon looking more effulgent than a million moons. Śrī Śacīmātā had prepared a delicious feast in honour of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī, with an incredible variety of rice preparations, vegetables, and sweets. The Lord relished the transcendental delicacies and spoke about the glories of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī between His mouthfuls. It would be difficult to say which type of nectarine mouthful He relished more. The Lord said, “If one is fortunate enough to taste this wonderful *prasādam* in honour of the appearance day of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī, then one is immediately showered with loving devotion to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.”

The Lord then got up from *prasāda* and, after rinsing His lotus mouth, returned to sit down. Śrī Advaita brought sandalwood paste and many flower garlands and placed them all before the Lord. First, the Lord garlanded and smeared sandalwood paste on Śrī Nityānanda and Svarūpa Dāmodara Prabhu with great affection. Then, one by one, the Lord garlanded and smeared sandalwood paste on all the assembled Vaiṣṇavas with His very own hands. The devotees were extremely happy to have received these items directly from the Lord. They all loudly cried out the Lord’s Holy Name making a joyous clamour that is impossible to describe. Surely, there is no way to gauge the pinnacles of ecstasy to which Śrī Advaita climbed, because, above everything, He had the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha Himself as His honoured guest.

How is it humanly possible to fully describe all these transcendental pastimes of the Lord? The different activities the Lord performs within the span of a single day cannot be recorded by anyone even if he be allowed a period of a million years for the completion. Like a bird flying in the vast vault of the sky is unable to find its limits, similarly the pastimes of the Lord are unlimited, and one is enabled to know only as much as the Lord empowers one to see and understand. The wooden doll is completely controlled by the puppeteer; so also, I can say only as much as the Lord prompts me to say. I do not even properly know the chronological order of these pastimes. Yet, somehow or other, I am writing the glories of the Lord. I beg humbly at the lotus feet of all the Vaiṣṇavas to forgive me for my offences in this effort of writing.

One who listens to these transcendental topics will certainly attain loving devotion to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu are my life and soul. I, Vṛndāvana dāsa, humbly offer this song at Their lotus feet.

## 5: The Pastimes of Śrī Nityānanda

All glory to Śrī Gaurasundara, the original spiritual preceptor of the entire universe! You are the desire tree of all the surrendered devotees. All glory to You, who are the most brilliant gem of the *sannyāsa* order and the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha! Kindly, bless the living entities with Your most auspicious and merciful glance. All glory to the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurāṅga along with all His devotees and intimate associates who are always victorious! O Lord, You are the most munificent, kindness personified, and an ocean of divine compassion.

Please hear attentively the topics narrated about the Lord in this *Antya-khaṇḍa*, the concluding portion of this book.

The Lord stayed on for another few days in the house of Śrī Advaita and then went to the house of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita in Kumārahatta. As the Lord arrived, Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita was immersed in deep ecstatic meditation upon Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Therefore, when Śrī Gaurasundara, the Lord of Śrīvāsa’s life, suddenly appeared before Śrīvāsa the object and fruit of his deep and sincere contemplation was then realised.

Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita threw himself to the ground like a stick, paying his respects to the Lord. He clasped the lotus feet of the Lord to his chest and heaving long and deep sighs of love he wept profusely. The Lord picked up Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and embraced him, drenching him with His own jubilant tears of divine love.

By the causeless mercy of the Lord, the entire family of Śrīvāsa was truly blessed and, raising their arms in gestures of overwhelming joy, they all crowded to see the Lord and began to weep in joy. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita was beside himself with happiness. He could not fathom the exhilaration he experienced by the personal presence of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha as a guest in his house. Placing his best and most exquisite *āsana* upon his head, he brought it to the Lord. The lotus-eyed Gaurāṅga then sat down surrounded by His dearmost devotees who then began *kīrtana*. The ladies of the house all ululated, making auspicious sounds of welcome for the Lord, and the house of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita resounded with the highest joy, becoming engulfed in bliss.

News of the Lord’s arrival spread quickly and Ācārya Purandara came running swiftly to see Śrī Gaurasundara. The Lord embraced him with warm affection and reverence, considering him to be His father. In the Lord’s embrace Ācārya Purandara, the most exalted and righteous amongst men, felt great spiritual energy surge through his body and was overwhelmed with spiritual emotion. He was unable to hold back his tears of extreme joy.

Soon other visitors streamed in. Śrīla Vāsudeva Datta followed by Śrīla Śivānanda Sena, and all their family members, arrived to see the Lord. Vāsudeva Datta was very dear to the Lord. A swan-like personality, by the Lord’s grace, He knew all the most esoteric conclusions. He was constantly reflecting on how to properly benefit all living entities. Compassionate to everyone, he was perpetually absorbed in thoughts of Śrī Caitanya, deeply immersed in Śrī Caitanya *prema-rasa*.

He never looked for faults in others, but always praised their good qualities. He had great attraction and love for the Supreme Lord and His service, and was always respectful to the Vaiṣṇavas, rendering humble service to them. When the Lord saw Śrī Vāsudeva Datta, He was most pleased and jubilantly embraced him, weeping profusely in ecstasy. Śrī Vāsudeva quickly fell to his knees and clasped the Lord’s lotus feet, crying out loudly. He cried so piteously that, what to speak of men, even stones would be moved to tears. Śrī Vasudeva was endowed with such wonderful qualities that he alone could exemplify himself.

The Lord loved Śrī Vāsudeva so dearly and said, “It is indeed true that I belong to Vāsudeva.” Repeatedly the Lord said, “My body is the property of Vāsudeva and his alone. He can sell Me anywhere he pleases. I say truly, by him I willingly allow myself to be sold to any one. A moment’s association with Śrī Vāsudeva Datta can bless anyone with Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s protection from all dangers. O Vaiṣṇava devotees, please hear Me. I say truly that Śrī Vāsudeva owns me completely. Whoever is just touched by the breeze over his body will be always protected by the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.” The devotees became jubilant hearing the Lord shower such causeless mercy on Śrī Vāsudeva and loudly chanted the Holy Name. Śrī Gaurasundara is extremely adept in glorifying His devotees to illustrate their glories. Similarly, the devotees are always eulogizing the transcendental qualities of the Lord.

The Lord stayed for some time in Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita’s house performing exhilarating pastimes. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and his brother Rāmāi Paṇḍita were always engaged in singing the glories of the Lord, and the Lord, feeling spiritually animated by their singing, danced in ecstasy. Both the brothers, Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and Rāmāi Paṇḍita are very beloved of the Lord. In fact, they are like two expanded bodies of the Lord. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita always pleased the Lord in many ways by performing *kīrtana*, discussing the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*, and by maintaining proper standards of Vaiṣṇava etiquette. Surely, in the house of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, the Lord performed some of His most wonderful pastimes.

One day, the Lord called Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita aside and asked him confidentially about some family matters. The Lord said, “I see you never go anywhere. How will you manage to make ends meet in the family and how are you doing so presently?” Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita replied, “My Lord, I have not the heart to go anywhere.” The Lord gently prodded the subject further asking, “You have a large family to maintain, how then will you look after them?” Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita said, “Certainly, whatever is my destiny will come as provisions. Each person receives his due; he will surely find whatever providence provides. We shall manage with whatever comes our way.” Hearing this the Lord said, “Then, with this mentality, Śrīvāsa, take *sannyāsa*!” Śrīvāsa replied, “That is not possible for me.”

The Lord said, “On one hand you refuse to beg alms as a *sannyāsa* and on the other hand you do not make an effort for your livelihood or even collect food door to door. How do you plan to maintain your family? I am unable to understand you. Nowadays, if one does not make the effort of going hither and thither then nothing will come of its own. Under the circumstances, please tell Me what you propose to do?” Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita said clapping his hands thrice, “Here is my explanation—one, two, three.” The Lord insisted, “Kindly clarify why you have clapped thrice, what does, ‘One, two, three,’ imply?” Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita replied calmly, “I have taken a solemn vow that if after fasting for three days I do not get a morsel of food by it’s own accord, then, I will surely tie a stone around my neck and throw myself in the Gaṅgā to drown.”

As soon as the Lord heard these words He roared like thunder and said, “What did you say, Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita? You may fast due to a lack of food? By some rare chance, even Lakṣmī Devī may have to go begging, but your family will undoubtedly never experience poverty. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, have you already forgotten what I have said in the *Bhagavad-gītā* 9.22: ‘Those who worship Me with devotion meditating upon My transcendental form, to them I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.’ Those devotees who are fixed in undeviating meditation upon Me have never to beg at the doorstep of anyone. All the mystic potencies automatically manifest in them. Even when the personified four Vedic goals of *dharma*, *artha*, *kāma*, *mokṣa* come knocking at their doors, My servitors turn down such offers. My devotees are fully protected by My Sudarśana disc at all times and even at the time of the total annihilation of this material universe they remain completely transcendental and unaffected.”

The Lord continued, “Even one who simply remembers My devotee, I take the responsibility for maintaining him. Surely, the servitor of My servitor is most dear to Me, and he certainly attains My shelter. My servitors need not have any concern about their maintenance since I take their responsibilities on My shoulders, I will personally provide. So Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita you just remain happily in your house and every requirement will automatically come to you. I am also blessing you and Śrī Advaita with the boon that your transcendental bodies will never be affected by old age and debility.”

The Lord then called for Rāmāi Paṇḍita and told him, “Listen, Rāmāi Paṇḍita, I instruct you to always serve your elder brother, as if he were the Supreme Lord. Know also that you are as dear to Me as My very life, so I want you never to deviate from this service to Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita.” Both Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and Rāmāi Paṇḍita were overwhelmed with divine bliss; the blessed Lord had filled their hearts with indescribable joy. By the causeless mercy of Śrī Caitanya, even today, the pastime of everything arriving at the doorstep of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita is still occurring.

The characteristics and qualities of Śrīla Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita are impossible to enumerate. Just by remembering him the three words become purified. Truly, while the Lord stayed in his home, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura served Śrī Gaurasundara in every possible way to the Lord’s fullest satisfaction. Bathed in the affection of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita’s family members, the Lord even extended His sojourn for a few days more on the request of His dearmost servitor. The presence of the Lord transported the entire household upon continuous waves of exhilaration.

From there, the Lord went to Pānihāṭi to visit the house of Śrī Rāghava Paṇḍita, who was always busy in serving Śrī Kṛṣṇa. When the Lord arrived, Śrī Rāghava Paṇḍita was overwhelmed to see his beloved Lord face to face and fell to the ground offering obeisances. Beginning to weep in jubilation, He clasped the Lord’s lotus feet, the very same lotus feet that are the source of Lakṣmī Devī’s constant joy. The Lord also was extremely happy to see His dear devotee, and so while bathing him in unrestrained tears of joy, He picked him up and embraced him. Śrī Rāghava Paṇḍita did not know what to do or how to receive the Lord such was his effusive bliss. The Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, Śrī Caitanya, was very pleased with the devotion of Śrīla Rāghava Paṇḍita, and showered His mercy upon him.

The Lord said, “By coming to Rāghava Paṇḍita’s house and seeing him, all My gloom has now been dispelled. Coming to his house has resulted in the same purification and satisfaction as bathing in the holy Gaṅgā.” Then smiling benignly at Śrīla Rāghava Paṇḍita, the Lord said to him, “Dear Rāghava Paṇḍita, please go immediately and prepare food for Lord Kṛṣṇa’s satisfaction.” Rāghava Paṇḍita immediately went off swimming in ecstasy to execute the Lord’s order. His heart inundated with divine love, he cooked a great plentiful variety of preparations, just as his heart dictated.

The Lord came to eat accompanied by Nityānanda Prabhu and all His associates. The Lord thoroughly relished Śrīla Rāghava Paṇḍita’s cooking and praised every preparation. The Lord spoke sweetly, “Rāghava Paṇḍita has cooked everything so excellently. Especially, never before have I ever tasted such a delectable preparation of *śāk*, spinach.” Rāghava Paṇḍita already knew that the Lord was very fond of *śāk*, so He had made it a point to prepare *śāk* in many delicious ways. The Lord, finishing His food, washed up and came back to sit down.

Meanwhile, the word had spread that the Lord was staying in the house of Śrīla Rāghava Paṇḍita. Śrī Gadādhara dāsa heard the news and came hastily to meet the Lord. Śrīla Gadādhara dāsa epitomized pure devotion to the Lord and was most near and dear to the Lord.

The Lord was extremely pleased to see Gadādhara dāsa and out of great love for him, He placed His lotus feet upon his head. Śrī Purandara Paṇḍita and Śrīla Parameśvarī dāsa, a highly acknowledged scholar, also came rushing to see the Lord. Parameśvarī dāsa was so surrendered to the Lord that the Lord had reciprocated and personally manifested Himself in his body. Both these saintly devotees were in great ecstasy to see the Lord, and they cried tears of divine love. Śrīla Raghunātha Vaidya, that very exalted Vaiṣṇava whose good qualities are endless, also came to meet the Lord. In this way, an endless stream of devotees came to see the Lord. Pānihāṭi village experienced an extraordinary spiritual event by the advent and stay there of the Lord. By His personal presence, the Lord inundated the whole village with divine ecstasy.

Once, the Lord called Śrīla Rāghava Paṇḍita aside and spoke to him alone. He said, “Rāghava, I want to reveal to you confidentially that Nityānanda Prabhu is non-different from Myself. You must understand that whatever Nityānanda wants of Me, I do. Without sophistry, I say that everything I do is through Nityānanda. We are one and the same. That which is rarely attained by great mystics steeped in meditation is easily obtained from Śrī Nityānanda. Therefore, engage yourself with sincerity and deference in the service of Śrī Nityānanda, knowing Him to be the Supreme Lord.” Before leaving the most fortunate village of Pānihāṭi, the Lord instructed Makaradhvaja, “Serve Rāghava Paṇḍita nicely. Know that the loving attachment you have for him is equivalent to that you have for Me, and has My highest appreciation.”

The Lord then came to a place called Varāha-nagara. There He visited the residence of an exalted and saintly *brāhmaṇa*. The *brāhmaṇa* was well versed in the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* and, upon having the audience of the Lord, he began to recite choice verses. As the Lord heard the verses from the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* read with such sublime devotion, He went into an ecstatic trance. With a voice resembling the roll of thunder, He cried out “Read on! Read on!” The pious *brāhmaṇa* was blissfully submerged in reading aloud the text and soon the Lord began to dance in divine exultation, oblivious to everything around Him. Verse after verse described the transcendental glory of loving devotional surrender, and the Lord swooned repeatedly falling like a rod to the ground with tremendous force. Such was the Lord’s spiritual ecstasy that the amazed people were afraid to see Him fall with such intensity. This pastime lasted late into the night. The *brāhmaṇa* read and the Lord danced.

Gradually, the Lord came out of His ecstatic trance and then calmly sat down. He was extremely happy with the *brāhmaṇa*, and so embraced him. The Lord said to him, “Never before have I heard anyone recite the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* so sweetly, therefore I name you ‘Bhāgavata Ācārya’, the spiritual preceptor of the *Bhāgavatam*. You need not engage in any other activity—just continue to recite the *Bhāgavatam*.”

Everyone was jubilant with the *brāhmaṇa’s* new and deserved title, and appreciated it with loud chanting of the Lord’s name. Blessing the residents of that place, the then Lord travelled along the banks of the Gaṅgā, visiting the different houses of many devotees. He satisfied all the devotees, fulfilling the yearning of their hearts to see Him. Finally, He returned to Nīlācala, Purī. One who hears these descriptions of the Lord’s return to Bengal becomes immediately free from all distress.

Great crowds of people greeted the Lord as He entered Jagannātha Purī with jubilant sounds saying, “The moving Lord Jagannātha has come back to Nīlācala.” With the speed of lightning, the news flashed everywhere.

Śrī Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and the other Oriyan associates of the Lord came running to see Him. Owing to feelings of separation, the devotees had been morose ever since the Lord had departed and now upon His return they were exultant and welcomed Him with loud joyous *kīrtana*. The Lord, the reservoir of divine love, embraced them and reciprocating their spiritual affections bathed everyone with His effusive tears. Once in Nīlācala, He began to reside in the house of Kāśī Miśra.

Now in Purī, the Lord spent all His time dancing in ecstasy and performing sweet, sublime *kīrtana* everywhere. Often He danced before Lord Jagannātha losing Himself in His ecstatic graceful movements. Sometimes, He danced within the closed precincts of Kāśī Miśra’s residence and at other times, He simply ran out to the ocean shores and danced to the rhythmic crashing of the waves upon the sand.

Blissfully oblivious of every other activity, the Lord now engaged in His wonderful pastimes. With the first blowing of the conchshell in the temple He was up early and as the doors to Lord Jagannātha opened He would be there bowing before the Lord. So wonderful was His love for Lord Jagannātha that tears cascaded from His eyes and flowed like the River Gaṅgā. All the people stared transfixed in amazement, their worries and sorrows long forgotten. Crowds followed Him wherever He went; all were deeply moved and inspired. Loudly, they chanted, “Hari!
