If anyone other than Lord Śiva tries to drink deadly poison, then he will surely die. The scriptures carry sufficient examples to substantiate this fact. In the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* 10.33.29-30: “No one should try to act in this manner, not even within the mind. Just as a person other than Lord Śiva who tries to drink the deadly poison that came out of the Milk Ocean will certainly die; similarly, if due to foolishness someone tries to imitate the pastimes of the Supreme Lord, then he will surely be destroyed. O King, fire is all-consuming, yet it remains unaffected and uncontaminated by any sin or dirt; similarly, a very powerful and potent personality should not be condemned for transgressing religious laws or even if he associates with a woman.’

“Therefore, O *brāhmaṇa*, if anyone criticizes Śrī Nityānanda’s activities, then he will have to suffer for this mistake with severe reactions, life after life. If a very elevated soul acts in a manner that appears offensive and he is ridiculed, nay even just criticized, then the critic is surely doomed.

“All these conclusions can be learnt from the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*, but only if a pure Vaiṣṇava explains the subject. Listen attentively to what the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* has to say about the person who laughed at and ridiculed a great personality. Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Balarāma stayed and studied in the house of Their *guru*, Sāndīpani Muni. After completing Their education They wished to return home, but first They inquired from Śrī Sāndīpani what They could offer as *guru-dakṣiṇā*, a donation to one’s teacher. The *guru* consulted his wife and replied that he and his wife would like to have their dead son brought back to life. Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Balarāma immediately went to see Yamarāja, the Lord of Death. On the request of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, all the formalities were concluded and the son was returned alive to Śrī Sāndīpani.

“When Mother Devakī heard about this wonderful happening, she also wanted her dead sons back. Therefore, one day she approached Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma and begged them saying, ‘O please listen to me, dearest Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. You are the Lords of all mystics. You are the original transcendental Lords of all creation, eternal and absolutely pure. You are the fathers of this universe and the cause of all causes. Creation, maintenance, and annihilation of this universe are carried out by just a partial expansion of Your expansions. Yet, in spite of these infinite potencies, You have both appeared in this world as my sons only to alleviate the suffering of this world.

“ ‘Just as You have brought back Your *guru’s* son from the abode of Yamarāja as a parting donation to Your *guru* and his wife; similarly, I also yearn to see all my six sons that the mean and heartless Kaṁsa mercilessly murdered. The *guru’s* son had been long dead and yet You brought him back to life by Your mystical potencies. Kindly satiate my thirst to see my sons and bring them back to life.’

“As soon as they heard their mother’s wish, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma immediately proceeded to Bali Mahārāja’s palace. When Bali Mahārāja saw that the visitors were his most worshipable Lordships, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, he felt a surge of spiritual bliss in his heart. He had surrendered all that he possessed, his wealth, wife and children, and himself at the lotus feet of their Lordships. The ecstasy of *kṛṣṇa-prema* was building up inside him and horripilation appeared all over his body as he began to shed tears of divine bliss. Bali fell at Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma’s feet and clutching them to his heart, he offered prayers.

“Bali Mahārāja prayed, ‘All glories to Śrī Ananta, who has appeared as Sankarṣaṇa, and all glory to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the crest jewel of Gokula. O Balarāma, Haladhara, You are the best friend and leader of all the young cowherd boys. O Kṛṣṇa you are the most precious treasure of Your surrendered devotees. O Lords, both of You are rarely to be seen even by great purified sages who are on the transcendental platform. Yet, my Lord, You are so magnanimous that You have appeared before me, a demon steeped in the darkest ignorance. Therefore, it is clear that, as described in the *Vedic* literature, You have no friends or enemies—this I am witnessing at this very moment. Pūtanā who came to murder You by making You suck her poisoned breast got liberation to the Vaikuṇṭha planets after being killed by You. Hence, it is difficult to understand Your heart. Even the *Vedas* and the great mystic *yogis* have failed to do so.

“ ‘Your illusory potency is so unfathomable that masters of mysticism fail to grapple with it. Then how can a sinful demon ever understand it? O Lord of the universe, my only prayer is that You do not cast me down to the dark well of material existence. I fall at Your lotus feet. Please just let me live under a tree and pass my days in peace. Kindly count me amongst Your servitors and give me their association, that I may never desire for anything else.’ Bali Mahārāja prayed in this manner at the lotus feet of Lords Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.

“Gaṅgā devī, the Bhagīratha, springing from the lotus feet of Śrī Nārāyaṇa purifies the abodes of Lord Śiva, Lord Brahmā, and so on as she flows through them. Now Bali Mahārāja and his family having washed the lotus feet of Their Lordships were now drinking and sprinkling over their heads that same sacred water of the Gaṅgā. Bali Mahārāja then worshiped Their Lordships offering Them incense, perfumed oils, flowers, camphor and ghee lamps, clothing and beautiful ornaments. He then prayed to the Lords, ‘O Lord, kindly instruct me if You consider me Your servant. Whoever follows Your instructions easily transcends all rules and regulations.’ Bali Mahārāja’s words pleased Their Lordships and They now attended to the business at hand.

“The Lord said, ‘Dear Sir Bali, please hear Our reason for coming here. The six sons of My mother were murdered by the wicked Kaṁsa; later, he was killed as a reaction to this grievous sin. Mother Devakī is greatly afflicted by this calamity and whenever she remembers her sons, she cries piteously. You have these six boys with you, so I have come to take them to please my mother. All six of them were the grandsons of Lord Brahmā, very exalted demigods and perfected beings. I will relate to you how they landed themselves in this distressful situation. One son of Lord Brahmā was Prajapati Marīci and these six souls were previously his sons.

“ ‘Once very surprisingly, Brahmā was struck by Cupid’s arrow. Blinded with lust, he chased his own daughter. These six grandsons of Brahmā—who were then just young boys—began to smirk and laugh upon seeing this scene; as a result, they fell down instantly from their godly positions. Having ridiculed a great personality, they had to take birth in the family of the vicious demon, Hiraṇyakaśipu, who had vowed to live by the sword and put everyone into subjugation. During the following fight between the demigods and the demons, Indra vanquished these six with his powerful thunderbolt weapon and they died after much torment. Yoga-māyā then arranged for them to be born one by one as the sons of Mother Devakī. In this next life, they also suffered greatly from the moment of birth. Even while mere infants, their own maternal uncle, Kaṁsa, murdered them. Mother Devakī, of course, is unaware of these hidden facts and she considers them her sons. I want to return them to my mother, Devakī, hence My presence here. When they drink the breast milk of Mother Devakī, they will be instantaneously acquitted of all their previous sins.

“ ‘Take heed, O Bali Mahārāja, the consequences of ridiculing a devotee of the Lord are very severe. Even perfected *yogis* suffer heavily if they disrespect a Vaiṣṇava, what to mention about lesser humans. An offender of Vaiṣṇavas has to pay a heavy price, life after life. I am delving into this subject for your benefit so you may learn from this and never insult a Vaiṣṇava. If a person worships Me and chants My name, but offends a Vaiṣṇava, he has to suffer severe setbacks in his devotional life. As for those who love and respect My devotees, I make Myself easily available to them.

“ ‘The *Varāha Purāṇa* states: “There may exist some doubt about success in attaining perfection by serving the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but there is no doubt whatsoever in achieving perfection by serving the pure devotees of the Supreme Lord.” Further, in the *Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya* 13.76 it is stated, “Those who only worship Śrī Govinda, Kṛṣṇa, but do not worship and serve the Lord’s devotees, are highly insolent. They never receive the Lord’s blessings.” Dear Bali, you are dear to Me and you are My servitor, hence I have revealed these esoteric meanings of the scriptures to you.’

“Bali Mahārāja felt divine exhilaration by hearing the instructions of the Lord. On the moment, He acted and immediately brought the six sons, offering them as gifts to the Lord. Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa thus escorted the six boys to Their mother, Devakī. Mother Devakī was overwhelmed with joy and love seeing her six dead sons actually before her. Out of affection, her breast milk flowed and she suckled the six sons. When these six boys sucked the breast milk of Devakī, they were in fact taking the remnants of the Supreme Lord. This gave them instant realization of the Truth. Offering obeisances to the Supreme Lord and everyone else, they fell flat on the ground like sticks.

“The Lord looked kindly upon them and started instructing them. He said, ‘Now you may return to the heavenly abodes of the demigods, your actual residence, but remember never to ridicule or laugh at a great spiritual personality again. Lord Brahmā is an expansion of the Supreme Lord, therefore he is to receive respect equal to that of the Supreme Lord. He is not to be condemned even if found apparently doing wrong. You have already suffered severe consequences by deriding him, so in the future beware of further mistakes. Now you must go and beg forgiveness from Lord Brahmā, then only will you feel cleansed and blissful.’

“So my dear *brāhmaṇa*, I have related to you these topics from the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* so that you may give up your suspicions about Śrī Nityānanda, who is of the highest transcendence. Persons with little knowledge and piety cannot comprehend His position. Yet, if any person becomes just slightly attracted to Him because of the miracles He performs from time to time, then surely that soul will attain liberation. Nityānanda has advented only to liberate the fallen conditioned souls, and actually, they will be liberated only by His causeless mercy.

“Nityānanda’s behaviour is beyond the jurisdiction of any rules and regulations. Who has the capacity to understand His mind? Without properly gauging His extraordinary and supra-mundane character, if anyone should criticize Śrī Nityānanda—even though such a faultfinder may be directly serving the Supreme Lord—undoubtedly that faultfinder will lose all his devotion. Therefore, you must immediately leave for Navadvīpa and make everyone there understand these esoteric facts about Śrī Nityānanda. If by any chance someone criticizes Him, then no one can save this faultfinder from his imminent doom. On the other hand, whosoever loves and respects Nityānanda will be true in his devotion to Me. This I confirm most strongly. If Śrī Nityānanda marries a Muslim girl or even enters a drinking house, still His lotus feet are most worshipable, even for Lord Brahmā.”

The potent words of Śrī Caitanya acted effectively in the heart of the *brāhmaṇa*. He became blissful and his faith and love for Śrī Nityānanda increased tremendously. The *brāhmaṇa* returned to Navadvīpa. Upon arrival, he went directly to meet Nityānanda and honestly admitted his offences before the Lord, who in turn heard him patiently and then graced him with His causeless mercy.

The character and activities of Śrī Nityānanda are the most confidential topics in the *Vedas*. They are inscrutable to human norms. He is the Supreme Mystic who is also known as the original Supreme Lord, Ananta, holding up the entire material creation upon but one of His thousands of hoods. His body is absolute and transcendental. Without the mercy of Śrī Caitanya, it is impossible to fully understand Śrī Nityānanda.

Different people know Nityānanda in different ways. Some say He is exactly like Balarāma. Others say He is the foremost and dearest of Śrī Caitanya’s devotees. Again, someone else says He is supremely potent, an expansion of the omnipotent Lord. Many persons honestly admit that they cannot fathom His character at all. In this manner, people freely air their opinions about the Lord. Whatever the people might say about Śrī Caitanya and Śrī Nityānanda, may the lotus feet of these two Lords be ever imprinted upon my heart. I pray at the feet of all devotees to invoke this blessing: Birth after birth, may I remain the servant of my eternal master, Śrī Nityānanda. This is my only desire.

After hearing all this about the boundless mercy of Śrī Nityānanda, if anyone is so degraded and sinful as to still criticize the Lord, then I firmly kick him on his head. Śrī Caitanya is the Lord of my Lord and Master, Śrī Nityānanda. This fact gives me great hope and strength. Will I ever be blessed to see my Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu sitting together upon a throne, surrounded by all Their servitor associates?

All glory to Śrī Caitanya. O Gaurāṅga, kindly bless me so that I may have the shelter of Śrī Nityānanda.

Along with this plea, I further pray that even after gaining the association of Śrī Nityānanda, I may never forget Your lotus feet.

Wherever You and Lord Nityānanda appear as incarnations, I pray to be eligible to be Your eternal servitor there.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu are my life and soul. I, Vṛndāvana dāsa, humbly offer this song at Their lotus feet

## 7: Pastimes with Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita

All glory to the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gauracandra, the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha! All glory to Śrī Nityānanda, the embodiment of devotional service! All glory to Śrī Gaurasundara, the beloved Lord of Śrī Advaita Ācārya and Śrīla Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura! He is the life and soul of Śrīla Gadādhara Paṇḍita and Śrī Jagadānanda. He is also the life and soul of Śrī Paramānanda Purī, the most precious treasure of Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara, the divine benefactor of Śrī Vakreśvara Paṇḍita, and the enchanter of Śrī Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi. He is the dear master of Śrī Govinda. O Lord, kindly shower Your merciful glance upon the conditioned souls.

Śrī Nityānanda roamed about in Navadvīpa with His associates performing continuous *kīrtana* and thus He was always submerged in the ocean of bliss and *prema-bhakti*. The *saṅkīrtana* group’s only devotional engagement was dancing and singing for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa. As in Gokula, Balarāma went with His friends from house to house bringing joy to all the residents; similarly, Nityānanda manifested the transcendental happiness of Gokula in Navadvīpa.

One day, the Supreme Lord, Nityānanda Prabhu, intensely desired to meet Śrī Gauracandra. Thus, He begged leave from Śacīmātā and proceeded towards Śrī Nīlācala Purī. By the divine arrangement of Śrī Caitanya, Nityānanda’s associates were constantly relishing the Holy Name, qualities, and pastimes of Śrī Caitanya and thus always experienced the greatest ecstasy. They exhibited spiritual symptoms like roaring, shouting, dancing, weeping, etc. Always singing the glories of the Lord the entire way from Navadvīpa, they arrived near Nīlācala Purī after a few days.

In Kamala-pura, Nityānanda upon seeing the palace entered into an ecstatic trance, shedding profuse tears of *prema* and constantly loudly calling out, “Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya! Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya! Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya!” The Lord sojourned in a flower garden for a few days. Who can know the mind of Nityānanda other than the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. Śrī Caitanya upon hearing about the arrival of Nityānanda, immediately left alone for Ekeśvara and found Him in the deep bliss of meditation. Gaurasundara began to recite beautiful verses in glorification of Nityānanda as He continuously circumambulated Nityānanda, who was still deeply steeped in meditation. Whosoever hears the verses that emanated from the transcendental mouth of Gauracandra will surely develop love and attachment for Nityānanda: “Let Śrī Nityānanda accept the hand of a Muslim woman in marriage, or enter a drinking den. His lotus feet remain worthy of the worship of Lord Brahmā.” Śrī Caitanya continuously chanted this verse and in a state of sheer ecstasy went around Śrī Nityānanda.

Nityānanda, coming out of His trance, instantly recognised the voice of Śrī Caitanya and with utmost respect He chanted out aloud, “Haribol!” and upon seeing the face of Gauracandra was instantly swept away on a wave of ecstasy that is impossible to describe. Roaring like a lion, Nityānanda constantly uttered, “Haribol! Haribol! Haribol!” and fell to the ground like a stick, paralysed by intense joy.

Both of the Lords were in divine bliss, circumambulating each other, offering *daṇḍavats* to each other, sometimes embracing each other, shedding cascading tears of love and jubilation, sometimes rolling on the ground roaring like lions. Their exchanges of love and affection were truly wonderful—very much like the exchanges between Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. Each took turns to recite verses glorifying the other whilst offered respects with folded palms. All the ecstatic symptoms, the transformations of pure *bhakti*, such as tears, shivering, horripilation, laughter, swooning, pallor, etc. were manifest upon their divine persons. These wonderful pastimes are all the arrangements of Śrī Caitanya. Only the fully surrendered servitors were fortunate to feast their eyes upon this most rare display of the highest ecstasy in *prema-bhakti*.

After a while, Caitanya began to eulogize Nityānanda with folded palms, “O Nityānanda! The Holy Name has manifested in your form. You are the shelter of all Vaiṣṇavas, and the Supreme Controller, Śrī Ananta. All the jewelleries that embellish Your divine limbs and form are the very incarnations of *bhakti-yoga*. For Your own pleasure, You have decorated Your body with gold, silver, pearls, diamond, and *rudrākṣa*, which represent each of the nine limbs of *bhakti*. Members of the lower castes, outcastes, reprobates and all the other wretched souls receive liberation by Your mercy alone. With the treasure of *bhakti* that is eagerly sought by the demigods, *yogis*, sages and elevated mystics, You have rewarded the mercantile traders and others.

“The *Vedas* declare that Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Godhead, is absolutely independent, yet You have the capacity to sell even Kṛṣṇa. Who can fully fathom Your unlimited potencies for You are the divine embodiment, the incarnation of *kṛṣṇa-rasa*. When You become inebriated with the nectar of *saṅkīrtana*, You are oblivious to the phenomenal world and no other words emanate from Your transcendental mouth except descriptions of the wonderful qualities of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Śrī Kṛṣṇa always resides in Your heart and Your body is His pleasure abode. Therefore, whoever loves and respects You will certainly never be pushed away by Śrī Kṛṣṇa.”

Thereafter, Nityānanda began to speak with great humility, “My Lord ! You, being the Supreme Lord, are glorifying Me out of Your love and affection just like a guardian for His ward and devotee; thus, You are *bhakta-vatsala*, the lover of Your devotee. You are free to act in anyway You deem fit, whether You choose to circumambulate, offer obeisances, beat and reprimand, or protect. Actually, who knows Your mind? What remains unknown or unseen to Your mystic vision? You are the Supreme Controller of the mind and life-air of everyone. You are the Supreme Master; I simply execute Your desires. First, You made Me accept the life of an ascetic mendicant and then You made Me give it up. You instigated Me to carry the cowherd’s cane, lasso, rod, flute, and horn; thereby, I have given up the renounced order.

“You have instructed Your most favoured devotees to take up a life of austerity and *bhakti-yoga*. Yet, by weaning me away from the renounced order that befits a sage, You have made Me look ludicrous in the eyes of common man. I am simply Your puppet dancing to Your tune. You are the Supreme Judge holding the balance—punishment and grace are in Your hands.”

Śrī Caitanya replied, “The jewellery that decorates Your body is indeed representative of the nine limbs of pure devotion; hearing, chanting, remembering, praying, worship, offering obeisances, becoming a servant, becoming a friend, and surrendering fully. In truth, the nine-fold path of pure *bhakti* eternally embellishes You. Yet, the serpent, which is the eternal embellishment of Lord Śiva, is not properly understood by all. According to Their transcendental relationship, Ananta Śeṣa is most dear to Lord Śiva. So, Śrī Ananta takes the from of a serpent and remains around the neck of Śiva. Without this knowledge, people criticize the character of Śiva and as a result must suffer dire consequences. Other than *bhakti-rasa*, I do not see anything else in Your personality. You are always steeped in the mood of Vṛndāvana relishing with Your body, mind, and words the nectar tasted by Nanda Mahārāja with the cowherd boys. Those fortunate souls who can see this with their inner vision will certainly see the beatific face of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

“The cane, flute, bullhorn, flower garland, *guñjā* necklace, perfumed oil, etc. have always been your embellishments. All Your young associates remind Me of Śrīdāmā, Sudāmā, and the other cowherd boys of Vṛndāvana, as We played together. In You, I see the spiritual mellows of Vṛndāvana, the same sights and colours. The same divine potency of Vraja is fully manifest in You in the form of *nanda-goṣṭhī-bhakti*, the ecstatic love, great brilliance, all power, and devotion felt by the associates of Nanda Mahārāja. Therefore, in truth anyone who loves and respects You and Your associates also loves Me.”

In this manner, lost in their individual transcendental emotions, Mukunda, who is Caitanya, and Ananta, who is Nityānanda, discussed at length topics that had no end and were too esoteric for the comprehension of anyone. Gradually, after becoming aware of their external surroundings their Lordships went to a solitary place in the garden guarded by trees. The topics they discussed are not to be found even in the *Vedas*. Whenever Caitanya and Nityānanda met, they were mostly left to themselves. The ecstatic pastimes they—who are both the embodiments of divine bliss—performed are unknown to anyone, for by the arrangement of Śrī Caitanya no one comes near them at these moments. Nityānanda knowing the mind of Śrī Caitanya never has anyone accompany Him when He meets the Lord in such solitude. Just as Śrī Caitanya never reveals His real identity to the world; similarly, Śrī Nityānanda also keeps His identity concealed.

The heart and mind of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are unfathomable. This truth is unanimously reiterated in the *Vedas* by Lord Śiva, Lord Brahmā, and even by Śrī Lakṣmī Devī, what to speak of others. All of them agree that they do not know or understand the inner thoughts of the Supreme Lord. Yet, this does not hinder their loving glorification.

However, the Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya, steeped in His spiritual emotions, repeats the secrets of His mind to many, not just to one person. Those who have thus heard from the Lord joyfully think in the following manner, “He does not love anyone more than He loves me, for He reveals only to me the most esoteric and secret topics. He exhorts me to ecstatically serve Kṛṣṇa, giving up the path of dry renunciation like a sage who lives frugally. He also reveals to me the reason why He also rejected the life of renunciation and took up the cowherder’s cane, flute, peacock feather, *guñjā* necklace, and short lasso.”

Another person realises thus, “Of all the different grades of devotional mood of surrender, the activities and services of the cowherd boys and damsels of Vṛndāvana are the topmost. Such devotion, which is eagerly sought after by even Śiva and Brahmā, is a result of great austerities and *bhajana*. Only those greatly fortunate souls who are recipients of the Lord’s highest mercy are rewarded with the devotional mood of Vraja Gokula. Even the highly elevated devotee, Śrī Uddhava, aspires for this mood of devotion, as we learn from the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* 10.47.63. wherein Uddhava prays:

“I repeatedly offer my respects to the dust from the feet of the women of Nanda Mahārāja’s cowherd village. When these *gopīs* loudly chant the glories of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the vibration purifies the three worlds.”

When a Vaiṣṇava devotee develops such a devotional attitude then he is then fully accepted by Śrī Gauracandra as one of His own. By the Lord’s arrangement, others are tested rigidly. Certainly, Gaurasundara enacts His pastimes in wonderful ways.

All the devotees who accompanied their Lordships were constantly floating upon the cloud of divine ecstasy. Sometimes, they even witnessed affectionate quarrels between Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and Śrī Gaurasundara. The unfortunate person who takes sides in these verbal fights and criticises either of their Lordships places himself in a precarious condition. All living entities, especially the devotees are the non-different parts and parcels of the Lord, just like His different limbs, fingers, and feet.

Thus, in the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* 4.7.53. Lord Kṛṣṇa declares: “A person with average intelligence does not think the head and other parts of the body to be separate. Similarly, My devotee does not differentiate Viṣṇu, the all-pervading Personality of Godhead, from any thing or any living entity.”

Unanimously, all the Vaiṣṇavas declare that Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya is the Lord of everyone and everything. By the Vaiṣṇavas, He is glorified as the Supreme Controller, Maintainer, Creator and Inscrutable One. When He descends to earth, in every incarnation, His divine compassion rewards the living entities with *bhakti*. Although He rewards the worthy with transcendental knowledge and spiritual potency, He never spares those who are offensive and evil.

For Gaurasundara, two personalities hold unique positions: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and Śrīla Advaita Ācārya. If both act in an uncommon and unpredictable manner even millions of times, Śrī Gauracandra will not comment. These are the mysterious ways of Gauracandra when dealing with His beloved brother Śrī Nityānanda Avadhūta.

Śrī Gauracandra finally returned to His home bidding farewell to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, who feeling great jubilation then proceeded to the temple to have *darśana* of Śrī Jagannātha. Those who hear the narration of Gaurasundara’s meeting with Nityānanda are liberated from all material attachments.

As soon as Nityānanda beheld the beautiful form of Jagannātha, He fell to the ground and began to roll in the dust in ecstasy. When He was falling like a stick hundreds rushed to him trying to prevent Him from dashing to the stony floor, but they could not hold Him. Beholding the beauty of Jagannātha, Baladeva, and Subhadrā Devī, Nityānanda wept tears in spiritual bliss. The temple priests immediately offered Him the ‘*prasādi’* flower garlands from all the Deities. They were so impressed with His divine presence that they repeatedly offered Him many flower garlands.

All the devotees of Jagannātha who were present there were awed by His presence and they also began to experience spiritual bliss by seeing Nityānanda’s state of ecstasy. Those of them who did not know Nityānanda, upon enquiry were informed that He was the brother of Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. Nityānanda, the most compassionate one, went around embracing the servitors of Śrī Jagannātha and drenching their bodies with tears of ecstasy. Thereafter, Śrī Nityānanda proceeded to meet Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita at his home.

The wonderful affection shared between Nityānanda and Gadādhara Paṇḍita can be described only by the Supreme Lord Himself. The home of Śrī Gadādhara was blessed by the presence of the Deity of Gopīnātha, which is so charming a form that it appears as though Vraja-kumāra, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself, is standing there. Śrī Caitanya had personally embraced this Deity form. If even an atheist or agnostic was to actually see the Deity, he would surely forget his mistaken views. Nityānanda seeing the exquisite form and posture of Gopīnātha spouted incessant tears of ecstasy from His eyes.

When Śrīla Gadādhara learnt about the Lord’s arrival, he immediately stood up from his reading of the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* and hurried to meet the Lord. They rushed and embraced firmly, as tears flowed incessantly. They then offered obeisances to each other as they profusely eulogised each other. They felt that their eyes were now purified upon seeing each other and their lives had now found their real meaning and purpose. They lost touch with their own bodies and external surroundings as they floated on the ocean of spiritual happiness. The devotees who were present to witness this wonderful event were greatly moved by spiritual sentiments and experienced divine bliss. No one before had ever witnessed such expressions of love and affection. Nityānanda and Gadādhara were so close that neither could tolerate anyone speaking ill about the other. In fact, Śrī Gadādhara had taken a vow not to see the face of anyone who criticised Nityānanda and to reject the association of anyone who disliked Nityānanda. Once they calmed themselves, they sat down and performed *saṅkīrtana*.

Śrīla Gadādhara Paṇḍita begged Śrī Nityānanda to accept noon *prasādam*. Unknown to Śrīla Gadādhara, the Lord had brought with Him from Bengal a large amount of rice paddy for offering to Gopīnātha. The rice was of a very superior quality. He also had brought colourful and exquisite cloth material. He brought these two items and gave them to Śrīla Gadādhara, saying, “This rice is for offering to Śrī Gopīnātha.” When Śrī Gadādhara saw the quality of the rice, he said, “I have never set eyes on such a fine quality of rice. My Lord, did you bring this rice so caringly all the way from Vaikuṇṭha for Gopīnātha? Śrī Lakṣmī Devī alone is eligible to cook this rice, which is to be offered first to Śrī Kṛṣṇa and then to His devotees for them to honour His *prasādam*.”

Thus praising the high quality of the rice, Śrī Gadādhara took it along with the beautiful cloth for presentation to Śrī Gopīnātha. He draped the cloth around the Deity and feasted his eyes upon the combined beauty of the cloth and Gopīnātha. Feeling great ecstasy, Śrī Gadādhara went about arranging for the noon offering of Gopīnātha. He collected varieties of spinach growing wild in the garden and picked the tender leaves from a tamarind sapling, from which he made a paste by adding salt to prepare chutney. The pious and fortunate Śrī Gadādhara cooked rice and other simple and delicious preparations. He arranged the offering plate and brought it before Gopīnātha. Just at that instant, Gauracandra appeared with a beaming face, chanting the *Mahā-mantra*. He softly called out Gadādhara’s name, who was then overwhelmed with spiritual emotion and began to offer prayers to the Lord with great respect.

Smiling benignly, Gauracandra said, “My dear Gadādhara, am I not invited to the feast? I am not a stranger to you, or Nityānanda. If you refuse me, then I will take the *prasādam* by force. I certainly will not pass up this rare opportunity to take *prasādam*, which has been brought by Nityānanda, cooked by you, and offered to Gopīnātha. Both Nityānanda and Gadādhara were ecstatic. Gadādhara brought a plate of *prasādam* and placed it before Gauracandra and the aroma from the rice spread all over the temple premises and garden. Gauracandra repeatedly praised the rice and instructed Gadādhara to divide the rice into three equal portions, as He desired to honour *prasādam* with His Nityānanda and Gadādhara. When they also sat down, Gaurasundara began to glorify the cooking, saying, “The aroma from this rice is sure to reward anyone with *bhakti*. What an expert cook you are—I have never had such a delectable spinach preparation. You are the best of cooks and have made a unique item with tamarind leaves, which requires great skill. Now, I am sure that you are also cooking in Vaikuṇṭha. Now that this secret is out, is there any need for you to hide this truth any longer?”

This jocular mood prevailed all the while as the Prabhus took *prasādam*. They were the most intimate group who were bound to each other by an unbreakable bond of love. Each knew the intensity of the other’s love and they relished *prema-rasa* along with the *prasādam* of Gopīnātha. The matters spoken by Gauracandra in this company were never mentioned before anyone else. After they had finished *prasādam* and left, all the devotees who were waiting anxiously joyfully pounced on the divine remnants of the *prasādam*. Anyone who hears or reads this pastime of taking *prasādam* will undoubtedly develop *kṛṣṇa-bhakti* and attain the lotus feet of the Lord.

Anyone fortunate enough to be blessed by the merciful glance of Śrī Gadādhara can actually know the real divine identity of Śrī Nityānanda. Similarly, one who is dedicated to Nityānanda knows Śrī Gadādhara in truth. Thus, Nityānanda spent His days in Nīlācala with Gauracandra in the greatest jubilation. Gaurasundara, Nityānanda, and Gadādhara were always together. They went for *darśana* of Jagannātha together, performed *saṅkīrtana* together and so on, relishing the ecstasy of *prema* in each other’s divine association.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu are my life and soul. I, Vṛndāvana dāsa, offer this song at their lotus-feet.

## 8: The Narendra Sarovara Water Pastimes

All glory, all glory to Supreme Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glory, all glory to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, whose appearance has purified all the three worlds! All victory to Śrī Gaurāṅga and His followers! Anyone can develop *bhakti* simply by hearing the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya. Now hear about the arrival in Nīlācala of all the Vaiṣṇavas led by Śrī Advaita Ācārya.

As Ratha-yatra, the chariot festival of Jagannātha, drew nearer, many great Vaiṣṇavas began pouring into Śrī Purī-dhāma. Śrī Caitanya had instructed His followers to come every year for the Ratha festival. Therefore, this year led by Śrī Advaita Ācārya, all the Vaiṣṇavas from Bengal arrived. Some of the notable Vaiṣṇavas who came were: Śrīla Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, in whose home Śrī Caitanya performed *kīrtana*; Śrī Candraśekhara Ācārya, in whose house the Lord danced in the mood of Lakṣmī Devī; Śrī Gaṅgādāsa Paṇḍita, simply remembering him destroys all karmic reactions; Śrī Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi was jubilant as he entered Nīlācala, Śrī Caitanya weeps in joy just thinking about him; the expert performer of *kīrtana* and dance, Śrī Vakreśvara Paṇḍita was in the group, the Lord always danced to his ecstatic *kīrtana*; the great soul Śrī Pradyumna Brahmacārī also came, Lord Nṛsiṁha conversed with him often; Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura was in ecstasy as he arrived in Nīlācala; and the other Śrī Haridāsa, who lived on the seashore also came.

Śrī Vāsudeva Datta, who by the Lord’s desire is able to purchase Kṛṣṇa, also came. Śrī Caitanya’s personal singer, Śrī Mukunda Datta, and Śrī Śivānanda Sena along with his family and friends joined the merry band of pilgrims. Śrīla Govindānanda was immersed in bliss the entire way; he is capable of purifying all directions. Śrīla Govinda Datta, the main singer in the Lord’s party, was jubilant. The writer Śrī Vijaya dāsa was there; the Lord had manifested His bejewelled arm to him. Śrī Sadāśiva Paṇḍita, who was always in the purest of consciousness as he was now upon arriving in Purī; Nityānanda had stayed a long time in his home. Śrī Puruṣottama Sañjaya was happy to be in Nīlācala; as a mere child, he was blessed by Śrī Caitanya and was one of His main students. Śrī Śrīmān Paṇḍita chanted all the way; he would carry the burning torch while Śrī Caitanya danced.

Śrīla Nandana Ācārya also came feeling great ecstasy; His home was the first place Śrī Nityānanda had visited upon His arrival in Navadvīpa. Śrī Śuklāmbara Brahmacārī was in bliss; Śrī Caitanya had begged for *prasādam* from him. The perfectly renounced devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrīla Śrīdhara was most happy to be there; Viśvambhara had drunk water from his broken pot. In addition, there was Śrī Bhagavān Paṇḍita, in whose body Śrī Kṛṣṇa had appeared. Two other personalities who directly resembled Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Gopīnātha Paṇḍita and Śrī Śrīgarbha Paṇḍita, were in the group of pilgrims. Accompanying them was Śrī Vanamālī Paṇḍita who had had the divine vision of a golden plough and pestle. Two great devotees of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Jagadīśa Paṇḍita and Śrī Hiraṇya Bhagavat were thoroughly relishing *kṛṣṇa-rasa* on this pilgrimage; the Lord in his childhood pastimes had called for Ekādaśi *prasādam* from their home. Śrī Buddhimanta Khān was a respected person; he lived only to execute Śrī Caitanya’s orders. The person, whom Śrī Caitanya affectionately called ‘father’, Śrī Purandara Ācārya, was also there.

The noble and detached devotee, Śrī Rāghava Paṇḍita, in whose home the Lord stayed secretly, was happily entering Nīlācala. Doctor of the soul, Śrī Murāri Gupta, in whom Śrī Caitanya secretly resides, was there. Śrī Garuḍa Paṇḍita who was unaffected by a poisonous snakebite by continuously chanting ‘Harināma’ was there. Śrī Gopīnātha Siṁha, whom Lord Caitanya called Akrūra, also came. Two other beloved devotees of the Lord, Śrī Rāma Paṇḍita and Śrī Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍita, were in the group. Śrī Dāmodara Paṇḍita went to pay his respects to Śrī Śacīmātā before he undertook this journey. The Vaiṣṇava followers of Śrī Caitanya are innumerable and surely, it is impossible to know all their names. Without exception, all of them were feeling great jubilation as they neared Śrī Nīlācala Purī.

Before starting the pilgrimage, Śrīla Advaita Ācārya had first taken the *darśana* of Śacīmātā. After offering his humble respects, he proceeded to Nīlācala with a large group of devotees and family members. He carried with him a lot of foodstuffs and useful articles favoured by Śrī Caitanya, which he knew about from his previous visits to Purī. The entire way he led his group in loud ecstatic *kīrtana*, purifying the whole atmosphere of the land. In fact, their loud jubilant chanting sanctified the entire Three Worlds. Śrī Advaita was accompanied by his wife, sons, servants, and maidservants, who were eagerly desirous of seeing Śrī Jagannātha and again meeting Śrī Caitanya. Along the way, wherever they halted and sojourned, that place was transformed into Vaikuṇṭha.

Only Śrī Ananta Śeṣa could possibly attempt to narrate the wonderful and auspicious activities of the devotees on this pilgrimage. Countless devotees in small and large groups streamed toward Nīlācala. When they would reach Kamala-pura, from where the temple-spires and flag of Lord Jagannātha would be visible, the devotees, overwhelmed with joy, would offer obeisances and weep in bliss.

When Śrī Caitanya realized the devotees were arriving, He felt a strong urge to go and meet them even before they came into Purī. When news of the impending arrival of Śrī Advaita Ācārya reached the Lord, He immediately sent *mahā-prasādam* to greet that party at Kaṭaka. The divine love of Śrī Caitanya and Śrī Advaita for each other is extremely wonderful and boundless. The Lord would be heard often saying, “I was in My mystic sleep upon the Ocean of Milk when I was woken up by the loud calling of Nāḍā, Śrī Advaita. My present incarnation is due mainly to him.” For this reason, all the *mahāntas*, the exalted spiritual preceptors, greatly respected Śrī Advaita Ācārya.

So when the news reached Mahāprabhu that Śrī Advaita and his party were nearing Nīlācala, He instantly set out with His beloved devotees to greet them. Accompanying the Lord were Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Śrī Purī Gosvāmī, Śrīla Sārvabhauma, Śrī Jagadānanda Paṇḍita, Śrī Kāśī Miśra, Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara, Śrī Śaṅkara Paṇḍita, Śrī Kāśīśvara Paṇḍita, Śrī Bhagavān Ācārya, Śrī Pradyumna Miśra, Śrī Paramānanda Pātra, Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya, the servant of Mahāprabhu Śrī Govinda, Śrī Brahmānanda Bhāratī, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Raghunātha Vaidya, Śrī Śivānanda Sena, Śrī Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍita; the eldest son of Śrī Advaita, Śrī Acyutānanda; Śrī Vāṇīnātha, Śrī Śikhi Māhāti, and an endless number of the servitors of Śrī Caitanya. Everyone, big or small, was floating upon the waves of ecstasy, oblivious of the external world, as they accompanied Śrī Caitanya.

Śrī Advaita Ācārya’s party met Śrī Caitanya’s party at Aṭhāranālā. As soon as Śrī Caitanya had crossed the Narendra Sarovara, He saw Advaita’s approaching party at a distance. The Vaiṣṇavas of both parties fell to the ground and offered obeisances. The Lord, upon seeing Śrī Advaita, could not check the tears that welled up and cascaded to the ground. He fell flat upon the earth. Śrī Advaita beheld the Lord of his heart from a distance and offered repeated prostrations. Ecstatic symptoms like profuse weeping, shivering, pallor, swooning, horripilation, and roaring, etc. were manifest in the Vaiṣṇavas as they repeatedly offered prostrated obeisances. All of them were fully immersed in the ocean of *caitanya-rasa* and without exception all chanted the Holy Name and offered obeisances. Just like everyone else, the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurasundara, Śrī Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita were also repeatedly offering prostrations. The sky reverberated with their ecstatic chanting and joyous weeping. It is not humanly possible to describe this extraordinary scene. Only Śrīla Vedavyāsa and Śrī Ananta-śeṣa are able to narrate this event in detail.

Śrī Caitanya rushed to Śrī Advaita and clasped him in a tight embrace as tears of joy drenched his body. Śrī Advaita continuously uttered verses glorifying the Lord, beaming with happiness. He forgot all about the articles and foodstuffs he and his party had carried with them. Rumbling like a thunder, he simply repeated, “I’ve brought! I’ve brought!” The devotees began to loudly chant the Holy Name, which then echoed in all directions. What to speak of the Vaiṣṇavas even others who had come just to see what was happening became so inspired that they also loudly chanted, ”Hari! Hari!” and wept in unrestrained joy. The Vaiṣṇavas were embracing each other as they wept and chanted. Each Vaiṣṇava offered obeisances to Śrī Advaita, knowing that he was the cause of Śrī Caitanya’s advent. Meanwhile, the whole assembly of Vaiṣṇavas was engaged in a mammoth *saṅkīrtana*. Devotees were singing and dancing everywhere. Some devotees were rolling on the dust unable to check their ecstatic feelings. Śrī Caitanya entered the midst of everyone and joined in the exultant dancing.

Nityānanda and Advaita were locked in a long affectionate embrace. Soon, they also began to dance like intoxicated lions. Śrī Caitanya then went around embracing the Vaiṣṇavas in great jubilation. Śrī Gaurasundara, the Lord and Master of the devotees, the captive of his devotees, the life and soul of His devotees, was now crying like a child hanging on to his devotees with his arms around their necks. Just then, by the arrangement of Lord Jagannātha, hundreds of *prasādi* flower garlands and much sandalwood paste were brought to Śrī Caitanya. Śrī Gaurasundara was overwhelmed and He offered the first garland to Śrī Advaita Prabhu, placing it around His neck. He then went around personally garlanding all the Vaiṣṇavas and personally smearing Lord Jagannātha’s sandalwood paste on the different parts of the devotees’ upper torso.

The devotees were so moved by the compassion and humility of Śrī Gaurahari that they raised their hands and began to loudly chant the Lord’s Holy Name whilst weeping in joy. They avidly begged falling at Śrī Caitanya’s lotus-feet, praying, “O Lord, the only boon we ask of you is that we may never forget your lotus feet life after life, whether we are born as human beings, animals or even birds.” Meanwhile, the lady Vaiṣṇavas observed the ecstatic event from a distance and wept in bliss. Incessant tears of *prema* flowed freely for they were all embodiments of the *vaiṣṇavi-bhakti* devotional potency of the Lord. Śrī Caitanya Himself has commented that in the matters of spiritual knowledge and *bhakti-yoga*, the lady Vaiṣṇavis are equal to their husbands.

Still dancing and performing *saṅkīrtana*, the Vaiṣṇavas followed Śrī Caitanya as He led them into the city. Whosoever saw them was spontaneously attracted and experienced joy under the influence of the *prema-bhakti* that exuded from each Vaiṣṇava. They had walked but a short distance from Aṭhāranālā when they reached Narendra Sarovara. Right at that moment, the festive procession carrying Śrī Madana-Mohana arrived at the Narendra Sarovara Lake on the occasion of the Candana-yātrā of Jagannātha and Baladeva. Amidst loud chanting, the blowing of conch shells, the rhythmic beat of *mṛdaṅga* drums, the clanging of cymbals, and the high-pitched sounds of reed instruments, the procession halted on the banks of the lake. Hundreds of colourful festoons and flags were flapping in the wind. Many priests were fanning the Deity of Lord Madana-mohana with *cāmara* and peacock fans. The only audible sound was the combination of many instruments and loud voices all reaching a crescendo as the party of Śrī Madana-Mohana mingled with the *saṅkīrtana* party of Śrī Gaurasundara. Now the *saṅkīrtana* party swelled in ranks as everyone joined in the jubilant chanting. The excitement and ecstasy were palpable, as if the bliss had been personally transported from Vaikuṇṭha. All this was taking place simply by the transcendental arrangement of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

Śrī Madana-Mohana, which is the festival Deity of Jagannātha, and Śrī Baladeva, were placed on the boat as the devotees fanned Them with *cāmaras*. The Supreme Personality, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, was greatly satisfied to observe the boating pastimes of Śrī Madana-mohana and Śrī Baladeva. The Lord, with His many devotees then dived into the Narendra Lake. Now listen attentively how the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Gaurasundara, sported in the water of Narendra Sarovara. Just as in His previous incarnation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord as a child had sported in the waters of the River Yamunā with His young friends by holding hands and forming circles; similarly, He now sported with all the Vaiṣṇavas holding hands and forming circles in the Narendra Sarovara.

In Bengal, people play a certain game in the water known as ‘kāya’ and this was the first game the Vaiṣṇavas played. They called out, ‘kāya!’ ‘kāya!’ whilst clapping their hands upon the water surface; this sounds like a musical instrument. The Vaiṣṇavas were overcome with the spiritual mood of the young cowherd boys of Gokula and the Lord was their master, the Prince of Gokula, Gopāla.

All the Vaiṣṇavas were experiencing great ecstasy and they became oblivious of the external world. Without fear and inhibition, they began to splash water upon the Supreme Lord. Then a water-battle between the Lord and Śrī Advaita took centre stage. Each splashed water into the face of the other with great force. Sometimes, the Lord seemed to be getting the better of His opponent, at other times Śrī Advaita appeared to hold the upper hand. Soon the battle spread! Śrī Nityānanda, Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, and Śrī Purī Gosvāmī; this threesome was locked in a fearsome exchange of water splashing. Śrīla Mukunda Datta duelled with Śrī Murāri Gupta, both roaring like lions in jubilation. The two intimate friends, Śrī Paṇḍita Vidyānidhi and Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara laughed and splashed water at each other rather more sedately than the others. Śrīla Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, Śrī Rāma Paṇḍita, Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Śrī Vakreśvara Paṇḍita, Śrī Gaṅgādāsa Paṇḍita, Śrī Gopīnātha Ācārya, Śrī Candraśekhara Ācārya and so on, all intoxicated with *caitanya-rasa* soon joined in.

Hundreds of thousands of people celebrated the joy ride of Śrī Mādana-mohana and Śrī Baladeva upon His boat and entered the water in great jubilation. The householders, *sannyāsīs*, and *brahmacārīs* all mingled together, enjoying the water sports in the Narendra Sarovara. However, such was the influence of *māyā*, the deluding potency of the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, that unqualified persons were not allowed to enter the circle of Vaiṣṇavas, nor could they see the Vaiṣṇavas’ transcendental activities.

Those with insufficient piety and good fortune are ineligible to enter the company of the followers of Śrī Caitanya. The Lord is only captivated by unalloyed devotion and without *bhakti*, nothing of any value is achieved. Material education, learning, penances, and austerity, etc. inevitably lead only to more suffering. The Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, performed His *saṅkīrtana* pastimes with the greatest divine pleasure openly before the eyes of everyone in Nīlācala, but not all could realize their transcendental nature.

Many *sannyāsīs* respected as ‘*mahājanas’*, great souls, had not the good fortune to recognize the Lord. Some *māyāvādī sannyāsīs* and so-called renunciants criticized the Lord saying, “What is this Caitanya doing, leaving aside *Vedic* study and simply wasting time making clamorous *kīrtana*. He should rather follow the *sannyāsī* discipline of *prāṇāyāma*, etc. Instead, He is dancing, crying, etc.” The more elevated of these *sannyāsīs* said, “Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya is a great soul!” “He is very erudite and knowledgeable.” “Without doubt an exalted devotee!” and other similar praises. Yet, they praised Him without truly understanding His actual position. Undisturbed, the Supreme Lord continued His water pastimes.

In the past, in His previous incarnations, the Supreme Lord had performed water sports with His associates in the River Yamunā and Jāhnavī Gaṅgā, thus rewarding those rivers with great mercy. Now was the turn of the Narendra Sarovara to receive the same unlimited mercy. The merciful Supreme Personality performed innumerable similar transcendental pastimes for the liberation of the conditioned souls. Hearing and narrating these pastimes frees one from the shackles of fruitive reactions.

Śrī Gaurasundara gathered all the Vaiṣṇavas together after the water sports and proceeded to take *darśana* of Lord Jagannātha in His temple. Śrī Gaurasundara and the devotees began to shed unrestrained tears of joy as they took *darśana* of Lord Jagannātha and the newly arrived Śrīla Advaita and his party were beside themselves with spiritual exhilaration. The devotees offered prostrated obeisances to the ‘motionless Jagannātha’ in His Deity form on one side and to the ‘moving Jagannātha’, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, on the other side. Śrī Kāśī Miśra then brought the *prasādi* flower garlands of Lord Jagannātha and gave them to Śrī Gaurasundara who received them with the utmost devotion and respect. He did this to instruct and teach everyone by His own example, being the Supreme Lord who was now, by His *līlā*, in the renounced order. He alone truly knows the spiritual significance of the Vaiṣṇavas, Tulasī, the Gaṅgā, and the objects that are *prasādam*, and the need to respect these items with total devotion. He showed everyone the unique spiritual position of the Vaiṣṇavas by directly offering them His prostrated obeisances even though He was in the most highly respected position of *sannyāsa*, the renounced order.

The religious order of *sannyāsa* is the most elevated in human society. In fact, the father of a *sannyāsī* son must offer respects to his own son. Being in the highest order, generally a *sannyāsī* will offer obeisances to only another *sannyāsī*. This is the *Vedic* etiquette. However, in order to teach the world the exalted position of the Vaiṣṇavas, the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, in His incarnation as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, embraced the renounced order of *sannyāsa* and offered respectful obeisances to the Vaiṣṇavas. Thus, the Lord fulfilled His role as the original *śikṣā-guru*, instructing spiritual master, by His personal example.

Now hear attentively how the Lord showed respect to Tulasī devī in His divine pastimes. Once, the Lord filled a small pot with earth and appeared to see Tulasī in that pot, saying, “I feel despondent, like a fish out of water, if I do not see Tulasī.” When He chanted upon beads His prescribed rounds while walking, someone would carry the Tulasī pot in front while He walked behind so that He would have continual *darśana* of Tulasī. Tears of ecstasy cascaded down His cheeks and when He sat down to chant the Tulasī pot would be placed right next to Him. All through His chanting of prescribed rounds, He would have *darśana* of Tulasī. Who can understand the pastimes of the Supreme Lord in His mood and performance of *bhakti-yoga*? When He had finished His prescribed chanting, He would have Tulasī carried ahead of Him. Those sincere souls who take to heart the guidance of the Supreme Lord, as the supreme instructing spiritual master, will always be protected under all circumstances.

After offering obeisances to Lord Jagannātha, Śrī Gaurahari and the devotees returned to their residences. The Lord fulfilled the desires of all His devotees; He took care of them like a father to the son and the devotees stayed by the Lord’s side at all times. All the devotees from Bengal and Nīlācala did not want to leave the Lord’s association, having experienced in His company the highest level of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. By the mercy of the Lord, everyone could see the Vaiṣṇavas from the spiritual world of Svetadvīpa. Śrī Advaita repeatedly commented, “These exalted Vaiṣṇavas cannot be seen even by the demigods, but by Your mercy we are so fortunate to see them.” Then weeping in gratitude, Advaita would fall at the lotus feet of the Lord.

Certainly, these Vaiṣṇavas are incarnations from the spiritual world, who by the arrangement of the Lord descended upon this earth before His appearance. Saṅkarṣaṇa, Aniruddha, and Pradyumna incarnated as Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, and Śatrughna to assist the Lord in His earthly pastimes as Lord Rāma; similarly, by the order of the Lord, these Vaiṣṇavas have incarnated from the spiritual world to assist Lord Caitanya. Thus, they are not subject to the cycle of birth and death like ordinary mortals. They incarnate with the Lord and then disappear when the Lord withdraws His earthly pastimes. The *Padma Purāṇa Uttara-khaṇḍa* 257.57/58. confirms that they are transcendental to the rules of religiosity and the laws of *karma*:

“Just as Sumitra’s son, Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa, Saṅkarṣaṇa, and other forms of the Supreme Godhead incarnate upon the earth by their own sweet, independent will; similarly, the eternal associates of the Lord, the Vaiṣṇavas, incarnate upon earth with the Lord. When the Supreme Lord returns to His supreme eternal abode, the Vaiṣṇavas, their duties completed, also return. Certainly, the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu and His eternal associates, the Vaiṣṇavas, are not subject to birth, death, old age, and disease due to *karmic* reaction.”

In the Lords association, the devotees always experienced the ecstasy of *kṛṣṇa-prema*. Those pious souls who hear these narrations with devotion are fully ensured of obtaining the association of the Lord and His devotees.

I, Vṛndāvana dāsa, offer this song at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Śrī Nityānanda, who are my heart and soul.

## 9: The Glories of Śrī Advaita Ācārya

All glory, all glory to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the beloved husband of the Goddess of Fortune, Śrī Rāma Devī, and the prime object of the devotion and love of the Vaiṣṇavas! All victory, all victory to the Lord and Master of Vaikuṇṭha, the most munificent personality! Kindly cast you merciful glance upon the living entities.

The devotees eagerly took advantage of the Lord’s association and enjoyed every moment in the bliss of *saṅkīrtana*. When coming from Bengal, the devotees brought a variety of foods that they knew were the favourites of the Lord. They had seen the Lord as a youngster in Navadvīpa and so were well acquainted with the Lord’s likes and dislikes. Now in Nīlācala, each group of Vaiṣṇavas prepared the Lord’s favourite dishes and invited Him to eat. The Lord was extremely satisfied with this arrangement of taking *prasādam* in different Vaiṣṇava homes every day and thus enjoyed his favourite preparations. The Vaiṣṇavis, the wives of exalted Vaiṣṇavas, were expert cooks being partial expansions of Śrīmatī Lakṣmī Devī, the wife of Śrī Nārāyaṇa and the variety of preparations they made was astounding. All Vaiṣṇavas and Vaiṣṇavis were steeped in the ecstasy of chanting the Holy Name and serving the Lord. They wept tears of joy continuously. They cooked His favourite foods and the Lord ate with great exhilaration. This is the transcendental way of *prema-bhakti*—the devotees blissfully serving the Lord and the Lord receiving the service of His beloved devotees with immense pleasure.

One day, Śrīla Advaita Ācārya approached the Lord and said, “My dear Lord, kindly come to my house and take *prasādam*. Whatever little I cook, if you come I will be blessed by your presence.” Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya replied, “Anyone who eats your cooking is instantly rewarded with *kṛṣṇa-bhakti* and thus he is sure to attain Śrī Kṛṣṇa. My dear Ācārya, your cooking gives Me life, because Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself accepts your offerings of food. I would never hesitate to beg *prasādam* cooked by you.” Śrī Advaita was heaved to such heights of ecstasy hearing these affectionate words from the Lord that he was at a loss for words. Bubbling with joy, Śrī Advaita ran to his home and busied himself with his wife to prepare for the Lord’s cooking. His wife is the partial expansion and incarnation of Śrīmatī Lakṣmī Devī. Totally dedicated to her husband, she dived into the nectarine ocean of devotional service.

All the different foodstuffs, which were the Lord’s favourites, she had diligently packed in Navadvīpa. Now she unpacked them and gave them all to her husband. Śrī Advaita Ācārya sat down to cook enthroning Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya in his heart and mind. Advaita’s wife Śrī Sītādevī supplied all the vegetables and spices and looked after all the other pre-cooking arrangements while her husband began to cook. She knew the Lord relished *śāk*, spinach, so she handed ten varieties of spinach to her husband. Both were immersed in an ocean of bliss preparing the *prasādam* for the Lord.

Śrī Advaita said to his wife, “O mother of Kṛṣṇa dāsa, Sītādevī, we must make sure the Lord tastes each and every course we prepare. If He is accompanied by other *sannyāsīs* and *mahāntas*, then I know He will not take from every preparation. We expect that these *sannyāsīs* will sit down to eat with the Lord. They always wait and eat with the Lord, because they relish the Lord’s association so much.” Śrīla Advaita then began to consider in his mind, “If a situation arises whereby the Lord comes alone, then I can feed Him a little from everything I have cooked. How can I make this happen?” While cooking, Śrī Advaita was thinking in this manner.

Meanwhile, the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurasundara, after completing the chanting of His specified number of rounds upon His beads decided to perform His daily noon rituals such as *gāyatrī-japa* and so on. The *sannyāsīs*, who usually honoured *prasādam* together with the Lord, also decided to complete their noon rituals and so went away. Suddenly, a powerful storm brewed up accompanied by torrential rains by the arrangement of Lord Indra, purely for the benefit of Śrī Advaita Ācārya. Clouds loomed in the sky and clouds of dust engulfed the houses below in darkness, raining down hail like pellets. People caught in the storm lost their way unable to see through the thickly flying dust. Miraculously, where Śrī Advaita was living, the rain and storm was mild and the Ācārya continued cooking. However, the *sannyāsīs* who had dispersed earlier for their noon duties were now completely lost and did not know how to find their way and meet up with one another.

Unperturbed, Śrī Advaita completed cooking a very elaborate feast—varieties of rice preparations, delicacies from seasonal vegetables, ghee, butter-cream, yoghurt, and endless mouth-watering sweets. On every preparation, he placed *tulasī-maṅjarīs* and sat down to make the offering, immediately entering deep meditation with the sole intent of attracting Śrī Gaurasundara to come alone. The Supreme Personality of Godhead is independent, and He decided to comply with Śrī Advaita’s wish. By Himself and chanting, “Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa,” Lord Caitanya appeared in person before Śrī Advaita. With great reverence, Śrī Advaita offered obeisances at the lotus feet of the Lord and then offered Him a mat upon which the Lord happily sat down.

When Śrī Advaita noticed that the Lord was unaccompanied by anyone, he was extremely pleased. Together with his wife, he began to wash the Lord’s lotus feet and then applied sandalwood paste to the Lord and after fanning Him for a while then requested Him to accept *prasādam*. The Lord then sat down to eat and Śrī Advaita personally served Him. The Ācārya served each preparation with the utmost care while floating high on clouds of bliss. The Lord relished every morsel of *prasādam*, but made sure to leave little remnants from every preparation on His plate. The Lord smilingly asked the Ācārya, “Do you know why I’m keeping these remnants? I want to know the way of preparation of each dish, so I am keeping a little of everything. Tell Me something Ācārya, where did you learn to cook so expertly? I have never eaten such wonderful spinach dishes in such variety!”

Whatever Śrī Advaita served, the Lord ate with utmost satisfaction. The Supreme Lord is like a wish-fulfilling desire tree, who joyfully satisfies the desires of his devotees. Advaita Ācārya served to his heart’s content and the Lord relished to His heart’s content. While the Lord took *prasādam*, Śrī Advaita offered grateful prayers to Lord Indra. He prayed, “O Lord Indra, today I have realized the extent of your power and potency. Today I have become convinced that you are a true Vaiṣṇava. From today onwards, I will offer you flowers and water, for you have purchased me.”

Overhearing Śrī Advaita praying, the Lord enquired, “You are suddenly offering prayers and praises to Lord Indra, what is the reason for this?” Śrī Advaita replied, “My Lord, you are eating. Kindly continue—You have no business hearing about this.” To this the Lord knowingly smiled, and said, “Why do you attempt to hide, Ācārya. This sudden unseasonable pulsating rainstorm, hail and gusty gale is all your doing, I know this for sure. I will tell you the real reason why you made Lord Indra unleash this inclement weather. You knew that if the *sannyāsīs* accompanied Me here to take *prasādam*, I would hardly eat anything. However, if I came alone then you could fulfil your heart’s desire and feed me as much as you like. Therefore, to hinder the *sannyāsīs* from coming, you have created this chaos. The fact that Indra carried out your orders does not display the true extent of your real, spiritual potency. It is truly Indra’s great fortune that he could serve you. For a person such as You, whose wishes even the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, readily fulfils, and who is able to make Śrī Kṛṣṇa personally appear on this Earth, and whose every request Śrī Kṛṣṇa readily carries out, for such a person surely it is mere child’s play to orchestrate a lashing rainstorm. Yamarāja, the Lord of Death and Time, is your order carrier, and great *yogis* and sages pray at your feet, and anyone can break the chain of material bondage simply by remembering you. Therefore, for you to arrange a little rain and storm is nothing. Nobody knows your real identity. By your mercy alone, can one develop pure devotion.”

Śrī Advaita Ācārya replied, “My Lord, you are a loving guardian to your servitors. This knowledge gives me all-round strength in my body, mind and words. All the potency I have is simply based on the strength of my devotion to you. Thus, I always pray to you for the boon that you may never leave me at any time.” In this manner, the two Supreme Personalities enjoyed their conversation and the Lord completed His *prasādam* with great pleasure. These words spoken by Śrī Advaita were truly meant, undoubtedly. Those fools who are not pleased by hearing these words are despicable upstarts and offenders, whose faces Śrī Advaita would never want to see. The bond of love that exists between the Supreme Lord, Hari, and Lord Śiva is completely true, but the gross materialists have no understanding of this relationship. These Lords, Hari and Śiva, become most displeased if either one of them is shown disrespect. Similar to the affectionate dealings between Hari and Śiva is the bond of love and devotion between Śrī Caitanya and Śrī Advaita Ācārya.

Śrī Advaita Ācārya continuously speaks in this manner, because he is always concerned in his compassionate heart about the well-being of all the conditioned souls. One who can comprehend the words of Śrī Advaita will automatically understand that there is no difference between him and the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Any person who hears the narrations of these pastimes with faith and devotion will surely develop pure devotion for Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the most auspicious benediction. Thus, after completely satisfying Śrī Advaita in every respect, the Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya, returned to His home. The Lord greatly satisfied all His devotees like Śrīla Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura and many, many others by happily taking *prasādam* in their homes and spent the balance of His time in leading His devotees in the performance of congregational chanting of the Holy Name and dancing in ecstasy.

When Śrī Dāmodara Paṇḍita arrived in Purī, the Lord wanted to speak to him confidentially about His own mother, Śrī Śacīdevī, whom Śrī Dāmodara Paṇḍita had visited in Navadvīpa prior to his journey to Purī. The Lord enquired, “Dear Paṇḍita, you stayed with my mother in Navadvīpa. Tell Me truly does My mother possess any devotion to Supreme Lord, Śrī Viṣṇu?” Śrīla Dāmodara Paṇḍita is a great tapasvī, one who has performed a lot of penances and austerities, and an incorruptible, unprejudiced devotee. Thus, this question enraged him, and he retorted, “O Lord, did you ask if Mother Ai has any devotion to the Supreme Lord? What prompts you to enquire about this? All the devotion you possess is by the grace of Mother Ai, Śacīdevī. By her spiritual potency, you have developed devotion for Śrī Viṣṇu. Undoubtedly, this is the truth. The transcendental physical transformations of ecstasy such as weeping, trembling, perspiring, swooning, horripilation, roaring, etc. manifest upon her person in continuous waves and the Holy Name is constantly upon her lips. My Lord, you wanted to know about the devotion of Mother Ai. From what I have seen, she represents devotion to the Supreme Lord and is the very embodiment of *viṣṇu-bhakti*. My Lord, you know all this yet you ask me, probably to test me. Certainly, if anyone utters ‘Ai’, even considering ‘Ai’ a mundane word, by the influence of the transcendental sound vibration of ‘Ai’, he will be delivered from all his suffering.”

Śrī Gauracandra was overcome with immense jubilation upon hearing the glories of Śrī Śacīmātā from Śrīla Dāmodara Paṇḍita. He embraced Paṇḍita Dāmodara repeatedly and said, “Dear Dāmodara, today you have purchased Me by revealing your mind to Me. Whatever devotion I possess is only by the grace of Mother Ai, of this there is no doubt. I am in this world by her desire alone and I will never be able to repay My indebtedness to her. My dear Dāmodara, I am held captive by her. I always desire to see her.” Showering His causeless mercy on Paṇḍita Dāmodara, the Lord made him sit next to Him with the other devotees.

The real reason why Śrī Gauracandra asked about the devotion of Śrī Śacīmātā was to instruct human society. When friends meet, they generally enquire from each other, “Are you well?” To highlight the real import of the words ‘well-being’, the Lord asked this question, for the real meaning of ‘being well’ is to have devotion. If one actually possesses *bhakti*, then one is automatically well, but without *bhakti* even a king leads an inauspicious, unwholesome life. A person may have wealth, fame, luxury, and everything, yet without devotion all is naught and valueless. Someone may not have anything to eat, the height of paucity, but if one has devotion to the Supreme Lord, one is indeed the wealthiest person. When anyone invited the Lord for *prasādam* at his home, the Lord used the invitation as a means to instruct everyone. Smilingly, He would say, “First you become a *lakh-pati*, the possessor of a hundred thousand gold coins, then I will come. I accept invitations only from *lakh-patis*.” The *brāhmaṇas* would become extremely worried. They would approach the Lord and pray, “My Lord, what to speak of a hundred-thousand, none of us has even a thousand! And if you do not visit our homes, then they might as well be burnt to ashes!”

The Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurahari, would then say, “Do you know the real meaning of one who is actually a *lakh-pati*? The one who regularly chants a hundred thousand names of Kṛṣṇa is according to Me a *lakh-pati*. I accept *prasādam* only in his home, not in the home of others.” When the *brāhmaṇas* would hear this pronouncement of Śrī Gaurahari, they were relieved and began to rejoice. They said, “My lord, we will chant a hundred thousand names. Kindly come to our homes. It is our immense good fortune that You instruct us in this manner.” Thus, all the *brāhmaṇas* started to regularly chant a hundred thousand names of Kṛṣṇa, so that the Lord would accept *prasādam* in their homes. The Supreme Lord, the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, in this manner inspired everyone to embrace the path of *bhakti-yoga*, while He himself floated upon the ocean of *bhakti-rasa*. The prime reason for the descent of the Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya, was to inspire the mass of population to embrace *bhakti*. Thus, Śrī Gaurahari never questioned anyone about a topic not related to *bhakti*.

Śrī Gaurahari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, continued, “For a devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, well-being and auspiciousness are constant companions.” The Lord refused to associate with, even look at a person who did not glorify devotional service. One day, He asked His *guru*, Śrī Keśava Bhāratī, about *bhakti* and *jñāna*, “Which is greater, *bhakti* or *jñāna*? Dear master, please consider well before answering and your answer should be unequivocal.” Śrī Bhāratī pondered for a while and then said, “After due deliberation, I have arrived at the conclusion that *bhakti* is superior.” The Lord retorted, “Why do you say *bhakti* is superior? All the *sannyāsīs* assert that *jñāna*, not *bhakti*, is superior!” To this, Śrī Bhāratī remarked, “They do not understand the scriptural imports. One has to follow the path trodden by the previous *ācāryas* and *mahājanas*, preceptors and great devotional authorities. The entire *Vedic* scripture exhort all to follow in the footsteps of the *mahājanas*, but the foolish disobey these instructions and take to deviant paths. All the scriptures are full with the exemplary lives and devotional teachings of the *mahājanas* such as Brahmā, Śiva, Nārada, Prahlāda, Śukadeva, Vyāsa, Śanaka and the Kumāras, Yudhiṣṭhira, Priyavrata, Pṛthu, Dhruva, Akrūra, Uddhava and so on. These *mahājanas* always pray at the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord asking for *bhakti* alone. If *jñāna* were the superior of the two, why do they beg for *bhakti*? Are we to think that the *mahājanas* reject *mukti*, liberation, without proper and careful consideration and mistakenly opt for *bhakti* at all times?

“In the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* [10.14.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.30) we discover the boon that Lord Brahmā asked from the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu: ‘My dear Supreme Lord, whether as Brahmā, as a bird or even a beast, may I have the good fortune of being born as one of your devotees, so that I may serve your lotus-feet.’ Thus, we see that without exception all the *mahājanas* pray to attain *bhakti*.

“This truth is substantiated in the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* [1.20.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/1.20.18): ‘O Supreme Lord, Acyuta, it matters little in which of the hundreds and thousands of different species that I may take my birth, for my only desire is that *bhakti*, undeviating, uninterrupted devotional service to You, always remains enthroned in my heart. O Lord Hṛṣīkeśaḥ, by the result of my *karma*, let me be born in any species of life. All I desire is that in each of those species of life, I may maintain unwavering devotion to you.’

“The *Mahābhārata Vana-parva* 313.117 states: ‘Dry arguments are inconclusive. A thinker and scholar whose opinions and views do not differ from others is not considered a great sage. Merely by studying the *Vedas*, with its numerous schools of thought and departments of knowledge, it is impossible to choose the right path that leads to the proper understanding of the true religious principles. True religious principles are hidden in the hearts of the non-envious saintly souls. Thus, the scriptures exhort all to follow the path advocated by these *mahājanas*, the great authoritative devotional personalities.’ ”

When Śrī Caitanya heard from Śrī Keśava Bhāratī that *bhakti* was the superior, He began to chant, “Hari! Hari!” loudly and in great jubilation. He said, “Truly I say to you, the whole purpose of My descent to earth for so long is to establish the pre-eminence of *bhakti* over all. Śrī Bhāratī, if you had said ‘*jñāna’* was the superior then, indeed, I would have entered the ocean.” Feeling immense satisfaction in His heart the Lord fell at the feet of His *guru* and embraced them. With the greatest affection, Śrī Keśava Bhāratī also offered respects to the Lord. The Lord then said, “One who does not speak about the glories of *bhakti*, his austerities, penances, keeping of a *śikhā*, wearing of a sacred thread, and renunciation are all useless.” The Lord is not interested in discussing any topic other than *bhakti* and in this incarnation, Śrī Caitanya Himself is the embodiment of *bhakti*. All His speech, thoughts, and activities are steeped in *bhakti*. The devotees never see Him doing anything other than dancing, *kīrtana*, and loud chanting.

One day, Śrī Advaita Ācārya, immersed in divine bliss, said to all the devotees, “My dear Vaiṣṇava brothers, let us sing today only about Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya for He is the fountainhead of all incarnations. Today we will not sing about any other incarnations of Godhead. He has delivered the whole universe and has advented only for our sake. Today, we devotees are respected simply because Śrī Gaurāṅga has Himself propagated the congregational chanting of the Holy Name, the most valuable treasure in all the three worlds. You all sing His glories and I will dance. If you are fearful that the Lord will find out then sing more loudly to drown out your fears.”

Śrī Caitanya was always trying to hide His real identity, so the devotees were afraid to sing about Him as the Supreme Lord lest He would find out. However, they could not disregard the instruction of Śrī Advaita? Therefore, they began to sing about Śrī Gaurāṅga while Śrī Advaita danced with bubbling exhilaration. The devotees experienced unbounded joy as they sang about the eternally new and unique incarnation of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

Śrī Advaita then took the lead himself in singing his own composition. He sang, “Śrī Caitanya is none other than Nārāyaṇa, the ocean of mercy, friend to distressed and suffering, please Lord be kind to me.” Other devotees, as led by him, sang, “All glory, all glory to Śacīnandana, the son of Śrī Śacīmātā. All glory to Śrī Gauracandra, the Supreme Lord of Vaikuṇṭha. All glory to Gaura-gopāla who loves *saṅkīrtana*, who is beloved of the devotees, and who is Death Personified to the atheistic demons.” Śrī Advaita danced oblivious to the external world and the devotees glorified the transcendental qualities and activities of Śrī Caitanya:

“O see how Śrī Caitanya, the Supreme Godhead, sings in jubilation and rolls in the dust in ecstasy.

“He is the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, but has incarnated as a *brāhmaṇa* to propagate and Himself relish *saṅkīrtana*.

“His bodily lustre puts the brilliance of gold to shame. His beauty is a matchless sight. His hands extend down to His knees.

“He wears the robes of a renunciant and becomes inebriated with the ambrosia of His Divine Self. How skilfully He dances!”

Then, Śrī Advaita began to sing another composition of his own:

“All victory to Śrī Gaurasundara, the ever expanding ocean of compassion.

“All glory to the prince of Vṛndāvana, yet now He has appeared as the hero of Navadvīpa.

“Kindly offer to me the cooling shade of your lotus feet.”

Gradually picking up in tempo, the *kīrtana* built up with the devotees experiencing increasing joy and Śrī Advaita danced tirelessly thinking only of the lotus feet Śrī Caitanya. The compositions were new to the devotees, so they enjoyed the *kīrtana* even more. The ecstasy that descended upon the devotees is indescribable. Only Śrī Nityānanda could fully narrate this wonderful happening.

Hearing loudly and clearly the full-throated *kīrtana*, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the crest jewel of all *sannyāsīs*, arrived at the venue. The Lord beheld a magnificent scene where the devotees were radiant with divine bliss as Śrī Advaita danced in ecstasy. The devotees felt no fear as they loudly and openly sang His glories as He stood there in person. Śrī Caitanya had always maintained a mood of humble servitorship to the Supreme Lord. He always repeated, “I am the servant of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.” No one had ever dared to call Him the Supreme Lord is His presence. However, now, on the strength of the potency and position of Śrī Advaita, the devotees sang fearlessly, glorifying Śrī Caitanya as the Supreme Godhead. Listening to His own glorification for a short while, He seemed to feel ashamed. The Supreme Lord is the original *śikṣā-guru*, instructing spiritual master, of the universe and therefore He quietly left the venue just to teach everyone the proper etiquette. This however did not deter the devotees from singing even more loudly the glories of Śrī Caitanya.

The devotees were so steeped in *kīrtana-rasa* that they completely forgot themselves. Each of them saw Śrī Caitanya amongst themselves participating in the *kīrtana*. They became like madmen intoxicated with the ambrosia of the glories Śrī Gaurasundara. The pious were very jubilant upon hearing the glories of the Lord, but out of envy, the impious were disgruntled. Those fools and rascals who are not pleased to hear the divine excellences of Śrī Caitanya—even if some of them are big *brahmacārīs* and *sannyāsīs*—what is the use to them of this rarely attained human life? In this manner, the devotees were immersed in *saṅkīrtana-rasa* all the time. Whosoever hears or reads these narrations of ecstatic devotional activities is factually granted the opportunity to be amidst these wonderful pastimes in spirit.

After a long and enthusiastic *kīrtana*, the devotees went to take *darśana* of Śrī Gaurahari.
