However, the Lord, after returning from the *kīrtana* where He had been glorified, lay down and seemed quite upset. Śrī Govinda, the servant of the Lord, came and informed the Lord that all the Vaiṣṇavas were waiting at His door, hoping to see Him. The Lord instructed Śrī Govinda to usher everyone inside. The Lord remained lying and did not look at anyone and so the devotees became quite nervous and afraid and began to pray, quietly remembering the lotus feet of Lord.

After a short time the Lord, the loving guardian of His devotees, got up and asked, “Noble Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and my dear Vaiṣṇavas! Leaving aside the singing of the name and glories of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whom did you choose today as an *avatāra*? What were you singing today? Can you explain this to Me?”

Endowed with great oratorical skill, Śrī Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita replied, “My Lord, the *jīvas* are not independent entities. Like puppets, they do and say only as the Supreme Controller wishes. This is what has occurred today. We sang what the Supreme Controller wanted us to sing.”

The Lord retorted, “You and others are erudite scholars, so why do you expose that which is meant to be a secret?” Śrī Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita mimed by putting up his hands skyward as if trying to shade his eyes from the glare of the sun; he seemed to be smiling within himself.

The Lord then enquired, “Dear Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, what is the meaning of your mime, will you explain?”

Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita replied, “Cleary, I am trying to cover the sun with my hands. However, is it possible to cover the sun with the palm of one’s hand? Similarly, it is possible to hide your fame? Even if the sun may be covered with the palm, yet there is no way you can hide Yourself. The Supreme Personality, who could not remain hidden within the Milk Ocean, how can He be hidden in the midst of a teeming mass? From the Himalayas to Rāmeśvaram and to the very boundaries of the world, Your fame and glories are as self-evident as the sun. In fact, Satyaloka, the abode of Lord Brahmā, is now reverberating with *kīrtanas* that glorify You. How many of us are you going to punish for this?”

The Supreme Personality of Godhead is famous for championing His beloved devotees and just then, a wonderful miracle occurred. Thousands of visitors who had come to see Lord Jagannātha were now on the doorsteps of Śrī Gaurahari’s home anxious to see Him. They had all come from different parts of the country. Some were from Tripura, others from Caṭṭagrāma, a group from Śrīhaṭṭa, many from Bengal and so on. Thousands of voices sang the glories of Śrī Caitanya:

“All glory! All glory to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the tender of the forest of devotion! The Supreme One, who relishes devotional service unto Himself!

“All victory to the Supreme Lord who has put on the robes of a renunciant! He is Murāri, Kṛṣṇa Himself, and is now addicted to constant and ecstatic *kīrtana*!

“All victory to You! The King of twice-born *brāhmaṇas*, the Hero of Vaikuṇṭha, the Supreme Benefactor of this universe!

“All glory to you, O Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the son of Śrī Śacīmātā!”

Thousands sang and danced in ecstasy.

Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita then said to the Lord, “My Lord, what will you do now? Where will you hide? The whole world is singing Your glories as we heard just now. My Lord, although you are invisible, imperceptible and unmanifest, yet out of Your causeless mercy, You have personally appeared. You hide Yourself and then by Your will alone You manifest Yourself. Only those who are recipients of Your divine grace are able to know this truth.” Śrī Gaurasundara replied, “You, Śrīvāsa, have displayed your spiritual potency by making the people sing *kīrtana* and I have been thus defeated by you. Truly, you are empowered with the fullest potency of *bhakti*.”

It is a well-known truth that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is always eager to increase the fame and influence of His devotees. This is His natural disposition, which is confirmed in the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* and in fact all the *Vedas*. Śrī Caitanya then bade farewell to all the Vaiṣṇavas with a beatific smile on His face. The Lord is full of paternal love and protectiveness for His devotees and the devotees all glorify Him as Śrī Kṛṣṇa. All the stalwart Vaiṣṇavas like Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Advaita Ācārya and others unanimously assert that Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Yet the unfortunate and ignorant public do not heed the words of these Supreme Personalities, instead they falsely proclaim mortal *jīvas* as incarnations of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

The divine symptoms that embellish only the Supreme Lord are that He lies on the bed of Śrī Ananta-Śeṣa; is served by the Goddess of Fortune, Śrī Lakṣmī Devī; His chest is marked with the Śrīvatsa sign; the Kaustubha jewel adorns His necklace; His carrier is Śrī Garuḍa; and Śrī Gaṅgādevī emanates from His lotus-feet. All the revealed scriptures and saintly Vaiṣṇavas unequivocally declare that none other than the Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya, alone possesses these divine symbols. All who accept with good faith these instructions of the Vaiṣṇavas are surely blessed with all-round victory and success. Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya always gave His transcendental association to all the Vaiṣṇavas and being thus surrounded by pure devotees all the time, Śrī Caitanya was like the effulgent moon flanked on all sides by bright stars. The devotees sat around Him and Śrī Caitanya, the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, sat in their midst as the crest jewel of the *sannyāsa* order, chanting the name of Kṛṣṇa incessantly.

Two great and fortunate souls suddenly appeared in that assembly and presented themselves to the Lord. They were siblings, Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika. The Lord welcomed them, showering blessings upon them with His merciful glance. From a distance, the brothers offered prostrated obeisances with the utmost humility, holding straw between the teeth. They offered this prayer to the Lord, “All glory, all glory to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, whose mercy benedicts the entire universe. All victory to You! O protector of the poor and fallen, the benefactor of the world, having accepted the robes of renunciation, You are now the greatest *sannyāsī*. You are always enchanted by incessant *kīrtana* and You are the beginning, middle, and end of everything. In this incarnation, You have taken the role of a pure Vaiṣṇava devotee as Your divine pastime and by propagating the resplendent path of pure *bhakti*, You are delivering the entire creation. Yet, our Lord, why have we not been saved, are we not a part of this creation? From birth, we have been blinded by illusory sense enjoyment. Thus, we have neglected to worship Your lotus feet and thereby have deprived ourselves of any good fortune. Neither did we associate with Your devotees, nor did we participate in hearing and chanting Your glories.”

“You have cheated us, our Lord, by giving me a high government position and royal favour. Why then did You bestow upon us this human birth? The human birth is so highly favoured by even the demigods, yet in spite of this human birth, You have deprived us. Now, our Lord be kind and shower us with Your causeless mercy that we may live simply under the trees and chant Your Holy Name. We stand at Your door, grant us the wish that we may receive the remnants of Your pure devotees and thus spent the rest of our lives.” In this way, the two brothers Śrīla Rūpa and Śrīla Sanātana prayed to the Lord invoking His mercy. The Lord listened to their grave solicitations and showered them with the blessings of His compassionate glance.

Śrī Caitanya said to them, “You two brothers are truly fortunate for you have been able to sever the chains that bind one to family life and material existence. The entire world is shackled to family life and mundane relationships and you have been successful in breaking away from all of that. Now if you sincerely desire to enter spiritual life and gain *prema-bhakti* then fall and catch hold of the lotus feet of Śrī Advaita Ācārya. Śrī Ācārya is the repository of *bhakti* and by his grace, one obtains devotion to Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.” Hearing this the two great souls fell at the feet of Śrī Ācārya and prayed, “All glory to Śrī Advaita Ācārya, the deliverer of the fallen souls. Kindly save these two fallen, wretched souls.”

Śrī Gaurasundara said, “My dear Ācārya, kindly listen. Rarely will you find such renounced and saintly souls in Kali-yuga. Turning their backs to royal comforts and pleasures, they have taken up the water-pot and blanket of the itinerant *sādhu*, holy man. They now live in Mathurā Vṛndāvana and constantly chant Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s Holy Name. Without hesitation, inundate their hearts with *kṛṣṇa-bhakti*, so that they never forget Śrī Kṛṣṇa, birth after birth. You are the supervisor of the treasure house of *bhakti* and if you do not award *bhakti*, then who can obtain *kṛṣṇa-bhakti*, the association of the devotees of Kṛṣṇa, and even Kṛṣṇa Himself?”

Śrī Advaita replied, “My Lord, It is You who are the most generous benefactor of this world. As soon as You order, I will immediately give. I am just a keeper of your treasury of *bhakti* and my duty is to execute Your orders, which I follow with my body, mind, and words. Therefore, I wish that these two fortunate souls be swathed in the Nectar Ocean of *prema-bhakti*.” Hearing this the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurahari, was extremely jubilant and He began to loudly chant the Holy Name.

The Lord then spoke to Dabira Khāsa, Śrīla Rūpa, “Now you have received *kṛṣṇa-prema-bhakti*, for if Śrī Advaita blesses someone, that person immediately attains *kṛṣṇa-bhakti*. Śrī Advaita is invested with the full potency of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Stay here a few days, and take *darśana* of the lotus-like beautiful face of Lord Jagannātha and then return to Mathurā and continue to live there. Counteract the influence of passion and ignorance in the West by distributing *bhakti-rasa* to all souls. I will also be visiting Mathurā soon, so find a solitary place for Me to stay.”

The Lord changed the name of Sākara Mallika to Śrī Santana and Dabira Khāsa to Śrī Rūpa. Even today, these two brothers Śrīla Rūpa and Śrīla Sanātana are famous all over the world by mercy Śrī Caitanya, who is always eagerly enhancing the fame and glory of His devotees. Whether the subject is the esoteric position of Śrī Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, or another devotee, Śrī Caitanya with great satisfaction and pleasure broadcasts the reality about His beloved devotees. The Lord attentively reveals the transcendental truths about the incarnations and expansions of His devotees, how to worship a Vaiṣṇava, and the facts about the pure Vaiṣṇavis.

One day, the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurahari, was sitting encircled by His devotees Śrī Advaita, Śrī Śrīvāsa and others. The Lord asked Śrīla Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura about Śrī Advaita Ācārya, “Tell Me, Paṇḍita Śrīvāsa, in your consideration what sort of Vaiṣṇava is Śrī Advaita?” Śrī Śrīvāsa thought for a while and replied, “In my opinion, he is like Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī, or Śrī Prahlāda Mahārāja.”

Hearing this comparison of Śrī Advaita with Śukadeva and Prahlāda, the Lord in a fit of anger struck Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita. Just as a father affectionately slaps his son to teach him a lesson, the Lord had just done the same with Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita.

The Lord exclaimed, “What did you say Śrīvāsa! What did you say! My Nāḍā, Advaita, is Śukadeva or Prahlāda? You claim that Śukadeva is a fully liberated soul, but in comparison to My Nāḍā, he is but a mere infant. Such a derogatory statement about My beloved Nāḍā, coming from you, Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, is really breaking My heart.”

Saying this the Lord stood up, picked up a cane and rushed toward Śrīvāsa to beat him and drive him away. Right then, Śrīla Advaita Ācārya jumped up and with the utmost respect he caught hold of the hand of Śrī Gaurahari and very humbly said, “A father teaches the son with love and compassion. Thus, who in all the three worlds is a recipient of your ire?”

Śrī Advaita’s words pacified the anger of the Lord and in ecstasy the Lord then began to speak, glorifying Śrī Advaita, “All of you are like My children, thus I cannot remain angry with you for very long. Who is there who really knows My Nāḍā, Śrī Advaita? He woke me up from My mystic sleep and made Me descend to earth. My Nāḍā is very humble, but actually, Śukadeva, Prahlāda and others are all his children. Never forget, O Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, that I have incarnated for the sake of Śrī Advaita. His booming voice still rings in My ears as He woke Me up while I lay upon the Milk Ocean in the mystic sleep of *yoga-nidrā*.”

Śrīla Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita was extremely fond of Śrī Advaita Ācārya and upon hearing the Lord’s praises of Śrī Advaita, he felt very happy. Then with utmost reverence and remorse Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita said, “O Lord, kindly forgive my offences. You alone know the full truth about Your Advaita and only when You reveal this truth will the other devotees and myself understand the real identity of Śrī Advaita. Today, by Your grace, I am extremely fortunate because You have taught me that Śrī Advaita Ācārya is *viṣṇu-tattva* and not a *jīva*, a marginal living entity. This gives me immense strength and spiritual potency. From today, I vow in your presence, that even if I should see Śrī Advaita associating with low-class women or even drinking alcohol, I will always serve and respect him, truly this I say to you.” The Lord was completely pacified and content with the words of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and soon the assembly all felt as happy and carefree as before.

These confidential, transcendental narratives are full of esoteric truths and by hearing them, one is sure to attain the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. The Supreme Godhead, Śrī Gaurahari, is omniscient, omnipotent and the reservoir of all devotion. Those souls, who properly understand His supreme position, worship Him sincerely in complete surrender and are thus able to realise these esoteric truths deeply.

The *Vedas* declare that the truth about the Supreme Lord and His *viṣṇu-tattva* expansions is beyond the grasp of human thought. In the same way, the divine characteristics and personalities of His Vaiṣṇava devotees are also outside the comprehension of ordinary mortals. Generally, the sometimes extreme and even apparently harsh activities of exalted and self-realized Vaiṣṇavas are not understood by the common man, but if out of ignorance or envy they criticize these elevated Vaiṣṇavas such offenders pave their way to hell.

Therefore, always see the sometimes seemingly harsh activity of a perfected Vaiṣṇava as his most eloquent teaching. Many such extraordinary activities of perfected Vaiṣṇavas are recorded in the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*. The great sage, Bhṛgu, the son of Lord Brahmā is constantly meditating upon the lotus-feet of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, yet even though he kicked the Lord upon His chest, the sage is still considered a great Vaiṣṇava. In this context, I shall now narrate this pastime, which is described in the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*.

In ancient times, we read that many great sages had assembled on the bank of the sacred Sarasvatī River to perform the sacrifice of hearing the *Purāṇas*. Each of them was very learned and well versed in the scriptures and they discussed only transcendental topics. Thus, in their meeting they resolved to discover who of the three divinities, Brahmā, Śiva and Viṣṇu, is the chief and Supreme over all. Some said Brahmā is the Supreme, others said Maheśvara, Śiva, and yet others maintained that Viṣṇu is the Lord of all Lords.

The various *Purāṇas* apparently proposed each of the three major divinities as the Supreme. Of course, this was confusing so they turned to the sage Bhṛgu Muni for help in resolving the issue. Since he was the son of Lord Brahmā, born of his mind, and the most senior and expert amongst the sages, Bhṛgu, was the right choice to investigate. The sages agreed that they would unanimously accept the decision of Bhṛgu Muni after he had personally tested each of the divinities. Upon hearing their request, the great sage Bhṛgu took off to Brahmāloka, the abode of Lord Brahmā.

Śrī Bhṛgu Muni entered the court of Lord Brahmā and stood there in front of Lord Brahmā. Lord Brahmā was very happy to see his son and asked him about his well-being. Since the sage had come to test his father, he did not pay much heed to Lord Brahmā’s words, but simply acted haughtily. Neither did he offer respects, nor endearing words, as is becoming of a son to his father. When Lord Brahmā noticed his son’s misdemeanour and uncouth behaviour, he became livid with rage. Seeing the burning eyes of his father, which could quickly reduce him to ashes, the sage swiftly fled the scene. Others in Lord Brahmā’s court began to pacify Lord Brahmā saying, “After all he is your son our Lord, how can you as a father be so angry with your son?” Overcome with paternal affection Lord Brahmā put aside his anger. The words of the courtiers had acted like water upon a fire. The sage Bhṛgu then returned to explain everything to Lord Brahmā and next proceeded to Mount Kailāsa to test Lord Śiva.

Lord Śiva, upon seeing Bhṛgu Muni, became very exultant and together with his wife, Śrī Pārvatī Devī, stood up to greet him. The sage was his elder brother so respectfully, he approached the sage and wanted to embrace him. The sage said, “O Maheśa, do not touch me! You always dress like an uncivilized barbarian. You are also always surrounded by unclean and uncouth ghosts, hobgoblins, and what not—all untouchables. Your behaviour is unpredictable and ill mannered, and which scripture recommends one to smear ashes all over the body? If you touch me, I will have to take a bath, so stay away from me!”

Sage Bhṛgu was saying all these words simply to test Śrī Maheśvara, but otherwise never a word of criticism about Lord Śiva would be heard from his mouth. However now, Lord Śiva was so enraged with the sage Bhṛgu that forgetting he was his elder brother, he lifted his trident and looked as if he were about to destroy the Three Worlds. As he rushed towards the sage, Śrī Pārvatī devī stepped in between and caught hold of the hand of her husband. She then fell at his feet and begged him saying, “My Lord, is it proper to be so angry with your elder brother?” His wife’s wise solicitations calmed Lord Śiva and he felt ashamed for his outburst. From there, the sage went to Vaikuṇṭha to test Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

The Supreme Personality of Godhead was reclining upon His gem-studded bed, while the Goddess of Fortune, Śrī Lakṣmī Devī, massaged His lotus feet. Suddenly, Bhṛgu Muni appeared as if from nowhere and kicked the Lord upon His chest. Seeing the sage Bhṛgu, the Supreme Lord immediately stood up and offered His respects with folded hands, feeling very pleased. Together with His wife, Śrī Lakṣmī Devī, the Supreme Lord then bathed the feet of the sage and next offered him their finest seat to sit upon. With His own hands, the Lord smeared sandalwood paste upon the body of the sage. The Lord acted as if He were an offender trying to exonerate Himself from His offences.

Lord Viṣṇu said to the sage, “I was not at all aware of your auspicious arrival, thus kindly forgive Me for My transgression of etiquette. The holy water from the bathing of your feet purifies all the places of holy pilgrimage. Today, it has purified all the kings and emperors of the innumerable *brahmāṇḍas*, universes, which are situated in My personal form. May your character and personality remain forever unsullied and undiminished.

“The dust from your foot I will keep imprinted upon My breast with great happiness, in the same place where My beloved wife, Śrī Lakṣmī Devī, is seated. Let the *Vedas* declare My name as ‘Śrīvatsa-lāñchana’, one who is marked with the sign of Śrīvatsa.” The sage, upon hearing the words of the Supreme Lord and witnessing His humble demeanour, which was free from lust, greed, anger, and illusion, was truly amazed. He felt greatly ashamed, hung his head down, and remained so for a long time.

The actions of Bṛghu Muni were not really his own doing. Certainly, he had acted under some compulsion, as if under a spell. When he came out of this spell, he was overcome with joy and reverence for the Supreme Lord. Saturated with the ambrosia of *bhakti-rasa*, he began to dance, laugh, tremble, perspire, horripilate, and swoon, all at the same time. While dancing, he began to joyfully chant, “Lord Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Lord of all, the life of every living entity!”

The son of Lord Brahmā, the great sage Bhṛgu Muni, realised from observing the gentle and humble behaviour of Śrī Kṛṣṇa that loving devotion, *prema-bhakti*, could be reposed only in Śrī Kṛṣṇa and no one else. The sage in great ecstasy shed profuse tears of joy and became almost inert like a pillar. He surrendered himself totally at the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord and returned to the assembly of the sages on the bank of the River Sarasvatī.

The sages were jubilant upon the return of Bhṛgu. They said to him, “So kindly tell us what you experienced. Your decision will be unanimously accepted.” Śrī Bhṛgu narrated in full everything that had occurred, how Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva, and then Lord Viṣṇu had received him and behaved. Completing his narrative, the sage said, “Truly, I say to you, that the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, is certainly the topmost. He is the Supreme Controller of everyone, the father and maintainer. Even Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva accept His authority. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the Lord, Master and Protector of all beings. Therefore, worship His lotus feet without doubt or hesitation. Religiosity, knowledge, wonderful pious acts, opulence, renunciation, self realization and so on—all the various potencies emanate from Lord Kṛṣṇa, of this there is no doubt. Therefore, worship and glorify the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, alone.”

The self-same Supreme Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, has now appeared as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya in order to inaugurate the congregational chanting of the Holy Name. All the sages after hearing the verdict of Bhṛgu Muni that the Supreme Lord, Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the best and highest of all, first glorified Bhṛgu and then unanimously concluded, “O great sage Bhṛgu, you have dissipated our doubts and have cured our mental indecision.” They firmly embraced the path of devotion to Śrī Kṛṣṇa with determination and continued to worship Lord Śiva and Lord Brahmā, but as elevated devotees of the Supreme Lord.

The scriptures confirm that the activities of an exalted and perfected Vaiṣṇava are sometimes extreme, and hence are incomprehensible to most people. Simply to test the Lord many other options were available, but the sage decided to kick the Lord. Without the mercy of the Supreme Lord, the sage would never have had the audacity of kick the Lord upon His chest. Thus, the scriptural conclusion is that the activities of a divine personality are beyond the grasp of the common man.

The truth of the matter is that the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, had entered the body of Śrī Bhṛgu Muni and performed these acts to broadcast the glories of *bhakti*, pure devotion. As long as Bhṛgu maintained an attitude of awe and reverence towards the Lord, he would never have dared to do such an act, but the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, is always promoting the excellence of His devotees. Lord Śiva and Lord Brahmā displayed anger towards the sage Bhṛgu so that the glories of the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, would become obvious to all.

Just as the devotees are constantly and eternally endeavouring to glorify the divine mystery of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, similarly the Supreme Lord, in turn, is always expanding the name and fame of His pure devotees. Therefore, those, who—without understanding the activities of an exalted Vaiṣṇava—criticise him, are doomed to eternal perdition. Sometimes, even the most elevated Vaiṣṇavas act like fallen, low class men, but only by the grace of the Supreme Lord is one able to understand the real purpose of this unusual behaviour and thereby avoid any criticism and the resultant offence.

The safest way to behave and prevent offences is to be humble towards everyone and respectful to all. Take full shelter at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and be mindful of the words spoken by saintly souls and elevated preceptors. This will attract the grace of Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the form of good intelligence, which will then always protect one from all harm and remove all obstacles onthe spiritual path.

Those who hear these narratives about Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya with love and devotion will be blessed with happiness and ultimate release from all suffering.

I, Vṛndāvana dāsa, humbly offer this song at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, who are my life and soul.

## 10: Śrī Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi Pastimes

All glory, all glory to the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gauracandra, who is marked with the sign of Śrīvatsa!

All victory to the embodiment of the eternal religion of all souls, Śrī Gaurahari, for He is the crest jewel manifesting from the ocean bed of the womb of Śrī Śacīmātā!

All glory to you, O Gaura-gopāla, for You are always attracted to and propagate the congregational chanting of the Lord’s Holy Name. You are the protector of Your beloved devotees and Death Personified for the evil wrongdoers.

All victory! All victory to Śrī Gaurāṅga with all His followers! Simply by hearing the pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, one develops *bhakti*, pure devotion.

Enacting the role of a *sannyāsī*, the Supreme Hero of Vaikuṇṭha enjoyed the company of His devotees. One day, the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurahari, was sitting contentedly when Śrī Advaita Ācārya came, offered obeisances, and sat down. The Lord smiled and enquired of Śrī Advaita, “Where are you coming from and what work have you been doing?”

Śrī A:vaita replied, “I took *darśana* of Lord Jagannātha and now I have come to see you.”

The Lord insisted, “Yes, but after having *darśana* of Lord Jagannātha, what did you do?”

Śrī Advaita replied, “First, I had *darśana* of Lord Jagannātha and then I circumambulated Him several times.”

When the Lord heard ‘*pradakṣiṇa*’, circumambulation, He smiled and said, “You have been defeated.”

Surprised, Śrī Advaita enquired, “In what matter have I lost? First, tell me and then you can claim to have won.”

The Lord replied, “Very well, then hear how you have lost. You circumambulated Lord Jagannātha, so each time you were behind the Deities, you could not have *darśana* of the sweet smiling face of the Lord. When I take *darśana* of the Lord the entire time My eyes never leave the transcendental face of Lord Jagannātha, whether I stand on the left side, or the right side. Whereas, each time you go behind, His radiant face is lost to your vision.”

Śrī Advaita then admitted with folded palms, “Truly, I have been completely defeated by You. Other than you, no one in the three worlds understands the significance of what you have said. I have lost to your transcendental reasoning.”

The entire assembly of Vaiṣṇavas were joyful by hearing such a transcendental topic and exchange. They jubilantly chanted the Holy Name aloud. Śrī Gaurahari was constantly finding ways to convert everyday experiences into a point of instruction for His disciples. Moreover, in His dealings with everyone, especially Śrī Advaita, He was always very affectionate.

One day, Śrīla Gadādhara Paṇḍita revealed to the Lord, his reason for wanting re-initiation. He said, “I have revealed my *iṣṭa-mantra* (the *mantra* of one’s worshipable Deity) that I received from my *guru* to an undeserving person and since then my mind is disturbed. My Lord, You kindly reinitiate me with the same *iṣṭa-mantra*, then my mind will become jubilant again.”

The Lord replied, “Be very careful, that you do not commit any offences to your *guru*, the one who instructed you on the *iṣṭa-mantra*. As long as your *mantra guru* is present, you cannot go elsewhere, or even come to me. This would jeopardize the spiritual life of both you and Me.”

Śrī Gadādhara continued, “However, at present he is not here, so instead You kindly do the needful?”

The Lord replied, “Your *guru* is Śrī Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi. Providence will arrange that you meet him.”

The omniscient Supreme Godhead, the crest jewel of all the wisest mystics, knows everything, past, present, and future. He said, “Śrī Vidyānidhi is soon to come here to Śrī Jagannātha Purī. In about ten days, he will arrive just to see Me. For the past few days, I have been thinking often about Śrī Vidyānidhi and now I know that you also, Gadādhara, have been pulling him here like a magnet.”

The Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurasundara, spent most of his time with Śrīla Gadādhara listening to his readings from the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*. Whilst listening, the Lord manifested the ecstatic spiritual transformations of *prema-bhāva*. The Lord heard the pastimes of Prahlāda Mahārāja and Dhruva Mahārāja many hundreds of times, but every time he would hear it with completely rapt attention. All other activities were relinquished in order to hear the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* and discuss the Holy Name, form, qualities, and pastimes of the Supreme Lord.

The Lord heard the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* from Śrīla Gadādhara alone. Similarly, He heard *kṛṣṇa-guṇa kīrtana* from the mouth of Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, who sang as the Lord danced in a state of ecstatic spiritual trance. The physical transformations of *prema* such as weeping, quivering, laughter, swooning, horripilation, etc. appeared on His transcendental body. All these ecstatic symptoms are eternally present in the Lord and when Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara sang aloud the qualities of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Lord became oblivious of the external world and danced with full abandon. Śrīla Dāmodara Svarūpa was the foremost amongst the Lord’s eternal associates and *sannyāsīs*. The Lord favoured him as much as He loved Śrīla Paramānanda Purī.

The singing of Śrīla Dāmodara Svarūpa Gosvāmī was saturated with *bhakti-rasa*, the nectar of devotion, and the Lord could never withhold Himself from dancing each time Svarūpa Dāmodara sang *kīrtana*. However, Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara was extremely unassuming and He went about his business quietly, making sure he was undetected. In *kīrtana*, he was like Śrī Nārada with his *vīṇā-tamburā*, and none other than the Supreme Lord danced to his tune. Thus, amongst all beloved *sannyāsīs* of the Lord, none were so favoured, as were Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara and Śrīla Paramānanda Purī. Both remained always close by the side of the Lord. When the Lord entered the *sannyāsa* order, they were by His side and these *sannyāsīs* were like the two arms of the Lord. Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara stayed by His side in Purī whilst the Lord became increasingly deeply absorbed in *kīrtana* day and night. Whether on pilgrimage, honouring *prasādam*, or traveling, the Lord made sure that Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara was by His side at all times.

Before taking *sannyāsa*, Śrīla Svarūpa was known as Śrī Puruṣottama Bhaṭṭācārya and Śrīla Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi was his very dear friend and companion. Even while walking, if the Lord heard the *kīrtana* of Śrīla Svarūpa, He would be unable to check Himself from dancing and would lose his way. Anywhere and everywhere, Śrīla Svarūpa’s *kīrtana* would immediately put the Lord into ecstatic trance. In great jubilation the Lord would roar like a lion, fall down like a stick and Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara would be instantly by His side saving Him from falling. Who is able to describe the immense good fortune of Śrīla Svarūpa?

One day, the Lord in one of His ecstatic trances fell into a well. The devotees were shocked and began to wail loudly, while Śrīla Advaita knelt down holding his head. However, the Lord was not in the slightest aware of what had happened and like a small child he floated upon the water still deep in trance. However, the water in the well upon being touched by the transcendental form of the Supreme Lord turned into fresh butter cream and His body had not so much as received a scratch. The *kīrtana* of Śrīla Svarūpa generated such mystic potency that when the Vaiṣṇavas danced, they never felt any thorny bushes piercing their skins. Quickly, Śrī Advaita and others lifted the Lord out of the well, but the Lord was still unaware of what had transpired and kept asking, “What happened? What happened?” He was so steeped in *bhakti-rasa* that He was still oblivious to His surrounding. He enquired from everyone, unmindful of what had occurred. Hearing these nectarine words from the graceful lotus mouth of the Lord, Advaita and the devotees floated in bliss. All the devotees became relieved and extremely joyous that their beloved Lord was unhurt.

The Supreme Lord performed endless wonderful pastimes always steeped in the nectar of *bhakti*, pure devotion. When Śrīla Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi arrived in Purī, the Lord immediately knew and soon, by the desire of the Lord, Śrīla Vidyānidhi was drawn to the place where the Lord was awaiting his arrival. Seeing Śrīla Vidyānidhi, the Lord became overjoyed and said aloud, “Here comes My father! My father has come!” Śrīla Vidyānidhi was in ecstasy, His heart flooded with the ambrosia of *bhakti* and he became a *prema-nidhī*, an ocean of *prema*. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Gaura-nārāyaṇa, is the affectionate guardian of His devotees, *bhakta-vatsala*. He firmly embraced Vidyānidhi, the ocean of *prema-rasa*, and wept profusely in jubilation. All the devotees also began to weep tears of joy; the scene was directly from Vaikuṇṭha. The association of Śrīla Vidyānidhi augmented the ecstasy of the devotees at every moment.

The friend and companion of Śrīla Vidyānidhi from his earlier days was Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara and they met once more in the presence of the Lord. Each desiring to take the foot dust from the other, they jostled, pushed, and threw each other down upon the floor both wanting to be the first to touch the feet of the other. However, being equally matched neither could overpower the other. All the while, the devotees and the Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurasundara, were enjoying this transcendental competition with joyful laughter. After a while when they settled down, the Lord said to Śrīla Vidyānidhi, “Stay with us here in Nīlācala for a while.” Hearing the Lord’s words, Śrīla Vidyānidhi became euphoric, considering his greatest fortune to be near the Lord. Śrīla Gadādhara Paṇḍita availed of this opportunity and was reinitiated in his *iṣṭa-mantra* from his *guru*, Śrīla Vidyānidhi.

There is no end to the glories of Śrīla Vidyānidhi. Yet, foremost is that he was the *guru* of Śrīla Gadādhara, a disciple who reached limitless *prema*. Śrīla Advaita and Śrīla Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura were always eager to expound the greatness of Śrī Vidyānidhi and in this endeavour, they were joined by wonderful devotional stalwarts like Śrīla Murāri Gupta and Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura. In fact, all the Vaiṣṇavas were full of praise for the character and spotless purity of Śrī Vidyānidhi. Similarly, Śrīla Vidyānidhi was also extremely fond of all the devotees and he loved them with all his heart, mind and words. He was completely devoid of any pride or false ego. Truly, it is impossible to understand the degree of divine grace, he received from Śrī Caitanya and from the Supreme Lover, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Having heard the facts and stories directly from the divine lips of Śrī Gadādhara, I will try to describe a little about how dear Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi was to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

The Supreme Lord, Śrī Gaurasundara, kept Śrīla Vidyānidhi near Him and arranged a residence for him in Yameśvara next to the ocean. During his stay in Nīlācala, he always went with his bosom friend, Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara, for regular *darśana* of Lord Jagannātha. At other times, they were absorbed in discussing esoteric topics on the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

Soon, the time for the festival of ‘Oḍana-ṣaṣṭhī’ of Lord Jagannātha arrived. On this occasion by the desire of Lord Jagannātha, His servants dress Him in new, starched clothes. Śrī Gaurasundara accompanied by all His devotees came to see Lord Jagannātha on Oḍana-ṣaṣṭhī. Musical bands with numerous instruments, *mṛdaṅgas*, conch shells, bells, etc. echoed all around and the entire town wore a festive look. Their Lordships wore many different sets of clothes that day and the festival would last until the *Makara-saṅkrānti*, in mid-January. Śrī Gaurasundara and the Vaiṣṇavas stayed late into the night, gripped in waves of ecstasy, seeing Śrī Jagannātha’s many changes of dress.

The Supreme Lord as the worshiper, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, worshiped Himself in His Deity form, Lord Jagannātha. Unless the Lord blesses one, one cannot fathom this divine, esoteric, mystery, which was now being played out. Upon the altar the Supreme Lord, Śrī Jagannātha, in His wooden Deity form sat in *yoga-āsana* while He, as the crest jewel of all *sannyāsīs*, steeped in the mellows of *bhakti-yoga*, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, came for His own *darśana*.

On the occasion of the Oḍana-ṣaṣṭhī festival, the Deities are colourfully dressed in the finest of silks and with beautiful golden jewellery inlaid with precious gems. Garlands, bracelets, and earrings all made from fragrant seasonal flowers further bedeck Their Lordships. Scented oils, incense, flowers, ghee-lamps, and the sixteen different items for special worship are offered to Lord Jagannātha. Grand and opulent offerings of *prasādam* are also made continually. Śrī Gaurahari observed these festivities with His devotees and then feeling great joy and satisfaction returned home. Bidding farewell to all the Vaiṣṇavas, the Lord sought the calm of solitude.

After everyone had left, Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara and Śrīla Vidyānidhi remained together and they talked very intimately revealing their hearts and minds to each other. Śrīla Vidyānidhi had doubts regarding the starched dresses that Jagannātha was wearing and he asked Śrīla Svarūpa, “Why do they dress the Lord in starched clothes without first washing them? Here, in this land, the people are so conscious about scriptural rules, yet in the scriptures are not starched clothes considered unclean?” Śrīla Svarūpa replied, “Here no one faults this practice since it is considered a part of their religious tradition. Those who strictly follow scriptural rules may not completely agree with this, but this tradition is an integral part of the festivities. Besides, if the Lord did not wish it, surely the king would have prohibited this part of the ritual.”

Śrīla Vidyānidhi continued, “If the Lord desires it, then all is well. However, what the Lord does is certainly not to be imitated by His servitors. The priests and other *brāhmaṇas* should not even touch contaminated clothes. Śrī Jagannātha is the Supreme Godhead—everything is possible for Him, but not for others. One must wash his hands after touching starched clothes otherwise one is unclean. This is common sense and the King himself is ignorant, if he does not understand this point. Unfortunately, however, even the King ties a starched cloth around his head.” Śrīla Svarūpa replied, “My dear brother, all these things are not considered transgressions since they are a part of this Oḍana-ṣaṣṭhī festival. Besides, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Jagannātha Himself, does not pass judgement on the merit or demerit of this practice.”

Śrīla Vidyānidhi insisted, “My dear brother, hear me out. Lord Jagannātha is indeed transcendental and the Supreme Godhead, hence no rules apply to him, but what about His servitors? Have they become incarnations of the Supreme Brahman due to living in Nīlācala, and can therefore deviate from scriptural norms?” Talking and debating in this manner, these two intimate friends were enjoying and laughing together as they walked, sometimes holding hands, or sometimes putting their arm over the other’s shoulder in a carefree manner. Śrīla Vidyānidhi did not spare even the servitors of Lord Jagannātha for what he considered their negligence in serving the Lord.

Not everyone can understand the feelings in the heart of the servitors of the Lord. Only Kṛṣṇa knows the extent of one’s attachment to Him. The Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, first puts His devotee into illusion for a specific purpose and then He Himself dispels the illusion out of compassion. Thus, the Lord put Śrīla Vidyānidhi into illusion about His servitors. The two of them parted ways and returned to their individual residences to perform their devotional practices. They honoured *prasādam*, then came to the residence of Śrī Caitanya, and laid down to rest.

The Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya, knew everything about Śrīla Vidyānidhi’s views on the starched clothes. Therefore, He took the form of Jagannātha and together with Balarāma He appeared in the dream of Śrīla Vidyānidhi. In his dream, Śrīla Vidyānidhi saw that both Jagannātha and Balarāma were extremely angry as they began to slap him hard on his cheeks. Red welts appeared on his flushed cheeks and in pain and anguish he threw himself at the feet of the Lord and cried out, “O Kṛṣṇa, save me! Kindly forgive my offences. O Lord, for what offence am I being punished?” The Lord replied, “There is no end to your offences. Just like Me, my servitors do not belong to any caste and knowing all this you have taken up residence here, but if you at all wish to engage in splitting hairs about rituals and proper practices you had best return to your previous place and do so there! I have fixed all the customs to be followed in these festivals and now you have criticized my servitors and these performances by finding fault with My dressing in starched clothes.”

Śrīla Vidyānidhi became extremely fearful in his dream and weeping bitterly he placed his head on the lotus feet of the Lord and said, “Kindly forgive all the offences of this most sinful wretch. I fully accept My heinous faults, I promise you. My face, the face of your servitor, which had smiled derisively at these performances, has been beaten. I have been punished by Your own transcendental hand, surely that is my great fortune, my Lord.”

The Supreme Lord replied, “Since you are My devotee, I wanted to shower My blessings and compassion upon you and so I have punished you.” Their Lordships Jagannātha and Balarāma then graced Śrīla Vidyānidhi in his dream with their merciful glance and returned to their abode.

Śrīla Vidyānidhi woke up from the dream and began to laugh. Feeling the welts upon his cheeks, he said, “This is wonderful, I was offensive and got punished. The Lord slapped me with His transcendental hand. I was lucky to get away with so little.” Just observe the glory and greatness of Śrīla Vidyānidhi who is the perfect example of the limitless compassion of the Lord upon His devotee. The Supreme Lord does not take to task even His own son, Pradyumna, or even His wives Satyabhāmā, Rukmiṇī, Jānakī-Sītā, His other personal associates, or even the hosts of demigods and demigoddesses in this way. Yet, the Supreme Lord personally chastised and slapped Śrī Vidyānidhi in his dream for his offence. This act is the first of its kind, for it is not often that the Lord will directly appear before someone in a dream and mercifully punish him for an offence. When the Supreme Lord personally chastises someone in his dream then it is a real event and such a devotee is most fortunate. When such a devotee awakes, his offences are no more and he attains all the transcendental benefits. Such an individual is extremely fortunate because the Lord never chastises non-devotees even in their dreams.

All these scriptural conclusions are to be pondered upon. The *yavanas*, meat eaters, are constantly criticizing and are belligerent towards the Vaiṣṇavas. They are yearning for some spiritual realizations and happiness, but this is most elusive for them even in their dreams. What to speak of the *yavanas*, even *brāhmaṇas* and cultured persons suffer severely the consequences of their offences. Yet, the Supreme Lord never instructs such offenders and reprobates in their dreams. The truly fortunate are censured personally by the Lord; and this action of the Lord, they consider their greatest fortune. The next morning, when Śrīla Puṇḍarīka woke up from sleep, his cheeks were ruddy and puffed up from the hands of the Lord slapping him while he slept. The mercy he had received from the Supreme Lord was there for all to see.

Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara usually came every morning to accompany Śrīla Vidyānidhi to the temple to take *darśana* of Lord Jagannātha. When Śrīla Svarūpa came that morning, he said to Śrīla Vidyānidhi, “Every morning you accompany me to take *darśana*, but this morning you are late.” Śrīla Vidyānidhi replied, “My dear brother, come inside, sit down and I’ll tell you everything that has transpired.”

Upon coming closer, Śrīla Svarūpa saw that the face of his friend was all swollen up with red welts streaked across his cheeks. Surprised he enquired, “What has happened? Your cheeks are red and swollen! Have you hurt yourself?

Śrīla Vidyānidhi gave a short laugh and said, “Remember I was expressing serious doubts and reservations regarding Lord Jagannātha being dressed in starched clothes—well I have been taught my lesson. Last night, Jagannātha and Balarāma appeared in my dream and began to slap me saying, “You had the audacity to criticise My dress.” They left their finger marks on my cheeks so I feel very ashamed, I cannot meet anyone. Therefore, once this swelling goes away, I can once again go out into public. I cannot speak so openly to others about this, but in my heart, I feel greatly blessed. I have received in appropriate measure the consequences of my offence, otherwise, who knows, I might have descended to the darkest hell.”

Śrīla Svarūpa looked at his friend with great affection and experienced transcendental joy. A friend feels immense happiness at the good fortune of his friend. Therefore, the two friends broke out into peals of laughter unable to contain their jubilation. Śrīla Svarūpa said, “My dear brother, I must admit I’ve never seen the likes of such a punishment. The Lord personally comes to you in your dream, and then chastises you, this is extraordinary! I’ve never before heard of such an event, but now I see it with my own eyes.” They floated on waves of ecstasy swimming in the ocean of *kṛṣṇa-kathā*. Day and night, they relished *kṛṣṇa-kathā*. Such was the spiritual aura of Śrīla Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi that even the Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya, addressed him as ‘father’. He would never bathe in the Gaṅgā lest his feet touched her waters, yet he derived immense spiritual pleasure simply by having her *darśana* and sipping her sacred water. Śrī Caitanya received great joy by calling him ‘father’. One who hears about the character of Śrīla Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi will surely be rewarded with the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

I, Vṛndāvana dāsa, offer this song at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, who are my life and soul.

Thus ends *Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata*
